- **[cpy-stub] `Deref`'s stub reads a wrapper's ANNOTATED field as the payload's.** `lib/cpy/tpy/__init__.py`'s `Deref.__setattr__` keeps a name on the wrapper only when it is underscore-prefixed or in the class `__dict__`; a field declared by annotation alone (`target: Point` then `self.target = target` in `__init__`) is routed to `self.__deref__()`, which reads the same field back through `__getattr__` -- a `RecursionError` under CPython for a wrapper the compiler accepts (the wrapper's own members win there). - **[design] Rethink `Own[T]` at `str`/`bytes`: the explicit `Own[str]` spelling is not worth having, the generic `Own[T]` instantiated at `str` is.** Today a plain `str` parameter is `std::string_view` (a borrow) and `Own[str]` is `std::string` by value (the owned buffer), so `Own[str]` is the one spelling that lets a caller MOVE an owned string into a sink instead of copying it at the store. As a user-facing spelling it is obscure: nobody writes it, and a sink that stores a str copies once at the store either way. Where the owned form genuinely matters is a GENERIC slot -- `def push(self, v: Own[T])` on a container record instantiated at `str` must take the owned buffer, and today the instantiation's parameter form is decided on the open `T` (the same family as the view-at-a-generic-slot gap, which is closed at the CALL site by materializing an owned temp rather than in the signature -- see the param-form-as-template-argument entry below). Decide one rule for the value types that own a buffer: (a) `Own[str]` stays the owned-buffer form, documented as the exception, and generic instantiation at `str` derives it from the slot's `Own`-ness; or (b) `Own[str]` collapses to `str` (the view) like the scalars and the owned form is reached only through generic instantiation and the store-site materialization, with the move-at-last-use elision (`BUGS.md#own-str-slot-temp-copies-owned-source`) done at the store instead of the parameter. Either way the parameter form must be one channel read at instantiation. Raised by the user reviewing `str/own_str_arg_temp_in_while_condition` 2026-09-07.
- **[runtime] The static_assert pin blocks compile in every generated TU; they belong in a self-check TU.** `runtime/cpp/include/tpy/union_type.hpp` carries `union_pins`, `union_borrow_pins`, `union_buffer_pins` and `union_record_pins`, `variant_ref.hpp` carries `variant_ref_pins`, and `buffer_types.hpp` its sibling non-conversion and constructor asserts: 101 `static_assert` lines across the headers, five named pin structs of 121 lines, and nothing in the runtime or in generated code references any of them. A pin whose only job is to prove an invariant (layout parity, convertibility, a constexpr round trip, leaf well-formedness over packs no program uses) is a test, and the repo has the place for tests of that kind: a standalone TU under `runtime/cpp/tests/` registered in `tests/test_runtime_cpp.py`'s `_SELFCHECKS`, compiled and run once per toolchain. Move the pin structs and the pin-only asserts there; a header keeps only an assert that guards a definition at its point of use inside a template body. While there, add the missing `is_value_type<Union<Ts...>>` row -- true for a pack of value alternatives, false for a borrow pack and for a mixed one -- so a value union at a `param_val_or_ref_t<T>` slot would take the twin's `const Union&` form rather than a mutable reference if a generic at a union ever lowers (today every such instantiation rejects at `call.generic_arg_slot` / `decl.slot_type`). The row lives in `union_type.hpp`, not `type_traits.hpp`: `value_compare.hpp` (home of the pack predicate) includes `core.hpp` / `bigint.hpp` / `buffer_types.hpp`, all of which include `type_traits.hpp`, so the trait header cannot see the predicate without a cycle. Pin the three answers in the same TU.
- **[design] Declare a builtin type's view->storage construction and its coercions in the stub.** The generic parameter FORM question is SETTLED: `String`, `bytes` and `bytearray` each own a C++ type (`::tpy::String` / `::tpy::Bytes` / `::tpy::ByteArray`, derived from the std types), so `param_val_or_ref_t<T>` at a generic slot resolves to the monomorphic twin's own parameter form and no template argument is needed -- the second-template-argument design was rejected in favour of this. What is left is the second half of the same principle: the types are declared in the stubs (`@native("::tpy::String")`), but the compiler still owns their CONSTRUCTION and CONVERSION knowledge. A stub cannot yet declare: its view->storage construction (`view_to_owned_conv` and `view_owned_copy_init` in `tpyc/type_def_registry.py`, plus the five codegen lambdas that spell the same thing -- `str_to_string`, `strview_to_string`, `bytesview_to_bytearray`, `char_to_string` and `_any_storage_form` in `tpyc/coercions.py`); the implicit-conversion PAIRS between family members (`String` <-> `str`, `bytearray` -> `bytes`); `is_expensive_copy`; `param_needs_copy_for_reassign`; `boundary_marshal`; and `element_of`. The shape is a stub-declarable "construct my storage form from this view" hook -- a dunder -- that those sites read, so adding a fourth buffer type touches no compiler file.
- **[thir] `_container_method_call_supported` and `_record_method_call_supported` answer two different questions, so they were kept apart.** The record gate decides the receiver shape, the method resolution (single overload, MRO, native rename) and the return; the container gate decides only a resolved stub call's return -- widening the record receiver gate reroutes every container method call into the record member-call render. The mergeable half is the return admission, and it LANDED 2026-09-05: `_record_method_call_supported`'s result chain opens on `_stub_method_ret_ok` with the flag-free half enabled and its eight duplicated predicates are gone, so a value-result row added for the stub receivers reaches a user record's methods too. `storage_ret_ok` / `stmt_position` stay spelled in the record chain because those rows fire its own witnesses. Zero admissions gained over the whole case corpus (the shared core is a strict subset there), and the receiver/overload halves stay apart on purpose: routing a user record through the stub loop rejects loudly at `method.arg_shape` (the stub arg sink has no record pass-through row) rather than mis-rendering.
- **[thir] A user container's ELEMENT is not a native-arg source: `len(rows[0])` on `list[ArrayList[int32, 8]]` rejects at `call.native_arg.record_f1_slot`.** The NAME spelling (`len(al)`) already routes through the record arg row and renders `::tpy::__len__(al)`; only the SUBSCRIPT source is missing, and it is a record-row question rather than a container one -- `ArrayList.__getitem__` is an ordinary TPy method with no `native_function` / `native_name` / `cpp_template`, so the element family (membership = the receiver's `__getitem__` resolves to the builtin `::tpy::__getitem__`) correctly excludes it and forcing that spelling would be wrong code. Measured in the consolidation's stages 2 and 3.
- **[thir] `_container_slot_call_rvalue_arg` still enumerates its SLOT family, and silently excludes `bytearray`.** `tpyc/thir/lower/checks.py` gates the concrete same-family container slot with `is_list or is_dict or is_set or is_array`. The row it serves is `d.update(mk_d())` -- a container-returning call at a stub method's same-family slot, which renders `::tpy::dict_update(d, mk_d())`. No `bytearray` reproducer reaches the gate today (measured 2026-09-05): `bytearray.extend` takes `Iterable[uint8]` / `Iterable[int32]`, which the concrete-family test refuses for every family, and the only concrete-`bytearray` slots left are the operator stubs (`__add__` / `__eq__`), whose call operand rejects one step earlier at the result gate (`b + mk_ba()` -> `call.ret_type.record_other`). So the exclusion is unwitnessable rather than wrong -- but it is still a family list, not an axis test. Widening it to `_f1_container_ref` is the shape; a case per family is the proof, and a bytearray leg needs the operator-operand row closed first.
- **[thir] Three more name-keyed gates the fold did not classify.** `_inst_call_rvalue_arg` (`tpyc/thir/lower/predicates.py`) gates a call rvalue at an instantiation arg slot on `is_list or is_dict or is_set`; `_set_method_recv` (same file) is a set-only receiver branch; `_container_literal_inst_slot` (same file) is the `list([..])` / `set([..])` slot. Named in neither the deliberate-stop entries above nor BUGS.md -- each needs the same verdict the fold gave the others: an axis test, or an exclusion with a stated render reason.
- **[thir] `_comp_sized_iterable` enumerates the sized iterable families.** `tpyc/thir/lower/comprehensions.py` decides whether a comprehension can reserve up front with `is_array or is_list or is_dict or is_set or is_dict_view`. The question is really "does this source report `__len__` in O(1)", which is a per-TypeDef fact rather than a family list; `bytearray` is sized and absent, and a user container that reports its size cannot opt in. Only affects the reserve, never correctness, which is why it survived the fold.
- **[thir] `_lower_into_any` / `_lower_from_any` name list/dict/set as EXCLUSION tests.** `tpyc/thir/lower/expressions.py` refuses an `Any` round-trip for those three (the `make_any` wrap is a `{0}` placeholder that cannot express the paren copy a name/set/dict source needs, and the extraction has no container arm). Exclusions, not admissions -- so the risk is the reverse of the usual one: `bytearray` and `Array` are NOT named, so they fall through to a render nobody checked. Decide what those two do at an `Any` boundary, then state the fence on the axis.
- **[thir] The const-by-default param form is spelled twice: `_const_default_param_form` in the lowering and `to_cpp_param` / `to_cpp_const_param` in `typesys`.** The lowering predicate (`tpyc/thir/lower/predicates.py`) asks the registry whether a TypeDef carries the `param_cpp_formatter` + `param_mut_cpp_formatter` pair; `tpyc/typesys.py` renders the same distinction. One `TypeDef` / `TpyType` property should carry it, with both readers consulting it, so a second type adopting the pair cannot get one of the two answers. The second half is the load-bearing one: `_const_param_rvalue_ctor_arg` (`tpyc/thir/lower/expressions.py`) admits an rvalue at such a slot WITHOUT checking whether THIS constructor's slot took the MUTABLE spelling -- correct for `bytearray` today because no bytearray ctor slot is mutable, and a latent trap for the next type that adopts the pair. Add the mutable-slot check with the property. From /tpy-review of the container-family fold.
- **[thir] `TypeDef.subscript_borrows` is a redundant channel, and `_NATIVE_GETITEM` is a third spelling of the dunder table.** The element family now derives the element-borrow fact from the resolved stub's `fi.native_name`, which is the same fact `subscript_borrows` carries on the TypeDef -- wire the family to the TypeDef or delete the field, but do not keep two. Separately, `_NATIVE_GETITEM = "tpy::__getitem__"` (`tpyc/thir/lower/predicates.py`) hardcodes the string `tpyc/modules/defs.py`'s `DUNDER_CPP_TEMPLATES["__getitem__"]` already owns; derive it. From /tpy-review of the container-family fold.
- **[thir] `TypeDef` has `element_of` but no `key_of`, so the dict KEY is recovered from the stub instead of read off the registry.** `_native_getitem_key` (`tpyc/thir/lower/predicates.py`) matches the `__getitem__` stub's parameter against the record's type-param names and indexes `type_args` to find the concrete key. That is correct and better than a positional guess, but the fact belongs beside `element_of` as a first-class registry channel -- a new channel is a design decision, so it did not ride the container-family fold. From /tpy-review of that fold.
- **[codegen] Render a constructor's member-init list one initializer per line.** The ctor definition emits the whole member-init list on the signature line (`inline Grid::Grid(int32_t n) : cells(::tpy::from_range<...>(...)), tags(...), data(std::vector<int32_t>{}), mirror(std::vector<int32_t>{}) {}` in `tests/cases/records/ctor_container_sources`), which is unreadable once a record has more than two fields or any container initializer. Emit `: field(init)` on its own line per field, indented under the signature, the way the rest of the emitted C++ breaks statements. A pure formatting change in the ctor printer (`codegen_cpp/records.py`), but it churns the snapshot of every record with a member-init list, so it lands as its own comment-free change with a one-line diff class. Same treatment for a local declaration whose initializer is a container literal: `tests/cases/dict/nested_container_element_printers` emits a 225-column line for one nested dict literal, so break the initializer across lines once the declaration passes 100 columns.
- **[thir] Post-cutover follow-ups, decided 2026-09-02 with the deletion's eight open questions.** Decisions taken for the deletion itself: `faces.py` stays and its zero-witness report prints unconditionally in the summary; the reject-reason journal (`note()` / `note_detail()` and the composed reason helpers) survives and only the fallback tally dies, because the strict diagnostic reads it; class-constant and `Final`-global initializers get the same strict treatment as bodies (an unlowerable initializer is a compile error, no runtime demotion, no escape hatch); `shape.py` stays but its per-run harness recording goes; the docstring rewrite is its own commit right after the deletion; `--dump-thir`'s reject column keeps its plumbing and reads "why did this raise"; `scripts/thir_migration/review/` stays in place as the fix queue; the unit-test conversion in the deletion commit is minimum-green only. What those decisions defer, each its own change -- (a) the unit-test consolidation, (b) `faces.py` and (c) `shape.py` are DONE 2026-09-06 by measurement rather than by classification: a coverage difference over the whole corpus (6062 programs: every case, every reject probe, both example sets) against the 304 unit files found 687 lowering statements only a unit reached; each was mapped to its test function through per-test coverage contexts, converted to a case (342 added, `error_` for a reject path) and proven reached, and the files were deleted; `faces.py` STAYS because the whole-corpus zero-witness census in `tests/conftest.py` is the live dead-arm detector; `shape.py` and its tally script went with the tests they measured; the 36 statements reachable by no program and by no test were decided 2026-09-07: the test-only emit seam went (the no-op `CommentSink` / standalone `TempSink` / local `ModuleCounter` bases each collapsed into their single ctx-backed implementation, so `emit_thir_body` and the two leaf emitters now REQUIRE their sinks), and with it the whole-module `lower_module` entry, `THIRModule` and the `dump_thir` renderer that only read it -- the pins lower per body through `lower_function`, the entry codegen itself calls. The constant position, the one product caller of the standalone sinks, got its own sink that rejects at the allocation (`const.needs_statement_scope`) instead of detecting a pending temp after the render. The rest STAYS: every remaining line is a reject, a guard or a lowering arm that an earlier gate makes unreachable rather than scaffolding, and dropping one turns a hypothetical gate bug into a silent miscompile -- the class this compiler keeps producing. Still open: (d) **Convert the 54 `None`-returning rejects** in the resumable and simple-generator lowerings to raises, so one raise formulation covers every reject and the journal can shrink to the raise's own message. (e) **Opt-in THIR snapshots**: a `snapshot_thir` key in `options.json`, mirroring `snapshot_lib_modules`, writing `expected/thir/<module>.txt` for a curated set of cases (moves, narrowing, resumable frames -- the shapes the deleted audits guarded). Not before the typing pass: today 101 of 537 node fields are pre-rendered C++ text, so a dump would duplicate the C++ snapshot and then churn on every representation step while the C++ stays byte-identical.
- **[thir][test] First-reject-wins: an `error_` case's annotation pins whatever body rejects FIRST.** The attempt driver raises at the first rejecting body of a module, so a case whose subject body is not the first to reject annotates an earlier, unrelated reject -- and keeps passing after its intended boundary is widened, the one regression it exists to catch. The harness validates the annotation on the REPORTED line, which makes the pin honest but not necessarily the intended one. Fix per case: narrow the program so its own shape rejects first (one reject per `error_` case; two rejects cannot share a module). The unit-suite half of this entry (the `*_stays_ast` / `*_falls_back` names) closed with the suite's deletion 2026-09-06. (ii) **`dump.py`'s `_not_routed` fallback arm is probably dead.** `--dump-thir` goes through `collect_thir` -> `generate_code_and_thir`, which now raises `ThirRejectError` on an unlowerable body, so the `<fell back to AST: reason>` line is unreachable for a real reject -- a bodyless binding and an overload stub both take the other arm. Confirm, then delete the arm with its `reasons` plumbing; if something does still reach it, its wording names an emitter that no longer exists. Surfaced by the post-deletion BUGS/docs pass.
- **[thir][test] `# tpyc: ok` is now refused in an `error_` case, and update mode validates annotations.** DONE 2026-09-07. `tests/test_case.py` rejects an `ok` annotation in an error case naming the line (compilation stops at the first error, so the leg is satisfied by a line the phase never reached), and `validate_annotations` runs in update mode too -- after the snapshot is written, in `test_case.py` and `test_interop_exec.py` alike -- so a regeneration can no longer rewrite `diag.txt` around a wrong annotation and leave the next plain run to fail on it. All 58 legs across the 38 pre-existing error cases went: 32 dropped as pure scaffolding (a `def` line, a stub `...` body, a `nums = [1, 2, 3]` fixture), 20 dropped with a header pointer to the normal case that already pins the happy path, and 6 moved into a section of one of five existing normal cases (`calls/overload_literal_int`, `generators/narrowed_value_opt_field_yield` x2, `generators/narrowed_value_opt_frame_faces`, `movability/pool_custom_move`, `union/union_field_const_read`). No new case was needed and no leg turned out false. The comp-only annotations (`type`, `non_null`, `bounds_*`, `div_*`, `cast_*`, `is_send`/`is_sync`, `frame_*`) keep their update-mode exemption, since they feed no snapshot; the same argument applies to them, more weakly. The residue is the GENERAL form of the gate: an annotation on ANY line the phase did not reach is still accepted (`type` / `bounds_safe` / `non_null` and friends in a body that rejected), which needs the harness to know which lines were analysed.
- **[thir] `_ConstPositionSink` (`tpyc/thir/constants.py`) implements the sink protocol by duck typing, and nothing pins the protocol.** It is the temp sink of a namespace-scope initializer: every allocation raises `const.needs_statement_scope`, the counters just count, `comments` is None. A method added to the ctx-backed `TempSink` (or a statement arm reaching the comment sink from expression emission) surfaces there as an `AttributeError` ICE where a reject is wanted. Cheap closure: a `Protocol` the two sinks both satisfy, checked by a unit in the kept machinery files, or a `__getattr__` that rejects.
- **[thir] A resumable's TERMINATOR rejects report the `def` line, not the offending one** (fixing it moves `tests/cases/async/error_narrow_post_if_across_suspend`, which commits the coarse `def`-line diagnostic)**.** `_lower_leaf` in `tpyc/thir/lower/resumable.py` stamps the rejecting statement's location on a `ThirUnsupported` that has none, which covers the frame-field statement arms. Three terminator paths raise outside it -- the branch condition, the await operand, and the finally-helper walk -- so a reject there reaches `fold_attempt` with no location and falls back to the enclosing callable's `def` line. Correct but coarse today; once `--thir-strict` is the only behaviour it is the line a user is shown, so each of the three wants the same set-if-empty stamp at its own leaf.
- **[thir] Small cleanups left over from the deletion.** Three: fold `Compiler._make_codegen` into `_run_codegen`, since the split existed to keep the two emit entry points routing identically and there is only one route left; extract the four set-if-empty `ex.loc` stamps in `tpyc/thir/lower/` into one helper; and dispatch `_strict_error`'s `where` phrasing on `component` before falling back to the node's name, so a `top_level` fold over a named node cannot be phrased as a function.
- **[thir] The call-arg position kind is still five booleans beside a one-member enum.** `_lower_call_arg` names its GENERIC caller through `CallArgKind`, the axis beside `_ExprUse.pos` for which argument loop is filling a slot -- the callee's shape, not the sink's. The other five kinds are still booleans on the same signature: `method_arg` and `method_arg_stub` (four spellings for three positions, the illegal fourth combination held only by convention), `protocol_slots`, `marker_arg` and `inline_template`. Fold each into a `CallArgKind` member so a new argument loop is a new member rather than a sixth flag; the rights beside them (`temp_args`, `nested_temps`, `readonly_target`, `frame_capturing`, `union_divergent_ok`) are not kinds and stay. The slot half of this entry landed: `slot_threaded` and the `target_type` keyword are one `_ExprUse.slot_target`.
- **[thir] The validator's `THIRRaise` arm walks only `node.args`, so a non-call `raise <expr>` gets no form validation.** `_walk` in `tpyc/thir/validate.py` handles `THIRRaise` by walking the ctor argument list and RETURNING, which is right for `raise X(a, b)` (the args are the ctor's directly). The EXPRESSION form (`raise e` / `raise make_error()`) carries its subject on `raise_expr` instead, and the early return means that subtree is never walked -- no form check, no arg-temp check, on whatever it contains. Pre-existing; found while extracting the shared arg-list walk. Fix shape: walk the remaining children after the arg list instead of returning.
- **[thir] `_borrow_legal_return` and `_value_record_borrow` are two predicates joined at one `if`.** `tpyc/thir/validate.py`'s `THIRReturn` rule reads `not _borrow_legal_return(return_type) and not _value_record_borrow(stmt.value)` -- one question (may this BORROW value initialize this return slot?) split across a type-keyed half and a value-keyed half, so a reader has to reassemble it and a new row can land in the wrong half. Fold into one `_borrow_legal_return(return_type, value)`. Belongs in the deletion unit's cleanup sweep.
- **[cli] Five places stamp a `CodeGenError`'s filename, and only the compiler knows which file it is.** `tpyc/cli.py` wraps four codegen calls in the same `if e.filename is None and not compiled.is_entry_point: e.filename = os.path.relpath(compiled.path)`, and `Compiler._run_codegen` now does the same for a THIR reject -- so the rule lives once per call site instead of once. Consolidating it into the compiler (stamp every `CodeGenError` at the one place that holds the `CompiledModule`) would let the CLI drop all four wrappers. Held back because it changes the filename on EVERY codegen diagnostic, not just the ones that are unstamped today, and whether the entry point should stay caller-named is a design call rather than a refactor.
- **[test] Interop cases snapshot REGULAR emission, which is the corpus's job.** Each case under `tests/interop/` commits the module `.hpp`/`.cpp` alongside the CPython glue `_ext.cpp`, and the module half carries nothing interop-specific: `@export` affects the glue only, so an exported function's body renders exactly as the same source would in an ordinary case (checked on `floats`: no `PyObject`, no `Py_`, no export marking anywhere in the module `.cpp`). The interop-specific artifacts are the glue, `diag.txt`, the ext-exec `.so` build and driver run, and cpy-parity -- those are the case type's reason to exist. Consequences already paid: the THIR overlay there byte-diffs ordinary module emission and so duplicates corpus coverage, which is why it turned out to need no cutover successor after being scoped as a blocker. Worth narrowing the snapshot set to the interop-specific artifacts, which would drop roughly 68 committed files. **Do not act on the one-case check above** -- confirm across all 34 that no module emission differs from its plain-case equivalent before removing anything, since a shape where `@export` DID reach the module would be exactly the coverage worth keeping. Not cutover work; a cleanup that the cutover happened to expose.

- **[thir] The post-cutover fix queue: shapes that are now compile errors.** The primary queue is `scripts/thir_migration/review/` -- the BREAKS rows of `bins_*.json` (402 sites, each with a reproducer under `probes/<slice>/`) and the `BREAKS_AT_CUTOVER` entries of `program_verdicts.json` (478 programs). This entry holds what is NOT in those files: shapes found by two pre-deletion sweeps whose probe programs were not kept. Each is valid code that compiled and ran correctly before the deletion because a second emitter caught it; each is a `ThirRejectError` today. Close one by adding the lowering arm and landing an ordinary case, not a probe. **Nine witnesses from the guard-reading sweep** (2026-08-31/09-01): a generator expression over a DICT (`sum(k for k in d)`, `genexpr.iterable_shape`); `while 1:` (`truthy.literal`); an Optional match whose inner arm carries a guard (`case Node() if n.v > 0:`); a nested `def` shadowing a module-level function name (`nesteddef.name_collision`); a `print(..., file=<subscript>)` whose sink list folds at `expr.container_literal`; binding a `Final[tuple[...]]` class constant WHOLE (`v = Version.SEMVER`, `field.class_const_type`); a covariant upcast written to an Optional record FIELD (`h.node = Derived(4)` where `node: Base | None`); the truthiness of an Optional record field (`if h.node:`, `cond.field_access`); and `",".join([str(x) for x in xs])` (`method.view.arg_shape`). The last three are everyday idioms, which is the point.
  One of them is worth dwelling on: `tests/cases/class_const/final_tuple_constant` already covers that constant, but only through the UNPACK position, which routes -- the whole-tuple bind beside it does not, and no case reaches it. **A covered feature is not a covered position**, and that is the shape this sweep keeps finding.
  **The other seven fold in front of an AST that emits ill-formed C++, and that reframes the class.** `if "yes":`, a `for a, b in ...:` unpack inside a generator, a genexpr over any dict view, a literal passed to a pointer-representation union parameter, extracting a container out of `Any`, a GUARD on a union match arm (the guard does not narrow though the arm body does), and an Optional match inside a generator (the arm body does not narrow though the plain-function form does) all fail the C++ build today; each is filed separately in BUGS.md (five at HIGH -- all common spellings). Probing also turned up a rejects-valid-code defect that is NOT a fold: the return-path analysis does not credit a break-free loop's `else` clause, so a function whose only `return` sits there is refused. For these the fence was doing the right thing; the deletion traded a bad-C++ error for a reject diagnostic, which is a UX change but not a correctness one. **The reusable heuristic: an unwitnessed fence is a good place to LOOK FOR AST BUGS.** THIR declined to mirror those renders, and in three of eight cases the reason is that the render is broken -- so triaging the remaining sites pays twice, once in cutover risk and once in defects that no test corpus reaches.
  **The METHOD is the durable half.** Probes aimed from reject TAGS found nothing: 0 folds from 13. Probes aimed after READING the guard condition found all sixteen: 16 folds from 58 that reached codegen. That rate is biased UPWARD -- the most ordinary-looking guards were probed first -- so read it as a bound on the per-guard rate, not an estimate of one. **Three KEYS are in play here and they must not be swapped**: 16 FOLDS (a probe whose body did not route), 9 WITNESSES (a folding shape that is valid code working today), and 10 new BUGS ENTRIES (filed defects, which include ones found while checking a shape rather than by a fold, and which sometimes cover more than one shape). Saying "the sweep filed nine bugs" pairs the witness key with the bug label and is wrong in both directions. Reject tags name where a reason was FORMATTED, not what blocks the shape, so a tag-driven triage of the remaining 358 sites will read as clean and be wrong. Two guard docstrings were also contradicted by probe: `_lower_with` states that a `with` nested in a branch or loop still rejects, and both spellings route -- treat every prose claim about what a fence still catches as unverified until a probe says otherwise.
  **Negative results are triage output too -- record them.** Several depth-0/1 fences turned out to be SEMA-GATED, so no valid program reaches them and they need no lowering work: `getattr`/`setattr` with a literal name on a declared field (sema redirects to `obj.x`), a `@dynamic`-protocol local without an initializer, a class pattern on a scalar Optional inner, a nested `def` containing `yield`, and `Final[list[str]]` as a class constant. A fence behind a sema diagnostic is unreachable by construction, not untested.
  **Thirty-nine more from the 2026-09-01 adversarial sweep** (162 hand-written probes; 23 of the 39 compiled and ran correctly, the other 16 were already broken in ways the sweep did not look at and are filed separately). They spread over 32 distinct reject reasons -- 1.2 probes per reason, the same flat tail the stdlib grind ended on, the largest `stmt.match` at 6. Not a set-cover problem: pick by what the shape COSTS a user, not by tag frequency.
  **Three more shapes, found by the asymmetry matrix and NOT in the 39** -- 7 probes, all rejected today: `case A() | B() as n:` on an `A | B` union subject (an or-pattern of class patterns carrying an `as` binding, with and without a guard); `case n if True:` on an `A | None` subject (a bare capture arm with a guard on an Optional); and a GUARDED capture or wildcard arm (`case s if ...:` / `case _ if ...:`) inside a match with enough string-literal arms to select the string-switch tier. **Five of the seven compile and run correctly today; the other two do not, and saying they did was wrong** -- the two that place the guarded arm FIRST are a silent miscompile the AST render drops on the floor, now filed HIGH. So this set splits like the 39 do: mostly working programs that lost their emitter, plus a couple that were already broken and only looked like routing gaps. Check before claiming a rejected shape works.
  **The 39 shapes, written out because the TAGS ARE LOSSY** -- they name the first reject, not the blocker, so a tag alone does not let anyone reconstruct what to re-probe. The probe programs themselves are gone (they were a second, weaker copy of what a test case does); each shape below is cheap to re-author, and whoever closes a gap should land it as an ordinary case rather than a probe.
  *match (the only cluster):* a call as the subject with no intermediate binding; a dict-subscript subject with 5+ literal str arms (string-switch tier, non-name subject); a match in a `for` whose arm mutates a captured reference field then breaks; a match inside `try` whose arm raises; a bool subject that is a call, exhaustive with no wildcard; a subscript subject of `int32 | None` inside a `while` with a guard on the int arm; a walrus subject (`match (n := compute(x)):`) with the name used after; a field-access subject whose pattern captures and mutates a reference sub-field; a `@dynamic` subject with two-level nested keyword sub-patterns and an `as` on the inner pattern; a `@dynamic` parameter subject with an or-pattern spanning two classes; a guard calling `isinstance` on a union-arm capture; a match in a generator on a `Ping | Pong | None` subject; `yield` in a match arm over a union-typed frame local read again after resume.
  *comprehensions and iteration:* a list comp over `dict.items()` whose element is a call, plus a comp-of-comp; a dict comp over `zip(enumerate(...), ...)`; a genexpr over `reversed(list)` consumed by `sum()`; `zip` over three uneven iterables as a comp source; a comp element that is a conditional expression producing a tuple, sourced from `enumerate()`; a walrus in a comp filter whose name is reused in the element expression and leaks to the enclosing scope; nested `for` loops reusing one loop-variable name at the same and at different types.
  *unions and narrowing:* a 3-member union list element narrowed by `is None` plus `isinstance` inside a loop; a tuple element of reference-type union narrowed after unpacking; a union as a generic type ARGUMENT (`Box[Dog | Cat]`) narrowed after extraction; a walrus binding `Dog | Cat | None` then narrowed in two steps; a value union narrowed by `==` against a str literal rather than `is None`/`isinstance`; a mixed value+reference union as a RETURN type narrowed by the caller; `list[Optional[tuple[int32, str]]]`.
  *calls:* `@overload` on a constructor; overload stubs shorter than the implementation with trailing params from defaults; an enum-member default crossed with out-of-order kwargs and an overload group; a call result subscripted then field-accessed then chained again; a chained subscript straight off a call return (`f()[i][j]`) and a subscript on a slice-of-a-slice; nested generics (a list of lists through a generic function, a generic class instantiated with another generic); two OS-divergent error classes in one `except` tuple with the `open()` result chained into `close()`.
  *records and module scope:* `super().__init__` with a value-type union parameter; mutually recursive records with an owned value moved into a list via `append`; a list comprehension at MODULE scope; a union-typed global narrowed at module scope; bytearray element mutation by index alongside bytes-vs-str indexing. Everyday spellings in the list include a list comprehension at module scope, a comprehension over `dict.items()`, `zip`/`enumerate`/`reversed` sources, a walrus in a comprehension condition, nested loops reusing a name, a match inside `try`/`except`, a match on a field access or a subscript, and `super().__init__` with a union parameter.
  **Four probes DIVERGE across the three widths.** At int32: an overloaded generator's const-mismatched narrowing, a generic class returning a narrowed `Optional[T]` field, and an int literal at an inherited overload. At BigInt only: a list-literal for-loop source, where the AST emits a bare `{10, 0, 1}` and THIR constructs each element -- **the first option-gated AST/THIR divergence anyone has caught**, and the whole justification for sweeping every width. Each is filed in BUGS.md. In the two that emitted C++ the AST could not compile, the deletion fixed them by removing the wrong author; the other two ran identically on both paths and are filed for the class, not the instance. None has a corpus witness.

- **[thir][sema] An `@auto_readonly` / `auto_own` CLONE of an `@overload` impl gets no `overload_groups` entry, so it reads as a non-overloaded method.** `_collect_method_overload_groups` (`tpyc/sema/analyzer.py`, the `pending_stubs.pop(method.name)` line) hands a name's stub list to the FIRST non-stub method it sees; method expansion has already split an `@auto_readonly` method into a mutable + const pair, both non-stub, so the second clone is left unregistered. Ten AST codegen sites read `overload_groups` (`codegen_cpp/records.py`, `generator.py`, `functions.py`) and all of them therefore treat the clone as un-overloaded. The AST's emission happens to be correct today -- it emits every specialization from the REGISTERED impl and skips the twin by name (`records.py`'s `overload_dispatched` set) -- so this is a latent modelling gap, not a live bug. **THIR does not repair the registration: it SKIPS the twin** (`unemitted_overload_clones`, excluded from `iter_module_callables`), because the twin has no body on either path. An earlier attempt to PAIR the twin with its polarity-matching stub was built and discarded -- the lookup key is minted by the AST emitter, which has no group for the twin either, so a paired entry would have had no consumer. **Do NOT fix this by registering the clone without re-deriving those ten call sites**: they drive per-stub emission, so a naive registration would emit the clone once per stub where one body is correct. Fix shape: register the clone against its SINGLE matching stub (not the whole group) and audit each AST consumer for whether it wants the group or the pairing; the THIR skip then becomes redundant and should be deleted with it. - **[thir] The `Optional[Array[T, N]]` container-literal seams are inconsistent by accident.** The field-write and ctor-MIL seams admit an `Array` inner (they share `_optional_container_storage_inner` in `tpyc/thir/lower/checks.py`), but the sibling DECL seam still falls back because the pre-existing, unmodified `_opt_pointee_wide` gate (`tpyc/thir/lower/predicates.py:3714`) never included `is_array`. Probed: `arr: Array[int32, 3] | None = [1, 2, 3]` reports `stmt.var_decl:decl.opt_slot_pointee`. Output is byte-identical either way, so this is a coverage gap rather than a defect -- but the two seams now differ for no stated reason. The fix looks like one line (`_opt_pointee_wide` gains `is_array`); it is filed rather than taken because widening an admission gate needs the full wave discipline -- pins, disable-and-dualgen, a blast sweep -- not a one-line edit at the end of an unrelated branch. Surfaced by the markers-zero-0823 codegen-correctness review.

Full memo in the round C analysis (2026-08-15).

The witness (none_safety/narrowed_field_print) only reads the field as a WHOLE optional (print_optional_val), but admitting the condition without the path fact makes any deref read a silent divergence -- the fact model is the design item, not a row. Sibling: tuple/tuple_literal_unpack_alias chains into the REF_ALIAS park (`Counter& __unpack_1_0 = __getitem__(...)` element alias captures).
- **[thir] PARKED (design): wrapper-union match SUBJECT captures beyond the NAME slice.** The M4c wrapper-match route is NAME-only by design (match.py `_match_route`: "a field/subscript source would compose `.value` over a member read -- out of slice"). Two sole-blocker witnesses need subject-CAPTURE forms: a borrow-returning wrapper call subject (`match h.get():` -- union/generic_recursive_field_alias; the arg-position twin landed 2026-08-06 as arg.ru_wrapper_borrow_call) and a HOISTED pointer-local wrapper subject (`match v:` off a branch-hoisted `Tree<int32>*` -- union/match_hoisted_wrapper_local; needs the deref-subject spelling). Each is a new subject-bind render, not a gate row -- design the capture form once for both.
- **[thir] Alias-instance slice coverage: one targeted pass on `Box[RecursiveAlias]` semantics beyond the ctor-move shape.** The 2026-08-06 `RecursiveAliasInstanceType` type-arg admission widens `_f1_record` verdicts across ~266 consumers while only two unit pins + one corpus case exercise the new shape, all move-flavored. Worth one pass: a MIL COPY (not move) through a `Box[RecursiveAlias]` field, and a mutate-after-alias check per the reference-type test-adequacy rule. Safety-model review round 12 traced the slice contract (spelling identity, not ownership) and found no live defect -- this is coverage, not a bug.
- **[thir] The move-verdict join needs a denominator FLOOR, not just a denominator.** The gate prints `0 divergences over N joined nodes`; N guards against the detector being unwired entirely, but NOT against coverage collapse. At 729 joined nodes over 2933 routed cases (~0.25 per case) a refactor that drops the join to 40 still prints a nonzero N and still says `0 divergences` -- the exact silent-decay mode the module's own docstring describes. Ratchet it like the case dial: record the expected floor, fail when N drops below it. Also state in the summary WHAT N counts -- it is the subset of nodes both arm structures happen to ask about, not every candidate move site, and a reader will assume the latter.
- **[thir] The move-verdict join DIES AT CUTOVER and has no successor -- decide before then.** It joins on `id()` of AST nodes that BOTH paths walk, which is only true while THIR re-emits a module the AST pass already emitted. When the AST body emitters are deleted (the migration's stated endpoint) the gate loses its second side and becomes dead code -- taking with it the only detector for a divergence class the byte-diff structurally cannot see. The successor cannot be a cross-path join; it has to be a THIR-INTERNAL invariant (assert the move verdict against the sink's own requirement rather than against the other path). Belongs on the cutover checklist now, while the reasoning is loaded. Surfaced by the readiness second opinion as the biggest unasked question on the branch.
- **[thir] The comprehension element sinks have no move witness, and cannot get one yet.** Six of the twelve container-rule call sites of `_lower_container_elem` live in `thir/lower/comprehensions.py`. Pinning one needs a comprehension whose element is an outer frame-promoted value-typed local at last use -- i.e. a comprehension inside a RESUMABLE body -- and that shape falls back today (`resumable:expr.list_comprehension`), so the pin would be vacuous: a fallback emits the AST verbatim and byte-identity holds regardless. Probed, not assumed. Write it when the resumable comprehension arm lands; until then the AST-oracle reading (codegen-correctness verified all 17 sites) is the cover on its own -- the list and dict unit pins went with the THIR unit suite. Related: `set/set_comp_owned_move` is the parked comprehension-flush fork.

What is still unpinned is the rest of the payload surface at that row: str, tuple, record and generic (`TypeParamRef`) slots. Fixed-width ints never reach the predicate at all (the `Own[scalar]` no-op peel short-circuits first), so the families worth adding are the expensive-copy value types and the generic slots. Low priority -- the row's rule is now stated and guarded; this is breadth, not a hole.
- **[thir] Pins for the promote arms the movable-set fix left unwitnessed.** Of ~13 THIR `lc.promote_movable` call sites, four have a dedicated pin (tier-1 value filter, ptr-variant exclusion, own-element tuple + unpack targets, frame local). No dedicated unit for: the pointer-local family (`OPT_PTR_SLOT` x2, `REBIND_SLOT`, `POINTER`, `OPTIONAL_TO_PTR`), comprehension locals, owned-record / copy-record decls, the if/match pointer hoist, move-through locals, or `storage_call_tuple` / `storage_record_tuple`. A field on the layout would serve both paths. Touches AST and THIR together, so it is its own change-set -- not shareable with a THIR change. Do it together with the sibling joint in the same loop, `_frame_ptr_locals`, which is ASSUMED to equal the AST's frame-field `pointer_locals` membership and has never been shown to. The divergence that assumption once produced is CLOSED -- the AST now promotes an await bind at its own seam, so THIR's layout-driven promotion agrees there (probed both ways; the corpus move-verdict join reports zero). What is left is an unverified equivalence between two independently-built sets, with no witness either way: folding both onto the layout is what would make it true by construction rather than by coincidence.
- **[thir] Pin-discipline enforcement: the three-unit rule is 0-for-5 as documentation.** `CLAUDE.md` has carried "every new arm gets a routing pin, a byte-identity pin and a boundary pin" since 2026-07-28, and the ledger teaches the same lesson four separate times -- yet FIVE pins on the thir-longtail-grind branch alone could not fail (three caught by review, two more found only by a dedicated audit of the branch's own 81 added tests, one of them pinning that branch's own `movable_locals` bug fix). The gap is not knowledge: 107 of 112 THIR test files already use a routing idiom. Nothing FORCES it. PARTIALLY LANDED 2026-08-01: `_assert_routes_byte_identical` (byte-identity + every body routed) exists in `thir/testutil.py`, and CLAUDE.md now requires a routing-claiming pin to use it or to assert on THIR nodes. That is opt-IN. **The opt-OUT default was tried and measured, and the blunt version does not work**: flipping `_assert_byte_identical` + `_lower_ctx_witnessed` to assert zero fallback by default fails 205 of ~4100 THIR units, and only a minority are dead pins -- the check is module-wide, so it also trips every fixture that legitimately carries a deliberately-unroutable sibling function next to the routed one. Making the default work needs PER-BODY attribution, which already exists (`compiler._thir_reject_by_node`, keyed by AST callable): the helper would have to take the function name under test and assert THAT body routed. Worth doing -- the 205-failure list (many named `..._routes` / `..._moves`) is where the remaining dead pins are, and the per-body version turns triaging it into a mechanical pass. NB face COUNTS are not a clean substitute, though the reason has changed: the increment-site defect (an arm that witnessed before it could raise read as witnessed even when the body fell back) was FIXED 2026-07-29 -- witnesses are journalled per lowering attempt and rolled back on fallback. What still makes a count weak evidence is that for ~224 faces the witness fires at a GATE, so it proves a row was ADMITTED, not that the named render ran. The (a) proposal -- author-side revert injection -- is untouched and still open.
- **[thir] The `Own[Ptr[T]]` `_coerce_disposition` exception is protected by incidental filters, not by its stated property.** The exception returns "template" where the blanket `Own[...]` reject used to fire, reasoned from "Own over a value type is a no-op spelling, so no auto-move cascade owns the render". The claim still holds for `_lower_with`'s sibling gate, which is unchanged and has no witness to widen on; (4) the with-target PTR_DECL/ASSIGN_PTR arms in-branch (pointer decl placement unverified against the oracle). Each lift needs its blocking case + `expected/*.cpp` oracle read before touching (tags are lossy). - **[thir][tooling] `--dump-thir` arm-correctness coverage; the whole-corpus sweep was built and REJECTED.** The completeness unit proves every THIR node class HAS a render arm, not that the arm is right -- 3 of the 30 arms added with it shipped wrong (a mis-spelled field that silently dropped `except E as x:` bindings, a missing `orelse`, a native symbol spelled as an operator), a ~10% defect rate on the population the existence check certifies. A whole-corpus execution sweep WAS implemented (branch `thir-dump-smoke`, an opt-in `--thir-dump-smoke` rendering every routed body) and deliberately NOT merged. Do not rebuild it: it guards the LOUD failure mode -- a bad field access raises, so `--dump-thir` crashes and whoever ran it fixes it in minutes -- while the dangerous mode is a wrong-but-PLAUSIBLE render, which no execution sweep can detect by construction. Evidence: the sweep ran clean over 8768 bodies and found nothing; all three defects were caught by review and by writing the targeted table. The residual worth investing in is that table (`tpyc/thir/test_dump.py`, currently 8 of the 83 concrete THIRExpr/THIRStmt classes) -- extend it when an arm's render is load-bearing for a drill. Surfaced by the /tpy-ready retrospective of the dump-completeness branch; sweep built and dropped 2026-07-21.
- **[thir][tooling] `collect_thir` drops `cycle_peers`, so `--dump-thir` can render the wrong emission config.** `Compiler.collect_thir` goes through `_generate_to_strings`, which omits the `cycle_peers=` argument the file-writing `generate_code` passes -- so for a module in an import SCC, `--dump-thir` renders a DIFFERENT emission configuration than the one whose C++ was byte-diffed, and a CodeGenError arising only in the no-cycle-peers configuration would surface from a dump for a reason unrelated to the dump. Pre-existing since the dump became codegen-backed. Fix shape: thread `cycle_peers` through `_generate_to_strings` so both entry points share one emission configuration. Surfaced by the /tpy-ready retrospective of the dump-smoke branch.
- **[thir][tooling] The validator's generic argtemp_ok tail treats lazy expression positions as eager.** `validate._walk`'s tail propagates the flush right through EVERY `THIRExpr` child, but comprehension elements, `THIRLambda.body`, and `THIRChainedCompareStmtExpr`'s later operands are lazy/multi-eval positions where a hoisted temp would be a miscompile -- only ternary ARMS and `&&`/`||` operands are explicitly reset today. Lowering admission currently keeps temps out of those positions, so this is a guard gap, not a live defect; harden by resetting the right at those nodes (mirror the THIRIfExpr arm split). Pre-existing (predates the ternary-cond change that surfaced it). Surfaced by the /tpy-ready retrospective second opinion of `thir-wave-next3`.
- **[infra] `rpytest` can report results for a tree that is not the local one.** A remote run reported a case count (3483) that did not match the local branch tree (3480); the local tree only reached that count after a later master merge. A remote run whose numbers silently describe different source than the one being shipped will mislead any verification that trusts it -- which is how a grind wave certifies the wrong thing. Worth pinning down what state rpytest ships (working tree vs a shared/hashed remote checkout) and making a mismatch loud. **This entry previously advised verifying branch-critical results locally; that is superseded.** CLAUDE.md names exactly two local-run reasons (rpytest absent, or a run that must write on this host) and branch-criticality is not one -- follow CLAUDE.md. The case counts quoted above predate the 3746-case corpus and are illustrative only; the open question is what state rpytest ships, not whether to trust it. Surfaced 2026-07-21.

- **[ci][verify] First macOS nightly must confirm the BigInt-literal ambiguity fix compiles.** The macOS `const BigInt` overload-ambiguity fix now lives in ONE chokepoint: `int_literals.render_int_literal_value` pins a target-less `>int32` literal to an exact BigInt-ctor width (`static_cast<int64_t>` for `<=int64`, `static_cast<uint64_t>` up to uint64, `from_str` beyond), so a bare `long`/`ull` token never reaches an ambiguous `long -> BigInt` / `unsigned long long -> BigInt` conversion (int64_t == long only on Linux; uint64_t == unsigned long long only on macOS). Both codegen paths share the function (THIR pre-renders literals through it). Verified by a C++ simulation of the macOS/Linux ctor layouts plus Linux-green. A real arm64 Mac build has since happened (Apple clang 21, 2026-07-29) but only over the `tests/interop` corpus, which touches none of the cases named below -- so this stays open on THOSE cases. So a red first mac-nightly on any BigInt-vs-literal site (`datetime.py`, `sys_maxsize`, the `int/bigint_compare_large_literal` / `int/bigint_list_large_literal` / `float/as_integer_ratio` / `builtins/sum_basic` / `stdlib/datetime_datetime` cases) is this fix's regression, not new breakage; conversely a green mac-nightly closes the verify loop. Rides the phase-2 mac row. Surfaced by /tpy-ready + /tpy-review of `fix-bigint-list-literal`.

- **[perf][cleanup] `render_int_literal_value`'s BigInt-TARGET arm has no `[2^63, 2^64-1]` case -- a threaded huge literal in that range renders `BigInt::from_str("...")` (runtime string parse) where the target-less arm now uses `static_cast<uint64_t>(...)` (compile-time, exact `BigInt(uint64_t)` ctor).** Add the symmetric `uint64` fast-path to the BigInt-target arm (`tpyc/codegen_cpp/int_literals.py`) so a value like `n: int = 18446744073709551615` avoids the parse. Rare range, correct either way -- pure perf/symmetry, not a bug. Surfaced by /tpy-review (codegen-correctness) of the list-literal consolidation.

- **[test-gap] `_reindex_builtins_post_finalize` order-independence lacks a direct unit test.** The `threading/mutex_wrap_cross_module` regression guard reproduces the builtin-index ordering bug only because the module name `achan` happens to sort `tpy.sync` before `tpy._core._containers` in the Tarjan topo order (`tpyc/compiler.py:_compute_compile_order` ties-break via `sorted`); an unrelated future stdlib rename/reorder could silently stop reproducing it with no signal from the suite. Add a focused `tpyc/` unit test that constructs the two-module finalize order directly (no dependence on real stdlib module names) and asserts a builtin (`Ptr`/`uint32`) resolves in the consumer analyzer's registry regardless of finalize order. Surfaced by /tpy-review (test-coverage) of `fix-channel-prereqs`.
- **[investigate] Known asymmetry in `_reindex_builtins_post_finalize`: it re-runs only ONE of the finalize loop's three registration steps.** `_finalize_declarations`'s implicit-module loop (`tpyc/compiler.py`) does builtin-type indexing + `register_protocol` + a non-builtin record auto-inject, all with the same "read a peer's not-yet-fully-populated exports at call time" shape; the post-finalize re-index re-applies only the builtin-type step. So a stdlib protocol or plain record reached via an edge-less `from tpy import X` could be stranded in a consumer's registry the same way `Ptr` was -- the same mechanism, half-covered. NO witness yet: named cross-module imports create module edges that force ordering, so it may be unreachable in practice (the gap is specific to implicit-stdlib entities that record no edge). Repro FIRST; only if reproducible, generalize the re-index (or the loop) to cover all three steps -- do NOT broaden it speculatively (snapshot/behavior risk without a witness). Kept in TODO (not BUGS.md) because it is an unconfirmed latent gap, not a reproduced defect. Surfaced by /tpy-review (architecture-fit) + the /tpy-ready retrospective of `fix-channel-prereqs`.
- **[feature] Extend `unsafe_interior_mutable` to an inline (non-`Ptr`) field -- a C++ `mutable` member.** Today the hatch is `Ptr[T]`-only: `tpyc/sema/registration.py` rejects a non-pointer payload ("only supported on a Ptr[T] field"), so an interior-mutable primitive must live behind a raw pointer to a heap block (`unsafe_take`/`unsafe_release`). Allow `unsafe_interior_mutable[T]` (T a concrete, non-`readonly`/`Own`/nested type) to lower to an inline `mutable T` C++ member: registration accepts the non-`Ptr` inner and sets `is_interior_mutable`; codegen emits `mutable T name;` and suppresses const-projection on the field's access (the inline case of the flag the `Ptr` pointee already uses). Sound -- inline `mutable` is the same escape as the `Ptr` form (mutate through a shared readonly handle), just inline storage; the `Ptr`-only reject is conservatism/YAGNI, not a soundness gate, and the rename commit's own doc names "C++ `mutable` member" as an intended hatch form. Payoff: a `@nocopy` interior-mutable primitive with NO external pointer into it (nothing needs a stable/shared address, unlike `Mutex`'s guard cell or `Rc`/`Arc`'s shared refcount cell) becomes allocation-free. First consumer: `tpy.sync.Condvar` -- its `_cv` currently heap-allocates (`unsafe_interior_mutable[Ptr[_RawCondvar]]`) only because the hatch forces a `Ptr`; inline `unsafe_interior_mutable[_RawCondvar]` drops that alloc and keeps `_RawCondvar` an honest non-const wrapper (vs. the alternative of faking const ops in the C++ wrapper). Design decision on the escape hatch -> own `/tpy-add-feature` pass; do NOT bundle into the channel work. Surfaced discussing the Condvar allocation.
- **[cleanup] Consolidate the two receiver-mutation-recording sites.** `MethodAnalyzer` (`tpyc/sema/methods.py` ~849-929) + `CallAnalyzer._record_mutation_call_edges` (`tpyc/sema/calls.py`) record "calling this method mutates the receiver" for EXPLICIT calls; `_record_iter_receiver_mutation` (`tpyc/sema/statements.py`) mirrors a copy of the same logic for a for-loop's implicit `__iter__` (interior-field exemption, `mark_loop_var_mutated`, self-deferred-edge vs `mark_param_mutated`, parent-inclusive lookup). Two sites deciding the same question is a drift risk (the iter mirror already once shipped missing the parent lookup + `mark_loop_var_mutated`, caught by /tpy-review). Extract the shared receiver-mutation core into one helper both paths call -- the wrinkle is the explicit path records the Phase-2 edge separately in `calls.py` while the implicit path records it inline, so unifying also has to reconcile the edge-recording split. Own refactor pass; do NOT bundle into other in-flight work. Surfaced by /tpy-review (architecture-fit + safety-model) of the const-receiver `__iter__` fix.
- **[test-gap] Two `__del__` fail-fast paths lack a witness.** (1) A throwing CALL in a wrap-free `__del__` (no `with`/`try`/`raise`, so `_body_has_literal_throw` leaves it unwrapped) aborts at the C++ `noexcept` boundary via the generic `tpy_terminate_handler` (`TurboPython panic: uncaught <Type>: ...`), a DIFFERENT message/mechanism than the wrapped path's `report_del_exception` (`... exception in __del__: ...`) -- the code comment asserts this but no case exercises it. (2) A `with`/`try` `__del__` that ACTUALLY throws at runtime (vs the current clean-run smoke cases) would confirm `__exit__`/`finally` still runs before the wrap aborts. Both are low-priority (path (1) is C++-guaranteed noexcept behavior, not TPy codegen); add cases only if this area churns again. Surfaced by /tpy-review (test-coverage) of the `__del__` fail-fast change.
- **[thir, PARKED design-adjacent] `inherited_accessor_subst`'s last blocker: a field WRITE through a borrow-returning property receiver (`h.val.x = 8` -> `h.val().x = 8`).** The write mutates the aliasee through a call-result borrow -- neither a binding nor an escape (the loan dies at the statement), so it PARALLELS the ratified expression-scoped READ slice, but as a WRITE it sits beside the `call.ret_type.record_borrow` REF_ALIAS design stop whose widenings need their own decision. Decide: extend the ratified expression-scoped slice to statement-scoped WRITES through the borrow (field writes / setitem), or keep closed. One witness; the case's other blockers all cleared in the pointee-accessor waves.
- **[test-gap] `union/wrapper_param_const` is read-only through its `Expr&` return.** The case's own comment claims `passthru` returns a live alias, but main() never mutates through the returned reference -- a silent-copy regression at that boundary would not show in output.txt (the CLAUDE.md mutate-after-boundary rule). Now committed to the THIR ratchet, so worth closing: redesign with a mutate-and-observe assertion (append through the returned alias, then read via the original binding). Touches the case's expected output -- consult before update_snapshots per the snapshot policy. Surfaced by /tpy-review (cpython-parity) of the union-returns wave.
- **[test-gap] `tplib.channel`'s blocking-wakeup paths lack a deterministic witness.** Two paths in the blocking channel are only indirectly exercised: (1) `Sender.close()` waking a producer PARKED on the full ring (`_not_full`), and (2) `Receiver.__del__` waking producers parked on a full ring so they observe the close and raise `ChannelClosed` instead of deadlocking (the primitive's core anti-deadlock guarantee). Both require a producer thread actually blocked on `_not_full` at the close/drop instant, which isn't forceable without stress/sleeps -- so they're untested by the deterministic `channel_*` cases (`channel_mpsc` exercises drop-based close and send-blocking, but not the receiver-drop-wakes-a-blocked-sender edge). Add a best-effort stress case (modeled on `arc_spawn`'s probabilistic-but-real approach: many producers on a cap-1 channel, drop the receiver mid-run) rather than a flaky sleep-based one; low priority (the wake logic is verified sound by /tpy-review safety-model). Surfaced by /tpy-review (test-coverage) of `tplib.channel`.
- **[thir] Generics foundation -- landed cells + sliced-scope exclusions (branch `thir-generics-foundation`, 2026-07-16, dial 1241->1273).** TypeParamRef/bounds now thread through the decl / call-arg / method / return / coerce / subscript / setitem arms (bounded-T receivers via `_LowerCtx.tparam_bounds` -> the protocol checker; generic methods via `THIRMethodCall.method_targs_cpp`; raw-T method-slot temps; INT-kind `[N: int]` seeding; explicit `f[int](x)` targs; `copy(T-source)`). DEFERRED, filed as part of the same approval: (a) **resumable template frames** (`res.generic` / `res.generic_record`) -- DONE 2026-07-16, and the "separate emitter tier" premise was wrong: the template header and the `val_or_ref_t<T>` CAPTURE choice are SKELETON (AST-emitted), so both gates deleted outright and a bare `T` joined the new capture-only `_res_capture_ok` (param / return / yield -- NOT locals: a bare-`T` local is a `T*` alias, pinned by `test_generic_bare_t_local_still_defers`); only static-protocol coro params (`res.param_type` / `res.await_param_type`) remain from that slice; (b) **overloaded generic callees** (`len(fis) != 1` -> `call.callee_kind.generic`) -- per-overload arg loops + literal mangling; (c) **generic static-marker method targs** (`method.marker.static.generic.method_targs`, 1 case); (d) record rvalues into free-call T slots (the AST's covariant CHILD-typed temp, deliberately unmirrored). Left to the case-driven waves (concrete shapes, not generics): value-record copy decls (`q = p`), readonly-Ptr value decl slots, None-element containers (`list_dict_none`), chained method receivers (`box.get().append(4)`). ~57 `generics/` cases remain marked, all multi-blocker or wave-territory.
- **[thir][test-gap] Generics-foundation rows covered only by ratcheted corpus cases, not unit pins.** Each is guarded (the flipped `generics/` case fails the suite on regression, and the whole-corpus byte-diff pins the emit) but has no focused case: (a) `_tparam_name_pass_arg`'s ctor face (`self.inner = Box[T](value)` -- corpus: `generic_nested`); (b) record-level INT-kind seeding + the `int_type_param_*` coerce rows + T-element setitem/getitem (corpus: `generic_int_param_*`); (c) `call.copy_tparam` (corpus: `generic_own_return`); (d) bounded-T protocol ARG-passing (only the no-arg receiver is unit-pinned); (e) a marker-only bound negative (`[T: Send]` must resolve to no protocol and stay AST -- `_bounded_tparam_protocol`'s docstring promises it); (f) container/str sub-branches of the T-slot NAME row (only records pinned); (g) `_tparam_slot_temp_arg`'s literal branches (only the ctor-rvalue branch pinned); (h) negative pins for deliberately-AST shapes (record rvalue into a free generic-call T slot; reassigned `Own[T]` local); (i) the const CONTAINER alias off a `@readonly` method (`const std::vector<T>& xs = holder.get_items();` -- the record case is pinned, the `_alias_ref_container` composition is hand-traced only); (j) a `{T}`-template container/view stub method carrying method-level inferred targs would emit the placeholder raw (no such stub exists today -- the admission doesn't reject `fi.type_params` on those receiver families; add the reject or a witness when one appears); (l) `_f1_record_type_arg_ok`'s container/None/FloatLiteral widening fans out to EVERY `_f1_record` caller at once (decl, ctor instantiation, receivers) -- rows (b)/(f) pin it only per-consumer; a shared-predicate unit over the arg slice itself would pin the fan-out. Also hygiene: the nested-generic T->T arm in `_generic_plain_arg_ok` and `_tparam_name_pass_arg` intentionally differ (substituted vs unsubstituted slot-name compare, Own-unwrap) -- if a third T-name pass-through row appears, unify behind one subst-aware helper instead of a third copy. And: gate and lowering RE-DERIVE the raw method fi independently (the shape gate's `get_method_overloads_with_parents` overload vs lowering's `_raw_record_method_fi` -- same lookup, two sites); this exact split already bit twice on the generics branch (an own-methods-only lookup missed inherited methods; the vararg slot read the substituted fi where the AST reads the raw one) -- fold the raw-fi resolution into ONE place consumed by both sides, kin to the filed pointer-indirection single-resolution-point item. - **[thir][test-gap] Newly-reachable param-read fallbacks and guard-call temp boundary lack unit witnesses.** After the callable/param preflight removal (`_f1_param_eligible` / `_ctor_param_eligible` deleted), `_unrouted_binding_read`'s `name.own_optional_read` / `name.optional_ptr_read` reject branches became reachable from ordinary function params for the first time, but no unit routes a body READ of such a param (own-optional / non-F1 pointer-repr-optional) to prove the fallback fires rather than mis-lowering -- mirror the existing `test_own_str_body_read_stays_ast`. Same gap for a plain-function (not constructor) used-but-unsupported param (e.g. a `Callable`/`Waker`-typed param actually called). And with match guards now admitting calls, add a unit pinning the guard-call-needing-arg-temp boundary: the temp forms raise `ThirUnsupported` (not `assert`) since a guard is never a flush point, so the body must fall back cleanly. Surfaced by /tpy-review (test-coverage, architecture-fit).
