- **[ergonomics] Allow a `Final[enum]` module constant as a default parameter (and field) value.** The enum-MEMBER default half is DONE (`def f(order: MemoryOrder = MemoryOrder.SEQ_CST)` works; the `tpy.atomic` sentinel was retired). The remaining half is a `Final[EnumType]` module constant used as a default: still rejected because `tpyc/typesys.py:2631` restricts `Final` to "only primitive types and tuple". Relax that restriction to admit `Final[enum]` (an enum member is a compile-time constant with a scoped-enumerator C++ form), then the existing `Final`-name default path (`codegen_cpp/functions.py` `default_to_cpp` `TpyName` arm) already emits it. Separable and lower-value than the member half was. Surfaced writing `tpy.atomic`.
- **[feature] Mutable (non-readonly) property getter -- unblocks a faithful lazy-cached `.content`.** Every `@property` getter is unconditionally marked `auto_readonly` (`tpyc/parse/parser.py:1792`), so `sema/method_expansion.py` clones it into a const + mutable overload pair and the body must type-check as BOTH -- a getter that mutates/caches into `self` (the requests `Response.content` lazy-drain idiom) fails the const clone ("Cannot call non-readonly method on readonly reference"). No current spelling produces a mutable-only property. Add one: a property getter that mutates self skips the const clone (or an explicit opt-out marker). Semantic cost to weigh in design: a mutable-only property makes `readonly[T].prop` uncallable (the getter demands a mutable receiver) -- the readonly system forbids read-mutation on purpose, so this is a deliberate narrowing, not a free win. Touches parser + `sema/method_expansion` + registration (type-system-adjacent) -> architectural, own `/tpy-add-feature` design. Payoff: `tplib.requests` `Response.content`/`.text`/`.json()` could auto-drain a `stream=True` body (matching real requests) instead of the current declared divergence (a streamed `.content` stays permanently `b""` -- never auto-filled; full-body via `r.raw.read()` / `iter_content`). Generally useful for any lazy-cached property. Surfaced designing requests streaming.
- **[diagnostic] Warn that a truthiness test is statically ALWAYS TRUE -- and stop rejecting `not rec` in the same change.** `if p:` on a user record with neither `__bool__` nor `__len__`, or on any plain enum value, is unconditionally true, and TPy says nothing: the user probably meant `p is not None`, an `== Member` compare, or a hook the type never defines. Sema ALREADY computes this exact fact, just to the opposite end -- it HARD-ERRORS on `not rec` ("Invalid operand type for 'not'") where CPython accepts it, the rejects-valid entry in BUGS.md. So one change closes both halves of the asymmetry: accept `not rec` (CPython-faithful) and warn that the test is always true, from the same no-truthiness-hook verdict. Design questions to settle FIRST (this is a new warning -- `/tpy-add-feature`, not a drive-by): (a) does it fire on an operand narrowed past None (`if p is None: return` then `if p:` -- always-true as a CONSEQUENCE of the narrowing, which defensive code writes deliberately; witness `tests/cases/bool/bool_narrowed_optional` `plain_if`), (b) generic `if x:` on a `T` monomorphized to a plain record would warn per instantiation, un-actionably, in code the author cannot change, (c) there is no escape hatch spelling today -- `bool(p)` is itself rejected for value types without `__bool__` (its own BUGS.md entry), so "I meant it" has no form but deleting the check. Churns `diag.txt` + `# tpyc: ok` annotations at roughly 19 corpus sites (the always-true renders, greppable as `static_cast<void>(...), true`). Belongs beside `OPTIONAL_VALUE_TRUTHINESS_WARNING` (`tpyc/diagnostics.py`, raised from `tpyc/sema/narrowing.py`), the existing member of this diagnostic family. Surfaced by the user reviewing the always-true renders after the constant-fold operand fix.
- **[thir] Enum-typed module globals are not seeded for reads, so any read falls the whole body back.** `_readonly_global_type` (`tpyc/thir/lower/predicates.py:1300`) admits scalars, char, str/bytes, `Ptr` and value-tuples to the read-only value-global family but leaves "unions/enums unprobed", so `gc: Color = Color.RED` plus ANY read (`return gc`, `if gc:`) rejects at `name.global_read` (`tpyc/thir/lower/expressions.py:2396`) -- while an `int32` global routes bare and a plain-record global routes through the pointer-slot family. An enum is a value type whose read renders bare, so admitting it looks like a small widening, but "unprobed" is a not-yet-verified marker rather than an oversight, so it needs its own byte-diff verification (unions likewise, and they are the harder half). Pre-existing; newly reachable from truthiness position because the plain-enum always-true arm now lowers its operand instead of returning early, so `if gc:` meets the same gate that `return gc` always did. Repro: `gc: Color = Color.RED` at module scope + `def f() -> Color: return gc` -- lower it and read `_thir_reject_reason` (`name.global_read`); swap the annotation to `int32` or a plain record and it routes. Surfaced removing the truthiness purity predicate.
- **[thir] Per-case blockers for the truthiness cases left ratchet-exempt (from the constant-fold operand fix) -- THREE OF THE FIVE ARE NOW ROUTED, two remain.** `bool/truthy_call_effects`, `match/guard_truthy_call` and `enum/enum_truthy_call_int` all flipped in the 2026-07-27 truthiness wave (`_ExprUse.truthy_discard` for the `@property` returning `Own[T]`; `_lower_match_guard` now going through `_lower_truthy`; the IntEnum shape gate deleted). STILL BLOCKED, each ONE construct and already measured: `typed_dict/typed_dict_in_call` -> `stmt.if:if.cond_binop.in.str_record_f1` (the TypedDict `in` fold is un-migrated -- the one of the three fold sites whose AST fix has no THIR mirror, since the construct rejects wholesale); `bool/truthy_walrus_binding` FLIPPED 2026-08-03 (long-tail wave 4: the ALWAYS_TRUE walrus mode + the enum first-decl walrus row).
- **[thir] The value-position `and`/`or` bare-literal truthiness form has no THIR shape, and no case for its temp-hoisted LHS.** `_gen_logical_value` (`tpyc/codegen_cpp/expressions.py`) calls `_truthy_for_rendered` WITHOUT an operand, so the fold emits the bare literal -- correct, because the LHS is either a bare name or already materialized into a temp before the truthiness test runs. THIR cannot reach that shape at all: a value-position `and`/`or` with a non-scalar/non-str LHS rejects at `valuesel.lhs_truthy` (`tpyc/thir/lower/expressions.py` ~1466), which is why `THIRTruthy.operand` and `THIREnumWrap.operand` could be tightened to required and their bare-literal emit branches deleted. **The two are coupled**: widening `valuesel.lhs_truthy` to enum / plain-record LHS types needs an operand-less THIR form restored first, or the mirror cannot reproduce the AST's bare literal. Coverage gap on the AST side too -- `operators/logical_and_or_value` and `operators/logical_record_or_rvalue` both use a `TpyName` LHS (`use_lhs_temp` False), so the temp-hoisted variant of the always-true type family is unwitnessed. Safe by construction today (no dual-path divergence is possible while THIR rejects the position). Surfaced by /tpy-review of the constant-fold operand fix.
- **[thir][hygiene] Classifier/helper param order is inconsistent across siblings -- swap-prone once `_WalkState` is gone.** Removing the `_WalkState` bundle spread its fields (`declared`, `pointers`, `rebind_slots`, `storage_tuple_locals`, `narrowed`) as separate positional params across the remaining expression/comprehension helpers and the `for`/`match` classifiers in `tpyc/thir/lower/`, but the order is not uniform between siblings (e.g. `checks.py:_ref_field_write_ok(stmt, declared, analyzer, pointers, narrowed, prescan)` vs `_optional_record_field_write_ok(stmt, declared, pointers, analyzer, narrowed, prescan)` -- `analyzer`/`pointers`/`narrowed` swap positions). Since `pointers` and `narrowed` are both bare `set[str]`, nothing catches an accidental swap at a future call site. Options: (a) unify the arg order across the family, or (b) introduce a small FROZEN read-only carrier (a `NamedTuple`/frozen dataclass of the same fields, no `branch_copy`/mutation methods -- distinct from the deleted mutable `_WalkState`). The carrier-vs-flat call is a design choice; some of the ordering skew is pre-existing carry-forward. Surfaced by /tpy-review (architecture-fit) of `thir-lower-reject-expressions`.
- **[thir][hygiene] `THIRGenExpr` stores pre-rendered C++ strings where the sibling node keeps facts structured.** `_lower_genexpr` (`tpyc/thir/lower/comprehensions.py`) pre-renders `binding_cpp` (via `loop_var_binding`) and both `iife_captures`/`inner_captures` lists (via `_genexpr_captures`, called twice) into `THIRGenExpr` at lowering time, whereas the sibling `THIRComprehension` carries the equivalent facts structured (`var`, `elem_type`) and defers the `loop_var_binding`/capture render to `_emit_comprehension` in `emit.py`. Both nodes already store SOME rendered cpp (`container_cpp`, `cpp_iterable`), so this is a lower/emit boundary-placement inconsistency, not a bug -- byte-identical today. Refactor to carry `var`/`elem_type` + a structured captured-names tuple and build the capture list once in `_emit_genexpr`. Non-trivial (moves the capture logic across the boundary). Surfaced by /tpy-review (architecture-fit) of the generator-expression cells.
- **[thir][post-deletion] Replace the pre-rendered-string node fields with structured type refs once the AST codegen is deleted.** The whole rendered-cpp family on THIR nodes -- `THIRCall.template_args_cpp`, `THIRMethodCall.method_targs_cpp`, `THIRVarDecl.cpp_type`, `THIRArgTemp.cpp_type`, `variant_cpp`/`callee_cpp`/the `THIRGenExpr` fields above -- stores resolver-rendered strings because (a) the spelling needs the lowering-time `TypeResolver` (cross-module qualification, pending-view resolution) and emit is deliberately a resolver-free printer (`_EmitState` carries only counters/sinks), and (b) rendering at lowering through the same functions the AST uses is what makes the byte-diff invariant checkable. AFTER the AST path is deleted that constraint relaxes: move the family to structured `TpyType` refs on the nodes and give the emitter a render context (a resolver handle or render callback), one boundary-move pass over the whole family -- not field-by-field, which would split sibling nodes across two conventions. Aligns with CLAUDE.md's LSP tie-breaker (introspectable/printable type representations) and IR_DESIGN's post-deletion end state (emitter becomes a printer over a real IR). User-agreed 2026-07-16 during the generics-foundation review.
- **[thir] Protocol boundary -- the rungs the param/arg cells deliberately left out.** The bare protocol param, the protocol-receiver method call, the protocol call-arg slot (Adapter / RefAdapter / concrete + `auto` rvalue temps) and `len(p)` are routed. Excluded, roughly by remaining mass: (a) **`Own[P]` params and returns** (~16 bodies, incl. 2 resumable) -- `T_p&&` / `std::unique_ptr<P>` slots whose reads move, whose method calls render `->` (`_receiver_is_own_dyn`), and whose call args take `::tpy::make_adapter<Base>` / `std::make_unique` (`_gen_dynamic_protocol_own_arg`); (b) **protocol RETURNS** (~8) -- `auto` (structural) / `Base&` (@dynamic); (c) **resumable protocol params** (21 blocked at `res.param_type`) -- need the two-phase `decltype` frame capture (`thir/lower/resumable.py`, `protocol_param_template_name`); (d) **`Optional[P]` / protocol-union params and arg slots** -- `_gen_protocol_arg`'s typed-null / `&(...)` / `optional_to_ptr` renders; (e) **protocol SUBSCRIPT** (~16 at `subscript.recv_type`) -- NOT uniform: `items[0]` emits `::tpy::__getitem__(items, 0)` while `items[i]` emits `items[static_cast<std::size_t>(i)]`, so the rung must first establish which dispatch the AST picks; (f) **protocol slots in the record-method arg loop** (`_record_method_call_supported` still rejects them as `method.arg_shape`, though `_gen_method_call`'s user-record loop does run the protocol pre-arms); (g) **for-each over a protocol iterable**, which rides the `stmt.for_each` rock (the corpus's #1 blocker, 333b/184sh). Landed on `thir-protocol-boundary`.
- **[thir][telemetry] `return`-of-record-source fallback reasons lost their sub-tags in the gate-removal inlining.** The inlined `TpyReturn` record-source reject in `tpyc/thir/lower/statements.py` (~2056) now routes both the `Own`-typed-source-at-a-borrow-slot case (old `return.record_source.own_at_borrow`) and the non-F1-record bare-name source (old `return.record_source.name_notf1`) through the generic `_record_source_reject_detail` bucket (`return.record_source.name.{slot}`). Correctness is unaffected (accept/reject boolean unchanged; byte-diff green), but `$THIR_FALLBACK_JSON` triage can no longer distinguish these two return-source fallback causes. Restore the two `note_detail` calls at the collapsed branch if the distinction is still wanted for porting triage. Surfaced by /tpy-review (codegen-correctness + architecture-fit) of `thir-read-only-admission`.
- **[thir][test-gap] Two protocol arg arms are unit-covered but never routed-and-exec-diffed by the corpus.** (1) The @dynamic structural-conformer **lvalue** RefAdapter arg (`::tpy::RefAdapter<Base,C> __tmp{p}`, `_protocol_arg_temp` `rvalue=False` / `is_dyn_protocol` branch): the case written for it, `tests/cases/protocols/protocol_dynamic_structural`, still carries `no_thir.txt` because its `main()` falls back wholesale on an unrelated var-decl (`pet: Pet = Parrot()`), so the `greet(p)` RefAdapter site is never emitted from THIR. (2) The ctor-protocol-param path (the `_ctor_param_eligible` doc update admitting a protocol param on `__init__`): `protocol_method_dynamic_param` falls back for pre-existing reasons (`ctor.mil_field.nominal.method`, `field.result_type`). Both arms are hand-verified correct; the units that pinned them went with the THIR unit suite, so this is a corpus end-to-end blind spot, not a live bug -- flip these cases (or add a minimal exec case) once the unrelated blockers clear. Surfaced by /tpy-review (cpython-parity + test-coverage) of `thir-protocol-boundary`. [RESOLVED 2026-08-06: the owned-str call-rvalue MIL leg cleared it; case FLIPPED. Prune on next sweep.]
- **[thir][test-gap] Resumable leaf-shape rejects moved into `_lower_stmt_dispatch` are exercised only incidentally.** The predictive `_leaf_shape_reject`/`_gate_leaf` scan in `tpyc/thir/lower/resumable.py` was deleted; its rejects (`res.leaf_field_write` gated on `scope.in_branch`, `res.unpack`, `res.leaf_try`, `res.leaf_with`, `res.leaf_match`, `res.nested_def`; `res.leaf_return` ROUTED 2026-07-17) now fire inline in `_lower_stmt_dispatch` under `lc.resumable_leaf_mode`. No dedicated case pins the moved reject (e.g. a name-write nested two levels inside an `if` in an `async def` with no `await` in that branch); coverage rides on pre-existing `no_thir`-marked `tests/cases/async/*` cases being re-diffed by the overlay. Add a minimal case so the moved invariant is explicit, not incidental. Surfaced by /tpy-review (test-coverage) of `thir-structural-plans`.
- **[thir] Assert emit idempotence directly -- the harness depends on it but nothing states it.** The THIR overlay re-emits each local user module a second time, so "a module emits identically every time" is now load-bearing for the whole corpus -- yet it is an emergent property of the overlay, not a tested invariant. `recursive_alias_cpp_names` violated it (a definer rendered its own generic recursive alias qualified on a second pass) and the overlay caught it only incidentally; the bug was not a THIR divergence at all and reproduced with THIR fully off. `tpyc/test_compiler.py::TestCodegenStateIsolation` pins the one map. Generalize: double-emit every module on the AST path and byte-compare, so the next per-module codegen map that forgets its reset fails directly instead of masquerading as a THIR bug. Needs no THIR, and covers cases THIR never touches. Surfaced by `fix-recursive-alias-name-leak`.

Two same-named protocols in different modules could resolve to the wrong one; downstream the damage is bounded (the solved type still passes through the real bound's conformance check, so worst case is rejection-of-valid, not a miscompile -- probed with a two-module `Container` collision). Route the lookup through the bound's qname / `protocol_info_of(bound)` instead of the short-name scan when next touching this area.

Each one sends a reader to a path that does not exist, and the count is large enough that fixing them one-at-a-time as they are noticed will not converge. Do it as one sweep: grep the four names across `docs/` and `TODO.md`, and for each hit either re-point it at the lowering/emit site or, where the entry was only ever about the deleted emitter, drop it. The same sweep should catch the ~220 `AST path` / `fallback` phrasings in `tpyc/thir/test_*.py` comments, which describe a second author that no longer exists.

## THIR: a readonly field is rejected in the ctor member-init lowering (2026-08-30)

A record with `s: readonly[str]` and `n: readonly[int32]` and a two-line
`__init__` is rejected at `ctor.mil_field.nominal.name`; a single
`readonly[str]` alongside a plain `int32` lowers. So the trigger is a
`readonly[BigInt]` field, or two readonly fields together, rather than
readonly as such -- which is why it is not visible on the single-readonly
shape a test author would reach for first.

Found while shaping a match field-literal case around a readonly field: the
case had to be built with one readonly field instead of two to compile at all,
which is the same corpus-expressiveness constraint the void-body gap above
imposes. Unrelated to `match`; it is in the constructor lowering.

## THIR: a match arm in a void-returning body is rejected (2026-08-30)

**A match arm in a `-> None` body is rejected** (`body:stmt.match`). Isolated rather than assumed
-- the same arm in an `-> int32` body lowers, and the flat spelling of the
same match is rejected identically, so the trigger is the void return and not
the pattern shape or a container binding. It bites case authors directly: a
new case whose match arm returns nothing does not compile, so the fixture has
to be reshaped to return a value. That is a constraint on what the corpus can
express, which makes it worth closing rather than routing around.

## THIR: narrowed-name match subjects are rejected (2026-08-30)

`tpyc/thir/lower/match.py` returns `None` -- reject -- whenever a match
subject is a name in the narrowing map (`subj.name in narrowed`), and it does
so across ALL tiers, not just resumable ones. Verified with a plain sync
`def` holding a nested narrowed match: it is rejected with `body:stmt.match`,
no generator or async involved. That is ordinary valid Python that compiled
correctly before the deletion and is a compile error now.

Why nothing caught it before: no corpus case carries the shape, so every gate
was silent on it.

Sequencing note, now moot on its first half: the AST's own narrowed-subject
guard also rejected valid code, so the lane was ordered AST-first to avoid
mirroring a known-wrong rejection. That emitter is gone; what remains is
lowering the shape here, and it is wave-sized rather than a patch.

The lane must also re-check the non-lvalue capture gate in
`_select_match_route`. That gate guards a real use-after-free (a frame field
holding the address of a by-value dispatch local), and today narrowed subjects
never reach it because the reject above fires first. Routing them removes that
backstop. The gate's non-lvalue-only condition is believed to be the correct
final shape -- a narrowed subject that is an lvalue is frame-rooted, so it
should be admitted -- but that belief is untested precisely because nothing

What is actually left is the `storage_tuple_locals` acknowledgment plus the owned-tuple PARAM seeds. ## Next
- **[HIGH][tooling] Runtime counters for reference-type copies and heap allocations, committed per case and ratcheted.** Every class in `docs/PITFALLS.md` that the suite is blind to is a copy or an allocation the output does not show: the cpy phase compares stdout, the snapshot pins whatever was emitted, and a reviewer reads. Under a test-build macro, the copy constructor of every emitted record and the runtime containers increments a counter, and a global `operator new` hook counts heap allocations; the harness prints both per case and commits them as a ratchet, so a change that adds a copy or an allocation to a case fails even when its output is byte-identical. Copies must reconcile with the diagnostics in BOTH directions (`silent-copy-vs-alias`, `copy-warning-at-wrong-site`): copies == explicit `copy()` calls + warned sites. **The heap counter is BLIND to `str`/`bytes` materialization**: `std::string("b")` fits the small-string optimization and never reaches `operator new`, so the `view-not-copy` class (the 2026-09-06 needle regression, the set-literal lookups that still built a string per C literal) shows zero. That class is countable only at the CONSTRUCTION site: either the emitted-C++ scanner below, or -- the exact form -- route every codegen-authored materialization through one runtime helper (`tpy::owned(view)` or similar) that the macro counts and the scanner greps, instead of spelling `std::string(` / `bytes_copy(` at each site. Deciding that routing is a design fork for the counter branch, not a detail. Filed 2026-09-07 from the corrections audit (`docs/PITFALLS.md`).
- **[HIGH][tooling] Three pure-Python checks over the corpus and the lowering, each replayed against the case it was filed from.** (1) A hidden-allocation SNAPSHOT SCANNER in `/tpy-ready`: a hunk that adds `std::string(` / `bytes_copy(` / a container construction / a `BigInt(` temporary where the previous line had a bare literal or a view is a finding, never churn to acknowledge -- the `dict.setdefault` double allocation and the `list.remove` owned needle both showed in the snapshot diff and nobody read them against the mapping. This is the instrument for the SSO-blind class above. (2) A HARDCODING RATCHET over `tpyc/thir/`: the 119-site survey (method names, runtime symbols, `is_list or is_dict or ...` family enumerations, `container_gates.py`'s count) as a committed script with a ceiling that must not grow; catches the special-cased stub methods of 2026-09-06 and the per-kind bytearray legs. (3) NOCOPY-ABLATION as a pytest flag over new or changed happy cases: recompile the case with every user record marked `@nocopy`; a case that still passes could not have seen a copy and needs the marker or a mutating leg, one that fails names a real copy. Twelve cases in one three-day window passed three specialist rounds and the readiness gate while unable to distinguish a move from a copy; the CLAUDE.md prose rule did not hold. One cheaper lint rides along and landed first (`tests/test_diag_text.py`): (4) `no-cpp-in-diagnostics` / `no-internal-names-in-diagnostics` as a grep over every diagnostic string in `tpyc/` and every committed `diag.txt` (`std::`, `::tpy::`, `int32_t`, `string_view`, `Tpy[A-Z]\w+`; baseline debt is the two escaping-closure `string_view` files, allowlisted until reworded). (`error_` cases are never run under CPython -- decided 2026-09-07 -- so `reject-valid-python-only-as-documented-divergence` stays a reviewer probe, not a harness check.) Filed 2026-09-07.

The tag is also the key the step-6 reject queue and its `error_*` witnesses are organized by, so `tests/test_diag_text.py` does NOT police it: a ratchet would fail every batch that adds a witness. - **[MED][diagnostics] Give every diagnostic a stable code, registry-backed, and let tests pin the code instead of the wording.** Today 698 diagnostic sites emit free text, the corpus holds 1866 distinct diagnostic lines, and 2283 `# tpyc: error(/regex/)` / `warning(/regex/)` annotations pin WORDING, so every rewording churns annotations and a message can drift from its siblings unnoticed. A registry entry per diagnostic -- a slug in the `BUGS.md` style (`copy-into-field`, `unsupported-pattern-form`), not an opaque number -- with the canonical template and a one-paragraph explanation: annotations accept `error(copy-into-field)` beside the regex form; `tpyc --explain <code>` prints the explanation next to the existing `--explain-send` / `--explain-sync`; `tests/test_diag_text.py` checks the registry's templates instead of the reached corpus, so an unreached diagnostic is covered too; per-code suppression and an LSP get a key for free. Land it incrementally: the registry plus the annotation form first, a code REQUIRED for every new diagnostic from then on, existing sites back-filled in sweeps by module. - **[MED][tooling] A semantics-preserving REWRITE harness: the same seed program at every position and every wrapper, compiled, run and compared.** From seed cases, generate variants -- the body moved into a method, a constructor, module scope, a generator, an async body, a comprehension, a closure; the subject wrapped as `(x,)` and `(x, 1)`; `str` swapped for `bytes` -- and assert identical output under TPy and CPython, the same diagnostic class, and (once the counters exist) the same copy and allocation counts across variants. This is the mechanical successor of `same-construct-every-position` and `tuple-equals-scalar` in `docs/PITFALLS.md`, and the only instrument that reaches shapes no case has: `dualgen.py` diffs one hand-supplied file and nothing in the repo generates programs. Design fork: corpus-driven mutation of existing cases (cheap, biased to shapes the corpus already has) vs a grammar-driven generator over the type and wrapper space (more work, finds what no case reaches). Filed 2026-09-07.
- **[HIGH][tooling] Stand up compiler-CODE coverage over `tpyc/`, right after the cutover. We have never measured it, and every instrument we do have answers a different question.** The reject-site reach census, the arg-table family reach and the face/witness census all measure LANGUAGE-SHAPE coverage -- which shapes some test exercises. Nothing measures which compiler code no test executes. The two are not substitutes, and the 2026-09-01 sweep is the clean illustration: 39 probes fell back because no case covers those shapes, while the fallback machinery those probes ran through is heavily exercised, so line coverage would have reported those regions green. Plain `coverage.py` line/branch over `tpyc/` from the suite is cheap and would be a genuinely new signal.
  **Do it AFTER the flip, not before, and the reason is not scheduling.** With two emitters, an unreached arm in one of them is ambiguous -- it may be dead, or it may be live-but-shadowed by the other path taking the body. With one emitter that ambiguity is gone: an unreached render arm is dead code, full stop. So the same tool answers a much sharper question the day the AST body emitters are deleted, and the deletion itself is the largest coverage event this codebase will ever have. Expect the first run to be noisy -- `tpyc/` holds error paths, `@native` arms and option-gated branches no ordinary case reaches -- so budget for a triage pass, and treat the output as a worklist rather than a ratchet until it has been read once.
- **[codegen, rejects-valid and LOUD -- not a miscompile] A for-loop variable and a `with` target sharing one name collide in the frame layout.** `gen_async._frame_layout` collects `source_form_fields` from `for_loop_info` then `update`s it with `with_target_payloads`, so the with payload wins and the loop's own `pointer_form_loop_var` classification is never reconciled with the plan verdict. **Severity adjudicated 2026-08-29:** two entries described this site and were read as disagreeing (silent miscompile vs loud failure). They do not disagree -- both bodies say the advance step writes one form against a field declared as another, which is a hard C++ type mismatch. It fails loudly at `frame_slot<T&>::emplace(T&&) = delete`; only one entry's HEADLINE said miscompile, and that word was wrong. Reachable only when one name is both a source-form loop var and a `with` target. Reproduces on master, so it is pre-existing. Fix shape: make the two producers disjoint or state which wins and why -- the current resolution is an accident of dict ordering, not a decision, and master's only precedence pin covers source-form-vs-pointer-alias, not source-form-vs-source-form. Surfaced by /tpy-review (architecture-fit) and by the FrameLayoutPlan merge's semantic-conflict pass.
- **[thir] `with.opt_slot_target` has zero witnesses -- determine whether the shape still exists and delete the arm if not.** The `WithTargetArm.ASSIGN_OPT` row (`tpyc/thir/lower/statements.py`) mirrors a `with` target that an enclosing branch-decl pass hoist-predeclared into OPTIONAL_STORAGE, and the whole-corpus face census reports it unwitnessed. That is the same shape whose AST defect the with-target storage work closed (the hoist-predeclared `std::optional<Record>` target that COPIED `__enter__()`'s result where CPython aliases, fixed by binding an alias instead), so the arm may now be unreachable by construction -- but `_with_manager_needs_hoist` still tests `item.target not in self.ctx.optional_locals`, which reads as though a with target can still land there, so the causation is NOT established. Resolve it in one direction: either produce a case that witnesses the arm, or confirm the AST can no longer emit an optional-storage with target and delete arm + face together. An arm that can never route is exactly the unwitnessed admission the THIR contract's routing pin exists to prevent. Direct evidence from the with-family waves (2026-08-03): the one former candidate shape now provably takes the pointer arm, not ASSIGN_OPT (the unit that recorded that verdict went with the THIR unit suite) -- an ever-owned with-target name (borrow_only False at the branch-decl pass) is the remaining path that could still reach OPTIONAL_STORAGE; probe that shape first. Surfaced by /tpy-ready after merging master's THIR waves.
- **[tests] Cover two untested `with`-target frame shapes.** The with-target storage work pinned the aliasing, residency and single-slot rules, but two shapes still have no case: (a) a `with ... as t:` inside a `for`/`while` in a generator/async body, which re-enters `__enter__` and re-emplaces the frame slot each iteration; (b) a REFERENCE-typed target reassigned after the block (the existing `with_target_rebound_after_with` rebinds a value-typed `int32`, so the pointer-reseat of a with-target frame field is unexercised). Both are plausible homes for a wrong storage form, and (a) in particular re-runs the emplace path the aliasing fix changed. (The former multi-item shape is covered by `control_flow/with_target_multi_item_mixed`.) Surfaced by /tpy-review (test-coverage) of the with-target storage branch.
- **[CPython interop] the newly-buildable `default before required keyword-only` shape is unpinned at the `@export` boundary.** `docs/CPYTHON_INTEROP.md` documents `def f(a, b=10, *, c)` as building (the positional-defaults fix materializes that default at the call site instead of emitting it on the declaration), but no `tests/interop` case carries the shape -- the nearest is `combine(a, *, b, c=5)` in `tests/interop/defaults/src/defaults.py`, where no default PRECEDES the required keyword-only param. So a documented capability rests on the plain-TPy cases only, and the extra `PyArg_ParseTupleAndKeywords` interaction at the boundary is unverified. Adding it edits an existing interop case's committed snapshot, so it wants the snapshot-policy heads-up rather than a drive-by regen. Surfaced by the /tpy-review meta-review of the positional-defaults fix.
- **[CPython interop] boundary-message tests pin a CPython SNAPSHOT, not parity.** `tests/interop/defaults/src/ext_checks.py` asserts the `require_kwonly` text as hardcoded literals (`"f() missing 2 required keyword-only arguments: 'b' and 'c'"`). Those run ext-only, so the cpy-parity phase never cross-checks them, and the wording is CPython-version-dependent (the qualified `Cls.meth()` form in these messages arrived in 3.10) -- which is what the host-independent-output rule warns against. Fix shape: define an equivalent plain `def` inside `ext_checks.py`, call it the same wrong way, and compare the extension's `str(e)` against the live interpreter's, so the assertion tracks whatever CPython the suite runs under.
- **[CPython interop] `_boundary_default_expr`'s `Final` arm sniffs another phase's output string.** It qualifies a locally-defined `Final` default by testing `isinstance(default_expr, TpyName) and "::" not in rendered` -- i.e. it re-derives "was this already namespace-qualified?" from `default_to_cpp`'s rendered text rather than being told. The "an IMPORTED Final already comes back qualified" half is asserted only in a comment; only the local-Final path has a test. Fix shape: have `default_to_cpp` report the binding it resolved (or take the target namespace), and add an imported-Final default case.
- **[CPython interop] `registered_params` fails open into a codegen crash.** A lookup miss returns `[]`, so `unsupported_wrapper_param_form([])` admits every form, and codegen then indexes `fn_params[i]` for each declared param -> `IndexError` (an internal error, not a diagnostic). No reachable case is known -- unannotated `*args`/`**kwargs` are rejected upstream -- but a validator whose failure mode is silent admission should not degrade into a crash; raise `CodeGenError` at the emit site instead.
- **[tests] Make `protocols/isinstance_early_return_narrowing` mutate-and-observe through one alias.** Every cast-and-cache alias (`const Dog& __p = ...`) and every `narrowed = p` rebind in the case is read-only (`@readonly` methods throughout), so the cpy phase is parity-blind for copy-vs-alias at the extraction boundary; add one non-readonly mutator + post-alias observation. Snapshot-churning case change, rides the normal snapshot-consult flow. Surfaced by /tpy-review (cpython-parity, batch 4).
- **[tests] Make `generic_recursive_record_field` mutate-and-observe through its borrow boundary.** The newly-THIR-routed borrow shapes (`g = h.get()` aliasing the field; `leaf_count(h.t)` borrowing it) are only ever READ in the case, so the cpy phase is parity-blind for copy-vs-alias at exactly the boundary the genrec tail rows decide -- a future regression to copy-on-return would byte-match CPython. Probe-verified parity holds today (mutate-through-alias propagates on both). Add a mutation through `g` (e.g. `match g: case list() as b: b.append(...)`) and re-read via `h`; snapshot-churning case change, so it rides the normal snapshot-consult flow. Surfaced by /tpy-review (cpython-parity, genrec batch 3).
- **[tests] Add an exec+cpy regression case for union-element narrowing that MUTATES through the loop variable.** `tests/cases/union/union_iter_list` already iterates `list[Dog | Cat]` with an isinstance narrow, but it only PRINTS -- so it is parity-blind for copy-vs-alias exactly as CLAUDE.md's reference-type rule warns: a silent copy at the element binding would still byte-match CPython. THIR now routes that shape through the value-variant extraction (`auto& __x = std::get<Dog>(x);`), pinned only by the render of the case converted from the unit suite plus a scratch runtime probe. Add a case that mutates the narrowed element inside a helper and re-reads the container after, so the alias is asserted by exec+cpy rather than by generated-code inspection. Surfaced by /tpy-review (cpython-parity).
- **[codegen perf] Route narrowed-Optional container iteration through the native begin/end peephole.** `for k in d` over a narrowed `dict | None` (and list/set siblings) takes the universal `__iter__`/`__next__` path because `_gen_for_each_loop`'s NativeIterable check sees the declared `OptionalType` -- correct since the dangling-view fix, but each value-type element (e.g. a `std::string` dict key) is copied into the `val_or_ref` result per step, where the non-Optional receiver's begin/end peephole is copy-free. Dispatch on the narrowed inner type (like `narrowed_value_optional_iter_type` already does for value-repr `str|None`/`bytes|None`) so the pointer-repr narrowed receiver hits the peephole; the render side already derefs via `render_for_iterable`. Perf-only (one owned-string copy per element today). Surfaced reviewing the generated code of `iterable_long_str_elems`.
- **[sema hygiene] Consolidate the ctor-overload-group resolution duplicated between the raise and expression paths.** The oserror-exact branch grew two hand-synced copies of "resolve __init__ overload group (own or inherited via `get_method_overloads_with_parents`) + coerce args + own/readonly checks": `CallAnalyzer._resolve_ctor_overload_group` (`tpyc/sema/calls.py`) and the inline block in `StatementAnalyzer._analyze_raise` (`tpyc/sema/statements.py`), with drift in ambiguity reporting (calls.py routes `_ambiguous_overload_error`'s candidate-listing message; statements.py re-raises the bare `OverloadAmbiguityError.__str__`). Extract the shared logic into `sema/overloads.py` parameterized on args + error context. While there: (a) fold `_attach_ctor_overload_info` into `_set_record_constructor_info` via an optional pre-resolved `winner` param (near-verbatim duplicate today); (The former item (b) -- the hardcoded `"builtins.OSError"` warning sites -- was retired wholesale: the warning was replaced by the `@virtual_raise` raise-time mapping, leaving no OSError-specific compiler code.) Surfaced by /tpy-review (architecture-fit) of the oserror-exact branch.
- **[accepted divergence] Sibling submodule `__tpy_init` order is sorted, not CPython source order.** `from pkg import a, b` (and `from . import a, b`) store the imported names in a `set`, so source order is lost at parse time. Both submodule-injection paths (`_discover_absolute_submodule_imports`, `_resolve_relative_import`) now iterate `sorted(names)` for a *deterministic* (reproducible) build, but that is alphabetical, not left-to-right source order. Observable only if two sibling submodules have order-dependent top-level side effects (one's module body reads state the other's body sets) -- otherwise unobservable, and any real dependency is ordered by the discovery chain regardless. To match CPython faithfully, preserve name order through the parser (ordered container instead of a `set`) so the injected `TpyImport`s follow source order. Surfaced by /tpy-ready second-opinion of the submodule-init fix.
- **[sema hygiene] Verify or drop the `@property` sub-branch in `is_view_compatible_source`.** The property-access branch added to `is_view_compatible_source` (`tpyc/sema/local_deduction.py`) routes a property through `is_dangling_return(property_getter_call)`; its owned-str `-> False` arm is exercised (the @property owned-str-return fix), but the StrView `-> True` (view-safe) arm may be unreachable in practice because `_view_source_is_temporary` treats any `TpyFieldAccess` as non-temporary, so a StrView property source never reaches the pending-view machinery. Confirm the view-safe arm is reachable (some caller path -- walrus/annotated -- may hit it) or drop it as dead. Correct-if-reached, harmless if not. Surfaced by /tpy-review (safety-model, low confidence) of the @property owned-str fix.
- **[CPython interop] Continue past rungs 0-2 (harness gate now landed).** The ext-exec gate is done -- a first-class `tpyc` `.so` build mode (`tpyc -b` on an `# tpy: ext_module` -> `-fPIC -shared`, no `main`, `<mod>.so`) plus `tests/test_interop_exec.py` (snapshot glue/module C++ always; cached `.so` build + import + cpy-parity + ext_checks; facade self-check), retiring `verify.sh`. Every scalar marshaller is done -- `float` (C++ `double`), `bool` (truthiness via `PyObject_IsTrue`/`PyBool_FromLong`), all fixed-width ints (`int8`..`int64` / `uint8`..`uint64`, per-width range checks) -- plus void return (`-> None` -> `Py_RETURN_NONE`) and `str`/`bytes` (copy-in: PyUnicode <-> `std::string`, PyBytes <-> `std::vector<uint8_t>`; the boundary marshals the owned form and the function's borrow-form param converts at the call, so the glue emitter is unchanged). Containers are now done too (list/dict/set/tuple as @export fn params/returns, O(n) recursive copy-in/out -- see the dedicated entry below). Numeric `Span[T]` buffer input (phase 3) is now done too as an @export function PARAM (copy-in via the buffer protocol; see the dedicated entry below). Exposed-class dunders (Q4) are now DONE too (see the dedicated exposed-classes entry below). Containers/Span at the exposed-class METHOD boundary are now DONE too (method/`__init__` params/returns admit the same boundary set as free @export functions; getset fields stay scalar-only). @property on exposed classes is now DONE too (computed getset; see the exposed-classes entry below). Inheritance between exposed classes is now DONE too (single exposed same-module base -> real `tp_base` via `PyType_FromSpecWithBases`; base-before-derived creation, own-members-only tables + CPython slot/MRO inheritance, richcompare per-op delegation to the ancestor dispatcher, ctor inheritance, BASETYPE + tp_init exact-type guard rejecting Python-side subclass instantiation). Identity-preserving borrow returns are now DONE too (a `self`/param-sourced `-> Cls` return crosses as the ORIGINAL PyObject via a glue address match; see the dedicated entry below). Next candidates: the remaining exposed-classes deferred matrix -- static/classmethods, generic exposed classes and generic methods, and the CONTAINER getset field. (Public class-typed fields are DONE: a never-reassigned public reference-class field crosses as a read-only aliasing borrow-view getset, a reassignable one is a located error -- see the two matrix entries below.) Full phasing + locked design in `docs/CPYTHON_INTEROP.md`.
- **[CPython interop] exposed-class inheritance -- deferred slices.** (1) **Cross-module exposed base** (a base defined in another module is a located error, mirroring the cross-module enum/class-param guard; needs the general cross-module exposed-type story). (2) **Python-side subclassing of exposed bases** stays rejected at instantiation (tp_init exact-type guard) -- enabling it needs Python-override-aware dispatch from the C++ side (same root as the static-dispatch divergence; @dynamic territory). (3) **Multiple bases** are a PERMANENT reject (CPython refuses two bases with distinct C instance layouts), including one-exposed-base-plus-plain-record mixins (a second record base could displace the exposed base from offset 0). (4) **Value-type hierarchies at the boundary are untested** (sema allows a value-type record parent chain; the boundary composes per-class -- read-only getsets per value class -- but no interop case exercises it). (5) The `Instance<T>` payload static_asserts were relaxed for derived payloads (standard-layout -> !is_polymorphic + alignment cap); the non-movable-payload located-sema-pre-check TODO (filed at the internal-fields rung) now also covers polymorphic payloads reaching the static_assert as a raw g++ error when the @dynamic base is CONFORMED structurally rather than declared.

- **[CPython interop] identity-preserving returns -- deferred slices.** A borrow-form `-> Cls` return now crosses as the ORIGINAL PyObject when the returned reference address-matches a boundary-crossed candidate (`self` / an exposed-class param; `extension.py` `_scoped_alias_candidates` + `_emit_call_return`, candidates type-scoped to inheritance-related classes because an unrelated class can share the address via a first `_`-internal field). Deferred: (1) **`@nocopy` borrow-return stays a located error** -- now uniformly: dunder slots and readonly/bare-property spellings get the same located reject as plain methods (shared `nocopy_borrow_return_error` in `tpyc/interop/export_shape.py`, consumed by `the exposed-form check (tpyc/interop/module_validators.py)` and the dunder validator; in-place dunders exempt -- identity by construction). Enablement would allow an identity/view-safe body (`return self`/a param/a never-rebound field, the `view_safe_borrow_returns` classifier) by emitting the scan with an unreachable-error fallback instead of the copy; needs a decision on the no-match runtime error shape, and should cover methods + dunders together. (2) **The warning suppression is syntactic** (every return site a bare `self`/param name): a ternary `self if c else other` or a local alias (`x = self; return x`) still warns despite runtime identity preservation -- diagnostic-only false positive, extend the walk if it bites. (3) **DONE (branch interop-dunder-identity): every marshalled-return dunder slot threads identity/view candidates** -- binary/reflected/unary arithmetic, `__getitem__`, tp_iter, and tp_iternext all route through `_emit_call_return` with the branch's receiver + exposed-class operands as candidates (per-branch for the forward/reflected halves; the tp_iternext unwrap feeds the scan its `T&`; inherited halves classify against the declaring body via the ancestor-aware `_ast_method`), and sema's dunder warning dispatch collapsed to the method treatment (the `alias_records=None` always-copies wording variant is deleted; setitem/delitem returns are discarded, so they no longer warn at all). The arithmetic cells are LIVE (the two plain-TPy operator defects are fixed on fix-operator-dunder-borrow-returns) and witnessed in tests/interop/dunder_identity: binary self/operand identity, mutation through the crossed result, unary self, the readonly[...] spelling, and the class-typed __getitem__ KEY identity. SYSTEMIC NOTE (reduced but still live): sema suppression and the glue's per-site candidate lists are built independently (same rule, two constructions -- the glue's local names per slot vs boundary_alias_records' param names); the shared classifier keeps the ANSWERS in lockstep, but a forgotten candidate at a future emit-site kind would still silently copy while sema suppresses -- stamping the classification on the TpyFunction node (fact-on-node) is the THIR-era fix, and codegen re-walking each body at emit time (importing tpyc.interop.export_shape) goes away with it. The inherited-half rec_info asymmetry is ALIGNED: every method-family emit site classifies via _view_fallback_method, which pairs the declaring body with the DECLARING record's info (one construction rule at both ends; runtime candidates stay derived-typed). (4) **DONE (branch interop-field-borrow-views): never-reassigned field borrows ALIAS via borrow views** -- `return self._inner` (methods, free fns via params, property getters, tp_iter) and public never-reassigned reference-class fields (read-only getset) cross as a PyObject aliasing the live field: payload-pointer `Instance<T>` layout, owner keepalive, per-module address->view registry (type-scoped buckets; repeated accesses return the SAME view, so is/==/hash match plain Python), `within_payload` owner scan after the exact identity matches. Gate = `RecordInfo.fields_rebound_outside_init` (sema field-store hook; a rebindable field's view would read the storage SLOT through the rebind, so those keep copy+warn); one classifier (`view_safe_borrow_returns`) feeds both sema suppression and glue emission, one predicate (`exposed_view_field`) feeds validator admission and getset emit. The interim error-promotion alternative (uniform `-> Cls` = identity-only) is DROPPED -- the copy residue it targeted is now just module globals. Deferred sub-slices: (a) module-global sources still copy+warn (owner would be the module object -- decide if wanted); (b) upcast field views (field declared `Derived`, return `-> Base`) stay on the copy path (view would need the field's type handle per site; the gate is unit-pinned in tpyc/interop/test_export_shape_views.py -- a case-level witness is blocked by the derived-typed-field emit-order defect in BUGS.md); (c) deep paths (`self.a.b`) unclassified by sema (runtime range scan would handle them; extend the classifier if it bites); (d) Python-side rebind of a view getset is a loud AttributeError (a real setter needs registry invalidation at the store); (e) container ELEMENTS stay out permanently (realloc under a live view = UAF); (f) explicit `holder.__init__(...)` re-init is REJECTED (TypeError) while live views alias its fields (has_views_into registry scan in tp_init; a view's own `__init__` is likewise rejected) -- CPython would rebind attributes, so the loud reject is the acknowledged divergence; (g) exposed instances still wire no tp_traverse/tp_clear (pre-existing cyclic-GC gap, views add only acyclic owner edges). (5) Remaining boundary-semantics revisit items: Python-side subclassing enablement (guarded allow instead of the tp_init reject; must solve the `__new__` unconstructed-payload hazard in BUGS.md), container-element aliasing (permanently out: realloc under a live view). (6) **Property accessor FunctionInfos never get their `RefType` return/param wrapping** -- registration pops accessors out of `rec.methods` before `_normalize_function_info_refs` runs, so `PropertyInfo.getter.return_type` is the bare class; `_emit_call_return` works around it with a not-Own + reference-class borrow test. Proper fix: extend the normalization walk to `rec.properties`, then restore the plain `isinstance(RefType)` test in the glue.

- **[CPython interop] container boundary -- deferred slices.** `list`/`dict`/`set`/`tuple` cross the `@export` fn boundary O(n) by-copy, recursively (`marshal.hpp` `list_from_py`/`list_to_py`/`dict_*`/`set_*`/`tuple_*` element-fn-parameterized helpers; `extension.py` `_marshal_in_expr`/`_marshal_out_expr` emit nested per-element lambdas bottoming out at `from_py`/`to_py`). Recursion is glue-driven, NOT C++-template-driven: the C++ storage type is ambiguous at the leaves (`list[bytes]` and `list[list[uint8]]` both render `std::vector<std::vector<uint8_t>>`), so only the glue -- holding the unambiguous TPy element types -- can pick the leaf marshaller. `is_function_boundary_marshallable` recurses (new, split from the base `is_boundary_marshallable` which stays scalar/leaf-only; new `_container_element_types`/`_is_marshallable_element` in `type_def_registry.py`); the facade (`cpython_h.hpp`) gained the abi3 container C-API (type objects + List/Dict/Tuple accessors + iterator protocol for sets, since `PySet_Next` isn't in the limited API). Strict-by-container-kind IN (`PyType_IsSubtype` vs the exported type objects). Three acknowledged divergences documented (`docs/CPYTHON_INTEROP.md` "container cliff"): copy-in mutation (a mutated list/dict/set param **warns** via `mutated_params`; tuple exempt), strict-IN, per-element coercion (incl. dict-key collapse). Tests: `tests/interop/containers/`, `tests/cases/interop/{warn_export_container_mutation,error_export_container_exposed_element}`. **Deferred:** (1) **exposed class/enum types as TOP-LEVEL container ELEMENTS** -- DONE (branch `interop-container-element-exposed-types`): `list[Color]`, `list[Counter]`, `dict[str, Counter]`, `set[Color]`, `dict[Color, V]`, `tuple[Color, int64]` cross -- the per-element converter (`extension.py` `_marshal_in_expr`/`_marshal_out_expr` leaf arms) marshals each element through its module type handle (`instance_payload`/`instance_to_py`/`enum_from_py`/`enum_to_py`), copy-in/out; `_is_marshallable_element` admits exposed enum/class elements; a container param with an exposed element declares its local via `auto` (the bare element render isn't visible in the glue namespace) and `_elem_cpp` qualifies it. An exposed enum crosses in any position; an exposed CLASS as a `set` element or dict KEY is rejected by the general Hashable check before the boundary. **DEFERRED sub-slices (each a located error via `_exposed_form_error`'s `_unsupported_exposed_element`, NOT a misbuild -- surfaced by /tpy-review):** (1-i) **an exposed type NESTED inside a container element** (`dict[str, list[Counter]]`) -- HIGHER PRIORITY, MODERATE: `_elem_cpp` only qualifies a DIRECT exposed leaf, so a nested exposed leaf renders a bare unqualified name that the glue namespace can't resolve; fix = a recursive qualified container-render (re-render the container C++ type with exposed leaves namespace-qualified, a parallel to `to_cpp_stored` with an exposed-leaf hook). (1-ii) **an exposed CLASS as a tuple element** (`tuple[A, Counter]`) -- LOWER, HARD: a tuple's non-value element uses BORROW form (`std::tuple<A, const Counter*>`) but the per-element marshal builds STORAGE form -- the borrow/storage duality (needs the tuple storage->pointer conversion); tuple-of-ENUM/value works. (1-iii) **`@nocopy` exposed class as a container element** -- rejected (each element is copied; @nocopy forbids the copy) -- stays rejected permanently unless a move-in-place element path is designed. (1-iv) once the general Hashable bug (BUGS.md) is fixed, add a PRINCIPLED interop guard rejecting an exposed CLASS in a set-element/dict-key position (copy-on-cross has no stable identity for a hash key) -- today the general Hashable check incidentally covers it (safety-model W3). (1-v) test gap: `dict[Counter, V]` class-KEY rejection message untested (low value). Cross-module exposed element (class + enum) = located error (`_foreign_exposed_element` recurses into element types). Tests `tests/interop/container_exposed_elements/`, `tests/cases/interop/{warn_export_container_element_mutation,error_export_set_exposed_class_element,error_export_container_cross_module_element}`. Observation (BUGS.md): an exposed class defining `__hash__`+`__eq__` is still not recognized as Hashable, so it can't be a set element even in principle. **(1b) faithful exception DATA-FIELD crossing (exc TODO 1a)** -- DONE (branch `interop-exc-data-fields`): a data-carrying user exc's fields (scalar/str/bytes/exposed-enum) cross as INSTANCE ATTRIBUTES via a per-type generated setter (`extension.py` `_emit_user_exc_setters`) threaded through the `ExcRegistry` (now `typeid -> PyObject* + ExcSetErr`); the setter constructs `pytype(e.what())`, `PyObject_SetAttrString`s each field via `_value_out_expr`, then `PyErr_SetObject`. Message-only excs use the shared `exc_set_err_message_only` default. `str()`/`args` reflect the message only (acknowledged divergence; the C++ exc holds fields, not the original arg tuple). Container/exposed-class exc fields = located error (`_validate_user_exc_data_fields`), deferred. Tests `tests/interop/user_exc_data/`, `tests/cases/interop/{error_export_exc_container_field,error_export_exc_class_field}`. (2) **`Optional[container]`** params/returns (`list[int] | None`) -- not admitted (the boundary set has no Optional support yet; orthogonal). (3) **`tuple[T, ...]`** homogeneous/variadic tuple -- only fixed-arity `tuple[A, B, ...]` admitted; `_container_element_types` returns the fixed `TupleType.element_types`. (4) **`frozenset`** -- not a boundary type (only `set`); a `frozenset` ARG to a `set[T]` param IS accepted IN (`PyAnySet_Check` covers both) but there's no `frozenset[T]` TPy type to declare. (5) **`Array[T, N]` / `Span[T]` as containers** -- `Array` is a value type (fixed C++ `std::array`, not yet a boundary type); `Span` is the separate phase-3 buffer path. (6) **containers at the exposed-CLASS boundary** -- the METHOD half is DONE (the method-boundary rung): method/`__init__` params/returns are gated by `is_function_boundary_marshallable` + `is_span_boundary_param` (same set as @export functions; the method glue already shared `_emit_marshal_in`/`_emit_call_return`, so no codegen change), the copy-in mutation warning covers methods, and a borrow-form list/dict/set return warns (copy-out) with `Own[...]` acknowledged -- tests `tests/interop/class_method_containers/`, `tests/cases/interop/{warn_export_class_method_container_mutation,warn_export_class_container_borrow_return,error_export_class_method_span_return}`. STILL DEFERRED: a CONTAINER getset field. Scalar/str/bytes fields, an exposed-ENUM field (DONE, branch `interop-class-typed-fields`), and `Final`-constant snapshots use the base `is_boundary_marshallable` (scalar/str/bytes/@export-enum leaves; a class field is rejected for the aliasing reason, not marshallability), which does not recurse into containers, so a `list[int]` field stays rejected (an exposed class cannot STORE a container) -- the getset + constant-snapshot paths have no container marshaller; real per-field container marshal emission is its own follow-up. (7) **zero-copy** -- always copies; the read-only zero-copy path is `Span`+buffer (phase 3.5), and write-back has no v1 escape hatch (a copy-back-out-on-return option was considered and declined as out-of-rung). (8) test gaps (from /tpy-review): the `set`-OUT failing-element `to_py` null-cleanup branch (set_to_py/dict_to_py/tuple_to_py) is only exercised via the list path; an empty-`set` round-trip (`set_size(set())`/`to_set([])`) is untested; the dict-key-collapse coercion (`dict[int]` from `{True: ...}` -> `int` key) is declared but has no `ext_checks.py` assertion; a `frozenset` arg to a `set[T]` param is accepted (item 4) but untested and undocumented in the user-facing "strict-by-kind IN" note -- add a test + a doc line that a set kind includes `frozenset`. (9) the `is_boundary_marshallable`/`is_function_boundary_marshallable` split has no mechanical guard: `_validate_exposed_class` now uses the recursive predicate for method params/returns but the base one for FIELDS (by role, in one `check()`), and `_constant_exposable` stays base-only -- fold into a single `allow_containers=False` predicate when the field-getset work lands, or leave the split with this note. (10) the tuple-of-container mutation case (`tuple[list[int], str]` param, mutate the inner list) is copy-in-invisible like every container but is NOT the same as the list/dict/set warning: a tuple is a value type, so the inner list is already copied on element access in pure-TPy (the param is never `mutated`), so the warning correctly can't/shouldn't fire -- pre-existing TPy value-vs-reference model, documented in the container-cliff section, not a new divergence. (11) **borrow-form `bytes` returns are un-warned** -- `bytes` is a reference type, so a `-> bytes` @export fn/method return borrowing an existing object (`RefType[bytes]`) copies out at the boundary exactly like a borrow-form list, but the copy-out alias warning (added with the method-boundary rung) deliberately covers only list/dict/set to avoid churning existing-test warnings; widening it to `bytes` is a small follow-up (same `warn_if_borrow_return` predicate in `analyzer.py`).
- **[CPython interop] Span buffer boundary -- deferred slices.** `Span[readonly[T]]`/`Span[T]` (`T` a fixed-width int or `float`) cross the `@export` FUNCTION boundary as a PARAM ONLY (never a return -- return numeric data via `list[T]`), via the buffer protocol: `span_from_py<T>` (`marshal.hpp`) calls `PyObject_GetBuffer(PyBUF_ND | PyBUF_FORMAT)` (1-D, C-contiguous), strictly validates itemsize/format against `T` (no coercion), copies into a fresh `std::vector<T>` that implicitly converts to the function's `std::span<T>`/`std::span<const T>` param (the same owned-copy-converts-to-borrow-param trick as `str`/`bytes`), and releases the view. New predicate `is_span_boundary_param` in `type_def_registry.py` (param-only, checked at the `_validate_ext_module_exports` call site and the `assert_marshal` drift-guard in `extension.py` -- NOT folded into `is_function_boundary_marshallable`, which stays direction-symmetric for every other boundary type). Facade (`cpython_abi.hpp`/`cpython_h.hpp`) gained `Py_buffer` + `PyObject_GetBuffer`/`PyBuffer_Release` + `PyBUF_ND`/`PyBUF_FORMAT`, verified against real `Python.h` in the facade self-check. **v1.0 is copy-in for BOTH `Span[T]` and `Span[readonly[T]]`** (no `PyBUF_WRITABLE`, no write-back) -- a mutated `Span[T]` (non-readonly) param **warns** (the renamed `_warn_export_copy_boundary_mutation`, same `mutated_params` mechanism and no-escape-hatch bar as the list/dict/set container-mutation warning); `Span[readonly[T]]` can never warn (writing through it is already a compile error). Tests: `tests/interop/span_numeric/` (round-trips per width + float via `array.array`/`memoryview`/`bytes`/`bytearray`; `ext_checks.py` for format/itemsize mismatch, non-buffer arg, non-contiguous buffer, copy-in-mutation-invisible), `tests/cases/interop/{warn_export_span_mutation,error_export_span_return}`. **Deferred:** (1) **zero-copy** (both read-only and writable) -- phase 3.5, IR-gated (the foreign-borrow primitive; a spike showed the escape machinery can't fence a foreign-source param at all sinks). (2) **`bool`/`int` (BigInt)/`char` elements** -- excluded; `bool`'s buffer format (`'?'`) is inconsistent across exporters and rarely used as a numeric buffer, BigInt has no fixed-width buffer representation. (3) **`float32` elements** -- excluded because the scalar `float32` type itself isn't yet a boundary type at all (unrelated, orthogonal gap -- `Span[float32]` will "just work" once that scalar rung lands, since the admission predicate reuses `is_boundary_marshallable`). (4) **multi-dimensional / non-C-contiguous buffers** -- rejected (`PyBUF_ND` without `STRIDES` requires 1-D contiguity); no `ndim > 1` support. (5) **Span at the exposed-class METHOD boundary** -- DONE (the method-boundary rung; a `Span` method/`__init__` PARAM is admitted via `is_span_boundary_param`, return stays rejected, the mutation warning covers it); a Span getset FIELD is not a thing (a view field doesn't marshal; stays base-rejected). (6) **Span as a container element** (`list[Span[float]]`) -- not admitted, not a design goal. (7) **format-code table completeness** -- `span_from_py_impl`'s per-width accepted-code lists (e.g. int32 accepts `'i'` and `'l'`, int64 accepts `'q'` and `'l'`) cover the common numpy/`array.array` cases per-platform but are not an exhaustive `struct`-module mapping; revisit if an exotic exporter's format code is rejected in practice. **Post-/tpy-review (2026-07-01):** the buffer-view exception-safety leak (a `bad_alloc` during the copy skipped `PyBuffer_Release`) and the silent non-native-byte-order acceptance (a `'>i4'`-style buffer copied verbatim instead of rejected) were both found and FIXED in review (RAII guard + a native-byte-order check in `span_format_matches`); the transitive-mutation-warning gap (a `Span[T]` mutated only via a helper call gets no warning, unlike `list`/`dict`/`set`) was filed as a `BUGS.md` defect (needs `/tpy-fix-bug`, touches shared `mutation_propagation.py` infrastructure) rather than patched inline. Remaining cleanups from that review: (8) **`span_elem_type()` dedup** -- `is_span_boundary_param` (`type_def_registry.py`) and `_span_elem_cpp` (`extension.py`) both duplicate the "strip Own/Ref, assert Span, pull `type_args[0]`, unwrap readonly" sequence; extract one shared helper. (9) **widen `span_numeric` test coverage** -- DONE in part: added `peek_int32` (a mutable, non-readonly `Span[int32]` param that only reads), round-tripped in `driver.py` via `array.array`/`memoryview`, proving the mutable form marshals correctly and that a read-only *use* of it doesn't warn; mirrored with a `peek` case in `tests/cases/interop/warn_export_span_mutation` (declared-but-never-mutated `Span[int32]` stays quiet, unlike `scale`). STILL OPEN: only 4 of the 9 `span_from_py<T>` specializations (`float`/`int32`/`uint8`, now also exercised via `peek_int32`) get a happy-path test; the dual-format-code branches for the untested widths (`int8_t`/`int16_t`/`uint16_t`/`uint32_t`/`int64_t`/`uint64_t`, e.g. `int64_t` accepting `'l'` alongside `'q'`) remain unexercised. (10) **the native-byte-order rejection (review fix, item above) has no regression test** -- and, unlike the width/format-mismatch cases already in `ext_checks.py`, it can't be added cheaply: `array.array`/`memoryview.cast()` only ever expose a NATIVE format string (no stdlib-only way to construct a Py_buffer with an explicit non-native `<`/`>`/`!` prefix), so covering this branch needs either a numpy test-only dependency (the one common exporter that does emit explicit byte-order codes) or a from-scratch C++-level unit test calling `span_format_matches` directly (`runtime/cpp/tests/` currently has only the facade self-check, no general header-logic unit-test harness). Small infra/scope decision either way -- pick one before adding the test, don't assume it's a five-minute addition. Surfaced by the `/tpy-ready` retrospective for `interop-span-buffer`.
- **[CPython interop] exception bridge follow-ups (built-in types DONE).** Built-in TPy exceptions raised in an `@export` body now cross as the matching `PyExc_*` with the message (`tpy/interop/exc_bridge.hpp`; glue catches `const tpy::BaseException&`). Remaining, all tracked Planned in `docs/CPYTHON_INTEROP.md`: (1) **user-defined exception classes -- TYPE crossing DONE** (`PyErr_NewException` per ext_module-defined exc class at `PyInit_`, registered `typeid -> PyObject*` in an `ExcRegistry` the glue passes to `set_py_err_from`; own importable type, inheritance chain, catchable as base). Still deferred under this rung: (1a) **faithful data-field crossing -- DONE** (branch `interop-exc-data-fields`): a data-carrying user exc's fields (scalar/str/bytes/exposed-enum) cross as instance attributes via a per-type generated setter threaded through the `ExcRegistry` (`typeid -> PyObject* + ExcSetErr`; `extension.py::_emit_user_exc_setters`, `exc_bridge.hpp`); the setter constructs `pytype(e.what())`, sets each field via `PyObject_SetAttrString`, then `PyErr_SetObject`. `str()`/`args` reflect the message only (acknowledged, unavoidable -- the C++ exc holds typed fields, not the original arg tuple). Container/exposed-class exc fields = located error (the user-exc field validator (tpyc/interop/module_validators.py)), deferred. Full `args` fidelity (opt 1, needs `super().__init__` modeling) declined. The crossing is *transitive* (registry-driven, fires wherever raised) AND covers INHERITED user data fields (a subclass crosses its own + inherited fields via `TypeRegistry.user_declared_fields`, which skips native-base fields like `BaseException.message`; found+fixed in /tpy-review -- the first cut only marshalled own fields, a silent-drop divergence). The setter is `noexcept` + wrapped in try/catch degrading to `PyErr_NoMemory()` (a field marshaller can throw under OOM). Cross-module exposed-enum exc field = located error (routes through `_exposed_form_error` for the locality check). Two DEFERRED follow-ups filed from /tpy-review: (1a-i) **admit VALUE-TYPE exposed-class exc fields** -- the getset path admits an immutable value-type exposed-class field, but exc fields reject ALL exposed-class fields; admitting them reuses `_value_out_expr`'s `instance_to_py` arm (now safe under the setter's try/catch, since `instance_to_py` can throw) + needs a test; (1a-ii) **dedup the "is user exception" predicate** (`not is_native and implements_throwable and inherits_base_exception`) -- now spelled at 4 sites (`compiler.py`, `analyzer.py`, `registration.py`, `extension.py`); fold into a `RecordInfo.is_user_exception()` / registry helper. AND (higher value, /tpy-ready 2nd-opinion): the load-bearing drift is admission-vs-EMIT, not validator-vs-validator -- the user-exc field validator (tpyc/interop/module_validators.py) admits `is_boundary_marshallable(_, False) and not is_exposed_class`, but the setter EMIT is in `extension.py::_emit_user_exc_setters`; widening the shared marshallable predicate would auto-admit a type the setter cannot emit -> broken glue TU. Co-locate the "admissible exc-field type" predicate WITH the emit so admission+emit cannot drift (the exposed-class exc-field reject is already test-pinned by `error_export_exc_class_field`). Tests +`tests/interop/user_exc_inherited/` (hierarchy + transitive raise), +`tests/cases/interop/error_export_exc_cross_module_enum_field`; (1b) **the `str()`/`args` divergence is documented, not warned** -- a per-raise warning was shipped then REMOVED in /tpy-review: it was non-actionable (unavoidable under TPy's model, no escape hatch, no author-side fix -- making the exc message-only would drop the very fields, worse) and landed on the TPy author, not the Python consumer who reads `e.args`; so it is a doc-only divergence like the other no-escape-hatch ones (`_warn_export_user_exc_data` and its `warn_export_user_exc_data` test were deleted). (1c) **cross-module user exceptions** -- only classes DEFINED in the ext_module get a Python type; an imported user exc raised at the boundary still degrades to its built-in base (a data-field exc field typed as a cross-module enum is already a located error; the raise-through-an-imported-exc case is the remaining gap). (1f) **test gaps** -- bare user exc (no `__init__`), `py_exc_by_name` unknown-built-in-base fallback (e.g. inheriting `CancelledError` -> `PyExc_Exception`), and the `PyInit_` module-init (top-level) raise path are unexercised. (2) **`@error_return` Err -> raise** across the boundary. (3) **panic -> exception** (convert `tpy_panic` to a Python exception instead of `abort()`ing the host). (4) **exception chaining** (`__cause__`/`__context__`) not carried. (5) **`CancelledError` (and other `async.hpp` `BaseException` subclasses) degrade to `PyExc_BaseException`** -- no `PyExc_CancelledError` stable-ABI singleton exists (asyncio.CancelledError is Python-level), so bridging it needs importing `asyncio.CancelledError` at `PyInit` and stashing the type; deferred. (6) **test gaps**: the `PyInit_` (module-init raise) catch path needs a dedicated expected-import-failure interop case; broaden the cascade test with user-raised `RuntimeError`/`OverflowError`/bare `LookupError` (the latter exercises degrade-to-listed-base). (7) optional: extend the facade self-check to validate the new `PyExc_*` decls. (8) **low-prio perf:** `py_exc_for` is a linear `dynamic_cast` cascade (O(depth) RTTI probes). Fine -- it's a cold path (runs only when an exception crosses the boundary) -- but if ever revisited, the clean form is a virtual kind-tag on the `Throwable`/`BaseException` hierarchy switched on in the interop header (one vcall, keeps the Python C-API out of `core.hpp`), best bundled with the user-exc-class rung since that adds per-type metadata anyway. Not a faster cascade.
- **[CPython interop] exposed classes (`PyType_FromSpec`) -- deferred slices.** The baseline rung ships: `@export class` -> a CPython type built at `PyInit_`, instances embedding the TPy payload after the `PyObject` header (`tpy::interop::Instance<T>`, `class_bridge.hpp`); `tp_init` runs `__init__`, `tp_dealloc` runs the C++ destructor; plain instance methods + annotated fields as read/write getset; instances cross as free-fn/method params (a borrow of the live payload via `instance_payload` -- mutation writes through) and returns (a `self`/param-sourced borrow return crosses as the ORIGINAL PyObject -- see the identity-preserving-returns entry above; other sources copy via `instance_to_py` and warn; `Own[Cls]` is the always-fresh form). The type is final (no `Py_TPFLAGS_BASETYPE`), no instance `__dict__`. The ext-module validator (`_validate_exposed_class` in `tpyc/interop/module_validators.py`) rejects, with a located error, what the glue can't emit yet -- this is the deferred matrix: **(1) dunders** (Q4) -- **checkpoint 1 DONE** (`__repr__`/`__str__` -> `Py_tp_repr`/`Py_tp_str`; `__eq__`/`__ne__`/`__lt__`/`__le__`/`__gt__`/`__ge__` -> one `Py_tp_richcompare`, `__ne__` auto-derived from `__eq__`; `__hash__` -> `Py_tp_hash`, `PyObject_HashNotImplemented` wired when a richcompare dunder is defined without `__hash__`; new `_validate_export_class_dunders` in `analyzer.py` mirrors `_validate_dyn_dunder_kind`'s decorator/kind rejections plus per-dunder param-count/type/return-type checks; fixed a real pre-existing gap surfaced by the first class-typed non-self method param: `_boundary_inner` didn't strip `ReadonlyType`, so `def __eq__(self, other: Vec2)` -- whose `other` arrives as `readonly[Vec2]` -- failed `is_function_boundary_marshallable`/`is_exposed_class` even though `Vec2` is exposed; tests `tests/interop/class_dunders/`, `tests/cases/interop/error_export_class_dunder_{return,arity,staticmethod}`, `warn_export_class_dunder` repointed to `__call__`). **checkpoint 2 DONE** (arithmetic/ordering operators -> `Py_nb_*`: binary ops -- `__add__`/`__sub__`/`__mul__`/`__truediv__`/`__floordiv__`/`__mod__`/`__pow__`/`__lshift__`/`__rshift__`/`__and__`/`__or__`/`__xor__` -- each wire ONE wrapper handling both the forward dunder and its reflected counterpart if defined, since CPython invokes the same slot with `(a, b)` regardless of which side is `self`; the non-self operand marshals as whatever type the dunder declares -- another `@export` class OR a scalar/enum (e.g. `def __mul__(self, scalar: int64)` for `vec * 3`), NOT restricted to the record's own type -- and a type mismatch downgrades to `NotImplemented` via a new `catch (const MarshalError&) { if (!PyErr_ExceptionMatches(TypeError)) return nullptr; PyErr_Clear(); }` pattern (a real error, e.g. `OverflowError` from a right-typed-but-bad-value operand, still propagates); `__pow__`/`__rpow__` use the ternary `nb_power` signature and reject a real 3-arg modulus; unary ops (`__pos__`/`__neg__`/`__invert__`) reuse the repr/str shape; in-place ops (`__iadd__`... the `CONST_PARAMS_METHODS` set) mutate self and return the SAME PyObject (`Py_IncRef`+return, no `instance_to_py` copy) since TPy already requires them to return `self` -- the borrow-return-copies warning is suppressed for this group specifically since identity IS preserved here (unlike every other dunder). New facade: `Py_nb_*` slot ids (25 constants) + `unaryfunc`/`binaryfunc`/`ternaryfunc` typedefs (`cpython_abi.hpp`, self-check-verified) + `PyErr_ExceptionMatches`/`PyErr_Clear` (`cpython_h.hpp`). Dunder-name tables (`_NB_BINARY_OPS`/`_NB_UNARY_OPS`/`_NB_INPLACE_OPS` in `extension.py`) are derived from the canonical `BINOP_TO_METHOD`/`BINOP_TO_RMETHOD`/`AUGOP_TO_IMETHOD`/`UNARYOP_TO_METHOD` tables (`modules/defs.py`), not a hand-rolled duplicate. Tests: `tests/interop/class_operators/` (same-type `__add__`, scalar-mixed `__mul__`/`__rmul__`, unary `__neg__`, in-place `__iadd__` with an identity check, ternary `__pow__`), `tests/cases/interop/error_export_class_dunder_arith_{arity,return}`. Verified end-to-end via a manual `.so` build+driver (forward/reflected/unary/inplace/wrong-type-TypeError/3-arg-pow-TypeError all matched). **checkpoint 3 DONE (Q4 fully landed)** (container protocol -> `Py_mp_*`/`Py_sq_*`/`Py_tp_iter*`: `__len__` wires ONE wrapper to both `Py_mp_length` and `Py_sq_length`; `__getitem__` -> `Py_mp_subscript` (a wrong-typed key's `TypeError` propagates directly -- no `NotImplemented` fallback, unlike arithmetic operators, since subscripting has no reflected side; slicing, `__getitem__(self, s: slice)`, is out of scope); `__setitem__`/`__delitem__` share ONE `Py_mp_ass_subscript` wrapper (`value == nullptr` means `del obj[k]`; if only one of the pair is defined, the other direction raises `TypeError`); `__contains__` -> `Py_sq_contains` (omitted entirely when undefined -- `in` then falls back to CPython's own iterate-via-`tp_iter` behavior for free); `__iter__` -> `Py_tp_iter` (reuses the checkpoint-2 unary-op emitter directly -- no self-identity special-casing needed: `__iter__` may legitimately return a fresh iterator object, not `self`, so it's marshalled like any other exposed-class-returning dunder, with the usual borrow-vs-`Own` warning); `__next__` -> `Py_tp_iternext` -- `__next__` is implicitly `@error_return(StopIteration)` (the parser default: `parse/parser.py`'s `if node.name == "__next__" and error_return is None: error_return = "StopIteration"`), so the compiled method returns `std::expected<T, StopIteration>` rather than throwing on exhaustion; the wrapper checks `.has_value()` and calls `set_py_err_from` on the `.error()` value directly (`StopIteration` is already in the exception bridge's built-in list, so no new bridging code needed) -- exempted from the blanket `@error_return` rejection the other dunders get. `list(x)`, `iter(x)`/`next(it)`, and a `for` loop all round-trip through CPython's own sequence/iterator machinery once these are wired -- verified end-to-end via a manual `.so` build+driver. New facade: `Py_mp_*`/`Py_sq_*`/`Py_tp_iter*` slot ids + `lenfunc`/`objobjargproc`/`objobjproc` typedefs (reuses `binaryfunc`/`unaryfunc` from checkpoint 2 for `mp_subscript`/`tp_iter`/`tp_iternext`), self-check-verified. Tests: `tests/interop/class_container/` (len/getitem/setitem-mutation/contains/iter+next via `list()`+manual+for-loop), `tests/cases/interop/error_export_class_dunder_{getitem_arity,setitem_arity,len_return}`. Never in scope for Q4 at all: `__call__`, `__bool__`, async iteration (`__aiter__`/`__anext__`), context managers (`__enter__`/`__exit__`), descriptors (`__get__`/`__set__`), and pickling (`__reduce__`) -- file separately if ever wanted. **Post-/tpy-review fixes (same session):** one Critical found and fixed, one Critical claim DISPROVEN by direct testing -- (a) [DISPROVEN] the review flagged `Py_tp_hash` being omitted whenever ANY richcompare dunder is defined without `__hash__` (not just `__eq__`) as a silent divergence from real Python's `__eq__`-specific unhashable-on-override rule. Building and running an actual `.so` showed this ISN'T a bug: `PyType_Ready` (the mechanism behind `PyType_FromSpec`, used for every exposed class) nulls `tp_hash` whenever `tp_richcompare` is populated AT ALL, with no way to tell which specific dunder populated it -- verified by removing the explicit `PyObject_HashNotImplemented` wiring entirely and confirming the type stayed unhashable regardless (a plain-`__len__`/no-richcompare class stays hashable, confirming richcompare-presence, not the explicit wiring, is what triggers it). So a `__lt__`-only class DOES become unhashable once exposed, unlike its plain-Python source (which stays hashable) -- this is a genuine, unavoidable, now-DOCUMENTED acknowledged divergence (comment in `extension.py`, `Ordered` class + `ext_checks.py` assertion in `tests/interop/class_dunders/`), not something fixable in TPy's glue. (b) [FIXED, confirmed real] richcompare codegen hardcoded the "other" operand's C++ type as the record's own type regardless of what the compare dunder actually declared, so a legal-per-sema `def __eq__(self, other: int64)` passed comp but failed the `.so` build with a confusing internal g++ error; fixed by requiring a compare dunder's operand type equal the record's own type at sema (`_validate_export_class_dunders`), +`error_export_class_dunder_compare_wrong_type`. **Known limitation from this fix (documented in `docs/CPYTHON_INTEROP.md`/`LANGUAGE_FEATURES.md`, not yet filed as a TODO before now):** unlike arithmetic operators (checkpoint 2), a comparison dunder can only compare against the record's OWN exposed-class type -- `__eq__(self, other: int64)` or `__eq__(self, other: SomeOtherExposedClass)` are both rejected at sema, even though sema's `is_function_boundary_marshallable` check would otherwise admit them. Lifting this needs richcompare codegen to marshal per-op-declared-type with a `NotImplemented`-on-mismatch fallback (mirroring `_value_in_decl_expr`'s already-built arithmetic-operator pattern) instead of the current single type-guard-then-switch shape shared by all 6 ops -- a real codegen redesign, not a quick follow-up.
