Also added from the review: `__delitem__`-actually-implemented coverage (`Slot` class in `tests/interop/class_container/`), an `OverflowError`-propagates-not-swallowed-by-NotImplemented test and an asymmetric `__sub__`/`__rsub__` pair (operand order matters, unlike the previously-only-tested commutative `__mul__`/`__rmul__`) in `tests/interop/class_operators/`, and `error_export_class_dunder_{contains_return,iter_return}` cases. **Post-/tpy-ready fixes (same session, second-opinion agent caught this before merge):** `compiler.py`'s per-method loop unconditionally skips all non-`__init__` dunders, so its `type_params`/overload/param-form rejections never ran against ANY dunder -- confirmed as a LIVE gap (not just theoretical) by direct reproduction: a generic dunder (`def __len__[T](self) -> int32:`) and a defaulted dunder param (`def __eq__(self, other: C = None)`) both passed comp-phase cleanly then failed the actual `.so` build with confusing internal g++ errors (`no matching function for call to ... __len__() const` / `could not convert 'nullptr' to 'const C&'`) -- the exact failure shape already fixed once for richcompare in this same round. Fixed: `analyzer.py::_validate_export_class_dunders` gained a `type_params` check and a new dunder param-form helper (since resolved: both homes now live in `interop/export_shape.py` and share their message tails, split as `unsupported_wrapper_param_form` vs `unsupported_slot_param_form` because the two emit shapes genuinely admit different forms). Tests: `error_export_class_dunder_{generic,default_param}`. The `@overload`-grouped-dunder case the second-opinion agent also flagged was checked and found to be ALREADY correctly rejected (the existing `is_overload_stub` check fires on the first stub before the impl is ever reached) -- not a live gap, no fix needed there.

**@export class single-value marshal duplication:** `extension.py`'s `_value_in_decl_expr` (operand/key/setter decode) and `_value_out_expr` (getset getter + exc data fields; dunder RETURNS now route through `_emit_call_return`) duplicate `_emit_marshal_in`/`_emit_call_return`'s (statement-form) branch structure -- two marshalling dispatch chains to keep in lockstep when a boundary type is added. Same-family: the `-1`-sentinel BaseException/catch-all block is hand-inlined three times (tp_init, field setter, property setter -- the field variant lacks the BaseException arm); a tiny shared `-1`-catch emitter would collapse it. (low confidence) `_value_in_decl_expr` always binds a `const&` for an exposed-class non-self operand regardless of Phase-2 mutation analysis; a dunder that legitimately mutates a non-self operand would hit a const-mismatch build failure rather than a clear diagnostic -- not confirmed against a concrete case. **(2) inheritance -- DONE** (branch `interop-class-inheritance`: single exposed same-module base -> real `tp_base` via `PyType_FromSpecWithBases`; see the dedicated deferred-slices entry); **(3) `@property` -- DONE** (branch `interop-class-properties`): a property crosses as a *computed* getset -- the getter is a zero-arg method return site (reuses `_emit_call_return`, so it admits the full method boundary set incl. containers), the setter a one-param method param site (reuses `_emit_marshal_in` via an `a0` alias; a non-value setter param is Own-auto-wrapped, so the marshalled owned local is `std::move`d in). Getter-only property = `nullptr` setter (`AttributeError` on write, as CPython -- message text differs). Shape checks route through `export_method_shape_error(allow_property=True)` (async/generator/generic/`@error_return` accessors still reject); a setter typed as an exposed class -- value-type OR reference (the property Own auto-wrap runs before a user record's ValueType flag is known, so both arrive Own-wrapped) -- is a dedicated located error steering to a plain method; a `Span[T]` setter is a located error (a setter stores, and the buffer copy-in dies at the call -- store `list[T]`); `del` on any property or field raises `AttributeError` via a `value == nullptr` guard in both setter emits (CPython's getset delete protocol; previously segfaulted); `_`-prefixed properties are internal (uniform `_`-attribute rule, borrow-return warn loop included); a borrow-return getter warns via the existing `_warn_export_class_return_alias` (labeled `property 'x'`, const-clone deduped). Tests `tests/interop/class_properties/`, `tests/cases/interop/{error_export_class_property_class_setter,error_export_class_property_value_class_setter,error_export_class_property_span_setter,error_export_class_property_setter_unmarshallable,error_export_class_property_error_return,error_export_class_property_unmarshallable,warn_export_class_property_borrow_return}`. Deferred follow-ups: (3a) **enable value-type exposed-class property setters** -- rejected today only because `_apply_property_setter_wrapping` (sema/method_expansion.py) runs before the protocol pass sets a user record's ValueType flag, so the param is Own-wrapped and the borrowed argument payload can't feed it; fix = defer/reorder the wrap decision (plain-TPy-wide, own design pass) or copy-emit at the boundary for a value-class `Own` setter; (3b) property accessors skip `unsupported_wrapper_param_form` (a defaulted setter value param passes unvalidated -- harmless today, the getset protocol always supplies the value; add for uniformity with the method path); (3c) test gap: no runtime (ext-exec) witness of an exposed-class-VALUED getter (`-> Own[Inner]` copy-out read; the borrow-form warn case is comp-only) -- needs a second exposed class in an interop case. The warning-dropped-on-error residual is now its own BUGS.md entry; **(4) class-typed fields** -- the ENUM half is DONE (branch `interop-class-typed-fields`: an exposed-enum getset field round-trips value-correctly, singleton-preserving -- see the enums entry item 2c). The CLASS half is now split by the borrow-view gate (branch interop-field-borrow-views): a NEVER-REASSIGNED public reference-class field crosses as a READ-ONLY aliasing borrow-view getset (write-through, registry-deduped identity), while a REASSIGNABLE one stays a located error (a view aliases the storage slot, so the rebind would show through it); the diagnostic steers to dropping the post-__init__ reassignment or making the field **internal** (a `_`-prefixed name -- see the internal-fields entry below -- kept as payload state, never a Python attribute) plus an accessor method (mutating through `self`) or an explicit `copy()`. A *public* `@nocopy` or cross-module exposed-class field stays rejected for the usual reasons (internal fields have no interop gate, so a `_`-named `@nocopy` member is fine). **Internal (`_`-prefixed) fields DONE** (branch `interop-internal-fields`): a field whose name begins with `_` never crosses as an attribute at EITHER site (exposed-class getset via the `extension.py` getset loop + `_validate_exposed_class`; exception data-fields via `_collect_user_exc_classes` + `_validate_user_exc_data_fields`), gated by one shared predicate `type_def_registry.is_internal_boundary_field`. It stays live payload state, so an exposed class can now hold ANY-typed internal member (reference class, container, `@nocopy`) reached through a method -- the pattern the reference-class-field diagnostic already recommended, now actually reachable. Divergence (acknowledged, like `e.message`): a `_`-field is an ordinary attribute under plain Python but absent on the `.so`, so drivers must not read one. Test `tests/interop/internal_fields/`; migrated `class_container`'s `_i` cursor (its pointless mutable getset drops). FILED-NOT-BUILT: replace the C++ `nothrow_move` static_assert on the payload with a located sema pre-check for a non-movable exposed payload (a `_`-field can now make a class non-movable, hitting the assert as a raw build error rather than a diagnostic). **(4a) exposed VALUE-TYPE fields -- DONE** (branch `interop-class-typed-fields`): a field typed as an @export `ValueType` record (`origin: Point`) is admitted -- value types are immutable, so copy-out is behaviorally invisible (the same safe bucket as enum, not the reference-class footgun). Two parts landed: (i) an exposed value-type class emits READ-ONLY getset (getter only, `nullptr` setter -- gated on `info.is_value_type` in `extension.py`; also fixed the pre-existing r/w-mutable fidelity gap that was filed in BUGS.md, now removed); (ii) the field reject narrowed to `is_exposed_class(typ) and not _boundary_inner(typ).is_value_type()`, so a value-type field falls through to admission -- getter copy-out via `instance_to_py`, the OUTER holder's field-set stays r/w (whole-value replacement). CPython parity: chose read-only `.so` + ext-only divergences (mutation-raises-AttributeError and copy-out `is`-identity in `ext_checks.py`, driver stays parity-clean) over freezing the `lib/cpy` `ValueType` stub -- no `no_cpython.txt` needed, consistent with the shipped strict-by-type/final/no-`__dict__` pattern. Equality gate resolved: value types have NO implicit structural `==` (it's a compile error without a defined `__eq__`), and a user-defined `__eq__` is already wired by the Q4 richcompare rung. Test `tests/interop/value_typed_fields/`. char fields (no marshaller) and tuple fields (value type, but the getset has no container/tuple emit -- pairs with the container-getset-field work) remain separate small gaps; **(5) static/classmethods**; **(6) generic exposed classes / generic methods**; **(7) faithful exception data-field crossing (exc TODO 1a)** -- DONE (branch `interop-exc-data-fields`); reused the getset single-value marshal helper (`_value_out_expr`) for each exc data field, not an exception-only path; container/exposed-class exc fields deferred (located error); **(8) `copy.copy`/`pickle`** (a C type with no `__reduce__`/`tp_copy` fails both where the source class succeeds -- track as a declared divergence); **(9) overloaded methods / `__init__`** (now *rejected* -- the glue emits one positional wrapper, so an `@overload` group would silently expose only the first arity; supporting it needs per-arity dispatch in the wrapper); **(10) `tp_traverse`/GC** -- not emitted (fields are scalar/str/bytes/enum or a nested value-type class, all held by value with no `PyObject` reference, so no reference cycle is possible -- an enum field holds an interned int, a value-type field an inline immutable value, not a Python ref). NOT triggered by the enum-field work, and NOT by the borrow-view rung either: a view holds exactly one strong ref (its owner) while no exposed instance references a view, so the graph stays acyclic by construction and refcounting suffices; tp_traverse becomes relevant only if exposed instances ever hold arbitrary PyObject refs (e.g. Python-side subclass attributes, currently rejected at instantiation); **(11) `Py_TPFLAGS_BASETYPE`** -- a LEAF exposed type stays non-subclassable from Python (honest `TypeError` at the class statement); a class that is another exposed class's base carries BASETYPE (required by `PyType_FromSpecWithBases`) with a tp_init exact-type guard rejecting Python-subclass instantiation, and the `PyType_IsSubtype` branch in `instance_payload` is now LIVE (a base-typed param accepts a derived instance); **(12) throwing re-`__init__`** leaves the instance with a destroyed payload reachable via getset (UB if then touched) -- exotic (catch an `obj.__init__()` failure, then read a field) and CPython is also ill-defined there; revisit if it bites. Code organization: DONE -- the glue emitter is now `tpyc/interop/extension.py` (`ExtensionGenerator`, wired as `CodeGenerator.extension`; `generate_extension_glue` is a thin delegator), and `boundary_cpp_type`/`boundary_unmarshallable_msg` moved to `type_def_registry.py` (next to `is_boundary_marshallable`), so both the sema validator and the glue import them from one neutral home. Byte-identical codegen. Full design in `docs/CPYTHON_INTEROP.md` phase 4. **Review follow-ups (from /tpy-review):** DONE in round 2 -- non-`__init__` dunders now *warn* (`_warn_export_class_unexposed_dunders`); `Own[<exposed class>]` params, `@nocopy` exposed-class borrow-returns, and class-typed fields are now *located errors* (`Compiler._exposed_form_error`, renamed from `_exposed_class_form_error` when it gained the enum cases) instead of opaque C++ failures (the `@nocopy` borrow-return suppresses the duplicate identity warning). Round-3 (ready gate): `@overload` method/`__init__` groups now reject (item 9) -- the silent-first-arity drop the rest of the branch was eliminating. (A plain *duplicate* `def __init__` was already rejected upstream; the new check covers the `@overload` group case codegen's `[0]` would otherwise truncate.) STILL OPEN: (a) keyword arguments -- DONE (positional/keyword, defaults, keyword-only and positional-only all cross). (e) cross-module exposed classes have no same-defining-module guard -- DONE (branch `fix-cross-module-exposed-class`): `Compiler._exposed_form_error`'s class branch now checks the class is locally `@export`-defined in the current module (mirrors the pre-existing enum-branch guard), resolved via `registry.imported_record_qualification_for_type` (qualified identity, not a bare short-name set -- a name-collision variant of this exact check was caught live by `/tpy-review`'s `cpython-parity`/`architecture-fit` passes and fixed before merge), so a foreign exposed class used as a param/field/return is a located error instead of a misbuild; tests `tests/cases/interop/error_export_class_cross_module_{param,return,name_collision}`. **Cleanups:** rename `type_def_registry._boundary_inner` -> `boundary_inner` (now a cross-module API); dedupe the dunder-exclusion predicate spelled at 3 sites (compiler/generator/analyzer); unify `is_exposed_class` (`td.record.exposed_to_host`) and `is_boundary_marshallable` (`td.boundary_marshal`) onto one canonical check (the `boundary_cpp_type`/`boundary_unmarshallable_msg` relocation is DONE -- now in `type_def_registry.py`). **Test gaps:** round 2 added `error_*` cases for the Own-param / class-typed-field / @nocopy-borrow-return rejects + a `warn_export_class_dunder` case; still missing `error_*` for the remaining `_validate_exposed_class` reject paths (throwable/generic/static/async; the inheritance rejects got their own cases on the `interop-class-inheritance` branch) + the `@export`-outside-`ext_module` ParseError + `@export("renamed") class`, and a happy-path for multiple exposed classes in one module or an empty class (no fields/no non-init methods).
- **[CPython interop] enums + constants boundary -- deferred slices.** An `@export` enum in an ext_module is recreated at `PyInit_` as a **real** CPython enum (`enum.IntEnum`/`enum.Enum` via the stdlib functional API with `module=` set; `runtime/cpp/include/tpy/interop/enum_bridge.hpp` `make_enum`/`enum_dict_add`) -- CPython-parity-verified observably identical to a source-level class-statement enum. Module-level `Final` constants of a boundary scalar (`int`/`IntN`/`bool`/`float`/`str`) become init-time module-attribute snapshots (read after `__tpy_init`; Final => immutable so the snapshot can't go stale). Enums are `@export`-gated (consistent with classes/functions; the enum parser accepts bare `@export` in an ext_module); constants are auto-exposed via `Final` (no decorator syntax exists for a binding, and Final is the only snapshot-safe global form). Validator (`_validate_exposed_enums` in `tpyc/interop/module_validators.py`) rejects `@export` on a `@native` enum or a nested enum; the glue collectors `ExtensionGenerator._exposed_enums`/`_exposed_constants` filter the exposable surface. Facade += `PyImport_ImportModule`/`PyObject_GetAttrString`/`PyObject_Call`/`Py_BuildValue`/`PyDict_New`/`PyDict_SetItemString`; `marshal.hpp` += `to_py(std::string_view)` (a `Final[str]` resolves to `StrView`). Tests: `tests/interop/{enums,constants}/`, `tests/cases/interop/error_export_{enum_outside_ext,native_enum,nested_enum}`. Deferred: (1) **enum *values* as `@export` function param/return types** -- DONE (branch interop-enum-values): an exposed enum crosses as a fn param/return via `enum_bridge.hpp` `enum_from_py`/`enum_to_py` against the module-static enum-type handle (promoted from a PyInit-local). OUT reconstructs the member (`EnumType(value)`, identity preserved); IN is strict-by-type (bare int -> TypeError; documented int-vs-member-vs-source divergence, ext_checks-tested). Admission = `boundary_marshal` on the exposed enum's TypeDef (sema registration) + `is_exposed_enum`. `int(enum)` inside a body is still unsupported (orthogonal TPy conversion gap, not the boundary). (2) **nested enums** (inside a class) and **cross-module enums** -- nested still rejected; a cross-module exposed-enum param/return is a located error (`_exposed_form_error`, checks the enum is locally @export-defined) rather than a misbuild -- the exposed-CLASS cross-module path now has the same guard too (DONE, branch `fix-cross-module-exposed-class`; see the exposed-classes entry's item (e)). From /tpy-review (treat as ONE deferred cross-module unit, all low-reachability today): (2a) the cross-module guard branch was UNTESTED -- DONE (branch `fix-cross-module-exposed-class`): a 2-file `src/main.py` + `src/enum_mod.py` fixture under `tests/cases/interop/` works fine (the "single-source-per-case" limit only applies to the `tests/interop/` ext-exec harness, not the plain comp-phase `tests/cases/` one); see `error_export_enum_cross_module` (and the class analog `error_export_class_cross_module_{param,return}`). (2b) DONE for both classes and enums: the class guard resolves by qualified identity (`registry.imported_record_qualification_for_type`, the same type-object-based "is this local?" helper codegen already uses to qualify a cross-module record) instead of a bare short-name set -- a module that imports a foreign exposed class under an alias while also defining its own same-named local one no longer defeats the guard; regression test `error_export_class_cross_module_name_collision`. The ENUM guard was similarly hardened (reads `EnumInfo.module_name` off the resolved type object rather than `registry.imported_enum_qualification`'s name-keyed lookup) and the underlying general enum name-resolution bug that initially blocked verifying it (an aliased cross-module enum import getting confused with a same-canonical-name LOCAL enum, no `@export` needed to reproduce) is now fixed too (branch `fix-enum-alias-collision`: `parse/type_resolver.py`'s enum branch now mints a qualified `NominalType` from the import tuple instead of trusting a bare-name registry lookup, mirroring the pre-existing record branch; `codegen_cpp/generator.py`'s `native_cpp_names` population gained the qname-keyed entry records already had plus a local-shadow guard on the bare-name compensating write). Regression tests `tests/cases/enum/enum_alias_local_collision` (general) and `error_export_enum_cross_module_name_collision` (interop). (2c) **enum getset field on an exposed class** -- DONE (branch `interop-class-typed-fields`): a locally-defined exposed enum is a valid read/write getset field; the getter/setter reuse the same single-value marshal helpers (`_value_out_expr`/`_value_in_decl_expr`) the operator dunders use, so the field round-trips `enum_to_py`/`enum_from_py` against the module enum handle (member singleton preserved, strict-by-type set). A cross-module exposed-enum field stays a located error (the same cross-module guard, now covering the field role -- retargeted `error_export_class_enum_field`). Tests: `tests/interop/enum_typed_fields/`. (2d) `is_exposed_enum` reads `td.boundary_marshal` as an exposed proxy rather than a first-class `EnumInfo.exposed_to_host`; correct today (boundary_marshal set only when exposed) -- fold into the existing "unify is_exposed_class / is_boundary_marshallable onto one canonical check" cleanup, don't add the field standalone. (2e) DONE: asymmetric enum signatures (enum-IN-only `is_red(c: Color) -> bool`, enum-OUT-only `default_color() -> Color`) now exercise each marshal side independently in tests/interop/enum_values. (3) **`bytes`/`BytesView` and `char`/`tuple` constants** -- a `Final[bytes]` resolves to a view with no `to_py(span)` overload, and `char`/`tuple` aren't boundary types; all are silently left unexposed (like a non-`@export` function), documented in `docs/CPYTHON_INTEROP.md`. A `bytes` constant would need either `to_py(BytesView/span)` or forcing the owned form. (4) **the auto-exposed-`Final` surface is implicit** -- there is no per-constant opt-in marker (unlike `@export` on enums/funcs/classes); a user intending to export a `Final[tuple]` gets silent non-export. Acceptable as the opt-in-parallel framing (only boundary-typed Finals form the surface), but if it bites, a future explicit constant-export spelling (or a warning on a skipped non-boundary `Final`) is the escape hatch. (5) **`_exposed_constants` re-resolves the Final type** via `resolve_stmt_type_cascade` (the generator's `seen_globals`/compiler's `ModuleVarInfo` already hold it) -- a small "consumer re-derives the fact" smell; fold onto a shared resolved-globals source when one is threaded to the glue. (6) **test gaps** (from /tpy-ready retrospective): an unannotated `X: Final = 5` constant (may carry an unresolved int-literal type that fails `_constant_exposable` where the annotated `Final[int]` form passes -- the item-5 materialized-type fix would also erase this) and an `auto()`-valued `@export` enum (the parser materializes `auto()` to concrete values at parse time, so the path is correct but untested) are both unexercised.
- **[CPython interop] str/bytes boundary -- deferred slices.** The str/bytes rung ships only the owned, immutable value forms by copy. Excluded, by design: (1) **`StrView`/`BytesView` (zero-copy view input)** -- a view param would borrow into the live PyObject for the call's duration; making that escape-sound for a *foreign* source is the phase-3.5 foreign-borrow primitive (IR-gated). Currently rejected with the standard "not marshallable" diagnostic; `str`/`bytes` (copy) are the workaround. (2) **`bytearray` (mutable buffer)** -- shares `bytes`' C++ representation (`std::vector<uint8_t>`) but is a reference type; marshalling it by copy as a `PyBytes` would silently drop the aliasing a CPython caller expects, so it is rejected (admission judges the `Own`-unwrapped inner type's `is_value_type`, so `bytearray` and `Own[bytearray]` both reject). Could later be supported as an explicit copy with a documented "no aliasing" note, or mapped to a real `PyByteArray` if a mutable round-trip is wanted. (3) **`str.upper()`/concat etc. produce fresh owned strings** -- fine today; no action. All three are in `docs/CPYTHON_INTEROP.md`.
- **[CPython interop] PIC stdlib `.o` cache for ext-exec builds.** The exec phase reuses a shared precompiled stdlib `.o` set, but the ext-exec `.so` build is `-fPIC` so those objects don't apply -- `tpyc -b` recompiles the runtime + imported stdlib fresh on every cache-miss build (correct, just slower; ccache warms most of it). If interop build time grows, add a PIC-`.o` stdlib cache variant (or build the `.so` from the non-PIC set where the linker permits) so ext-exec re-verifies as cheaply as exec. Deferred until interop case count or build time justifies it.
- **[CPython interop] `error_`-style interop cases.** The ext-exec harness snapshots front-end diagnostics (`expected/diag.txt`) but still fails hard on a nonzero tpyc exit, so a compile-error ext module cannot be a case (the main harness's `error_` convention: expected-to-fail source with the error pinned in `diag.txt`). Add when a rejection is worth pinning at the interop level; comp-phase rejections live in `tests/cases/interop` today.
- **[CPython interop] auto-emit `__text_signature__` into the exposed-class docstring.** CPython parses a leading `Name(sig)\n--\n\n` out of a type's `tp_doc` into `__text_signature__`, so `help(Cls)` renders a real constructor signature line (this is how `help(dict)` shows `dict(mapping)`). TPy knows `__init__`'s signature statically, so the glue could synthesize that prefix into the emitted `Py_tp_doc` -- **zero runtime cost** (it is a string already being emitted) and strictly better `help()` output than the plain Python source gives. It also gives the dunder-docstring exclusion a positive story: the constructor's documentation lands somewhere useful instead of merely being warned about. Verified the bare `(x)` form parses and populates `__text_signature__` at the abi3 3.12 floor; NOT verified whether annotated/defaulted parameter forms survive CPython's signature parser, which is the first thing to check. Open question: whether to merge a user's `__init__` docstring into the class doc automatically (convenient but magic -- the author did not write it there) or only synthesize the signature line and leave prose placement to the author. Surfaced investigating why dunder docstrings cannot cross.
- **[CPython interop] follow-ups from /tpy-review.** (1) **Facade function-signature self-check.** `test_cpython_facade_selfcheck.cpp` validates struct layouts + constants but NOT the `extern "C"` function decls in `cpython_h.hpp`, so a wrong signature surfaces only at link/ABI corruption. Add `static_assert(std::is_same_v<decltype(&::PyFn), decltype(&tpy::cpy::PyFn)>)` per decl. (2) **Boundary-marshalling render helpers live in `codegen_cpp/generator.py`** (`boundary_cpp_type`, `boundary_unmarshallable_msg`) but are consumed upward by `the ext-module validator (tpyc/interop/module_validators.py)` via a local import -- a layering smell; move to a neutral `tpyc/codegen_cpp/ext_boundary.py` (or similar) both sides import. (The admission predicate itself already moved to `type_def_registry.is_boundary_marshallable`, and `BOUNDARY_CPP_TYPES`/`boundary_type_ok` were deleted, so only these two diagnostic-render helpers remain.) (3) **`_Py_NoneStruct` is not a named stable-API symbol** -- it is binary-exported by every CPython and the only way to reach `Py_None` from the no-`Python.h` facade at the abi3 3.12 floor (the documented `Py_GetNone()` lands in 3.13). Marked "don't use directly" upstream; swap to `Py_GetNone()` once the abi3 floor rises to 3.13. (Done in this round: void-return `@export` and the `to_py` overload-ambiguity, now resolved by a `requires`-constrained integral `to_py` template that never competes with the `int64_t`/`double`/`bool` overloads.)
- **[design question, open -- discussion stage, no decision] Revisit the `# tpy:` directive surface: comment pragmas vs in-language spellings.** Comment directives (`# tpy: ext_module`, `macro_module`, `namespace(...)`, `link("pcre2", managed=True)`, ...) are poorly visible in code (dim highlighting) even though typos already warn (parser.py's unknown-directive ParseWarning). Candidates discussed 2026-07-12: (a) status quo -- honest "metadata, not semantics", matches `# coding:`/`# type:` pragma precedent; (b) marker import `from tpy import __extension_module__` -- the `from __future__` precedent, loud typos, highlighted as code; no parameter channel, and linters flag it as an unused import (F401) unlike the special-cased `__future__`; (c) dunder assignments `__ext_module__ = True` / `__tpy_namespace__ = "..."` / `__tpy_link__ = [...]` -- declarative, statically scannable pre-execution (required by `macro_module`, which decides whether the module RUNS under CPython at compile time), CPython-inert without stubs, param-capable via literals, linter-quiet; (d) a call form (`tpy.extern.ext_module()`) -- rejected in discussion: looks like an import-time side effect but would never execute (a declaration in a call costume). Constraint: whatever is chosen must cover the WHOLE surface in at most two coherent forms (flags + parameterized), not fork per-directive; migration would touch every directive consumer, all tests, and docs. Whole-surface redesign, own /tpy-add-feature design pass if picked up.
- **[CPython interop] ext-exec harness robustness gaps (from /tpy-review).** (1) `discover_interop_cases` (conftest) silently drops a `tests/interop/<case>/` dir that has a `driver.py` but no `# tpy: ext_module` source, and picks only the first such `.py` -- a mis-named or future multi-module case is underbuilt with no diagnostic; warn/fail loudly instead. Relatedly, if discovery ever returns nothing, `_INTEROP_CASES` is empty and the module collects zero tests silently -- add a module-load guard asserting at least one case so a broken discovery fails loudly instead of no-op'ing. (2) `compute_ext_exec_fingerprint` doesn't key on the Python version (`sys.version_info`/`sys.executable`): the ext-exec marker stays green across a CPython minor-version switch, so a driver-output divergence between versions stays invisible until `--force-exec`. Fold the version into the fingerprint. Both deferred -- low bite with one case.
- **[CPython interop] ext-exec THIR overlay follow-ups (from /tpy-ready).** (1) **The overlay's AST side is anchored to nothing.** In `tests/cases` the overlay's AST emission is itself byte-compared to the committed snapshot (`tests/conftest.py`, the `all_modules` loop), so any drift between it and the real emission is loud. `run_interop_thir_overlay` instead compiles in-process and never compares its AST side to what the `tpyc` CLI actually wrote, so the overlay could emit a slightly different program than the case really builds and a divergence unique to the CLI shape would be missed. Exposure is nil today -- `options.no_main = True` is the whole ext-module derivation (`tpyc/cli.py`, the `ext_module_build` branch) and the overlay mirrors exactly that -- so this is structural hygiene, not a live defect. Cheap anchor: diff the overlay's AST output against the CLI's `gen_hpp`/`gen_cpp`/`gen_ext` with `// #` comment lines stripped. (2) **Module-scope diagnostics cannot be annotation-validated.** A module-level warning (e.g. the ext_module NUL-docstring drop) formats without a line number, so no `# tpyc: warning(/../)` annotation can attach to it and `tests/cases/interop/warn_export_docstring_nul` pins that site through `diag.txt` alone while its other six sites carry annotations. Either give module-scope diagnostics a line (the directive or docstring line) or teach `validate_annotations` a module-scope form.
- **`urllib.parse` v2 follow-ups (deferred from the v1 stdlib add).** Tracked per-item in STDLIB_ROADMAP.md's urllib.parse table: `parse_qs` (dict-of-lists; needs `dict[str, list[str]]` build), bytes variants (`quote_from_bytes`/`unquote_to_bytes`/`SplitResultBytes`), `urldefrag`, and the extra params/forms (`urlencode(doseq=)`, `quote(encoding=)`). Also the namedtuple-compatibility gap: results are records, so integer indexing (`r[0]`) and unpacking (`a, b, ... = urlsplit(u)`) are unavailable -- all-str components mean `__getitem__(int) -> str` is feasible to add if a parity need surfaces. Each is a focused `/tpy-add-feature`. Surfaced building urllib.parse v1.
- **`urllib.parse.unquote` invalid-UTF-8 -> U+FFFD divergence (silent, documented).** `unquote`/`unquote_plus` of a percent-sequence that decodes to invalid UTF-8 (e.g. `unquote("%FF")`) returns the raw bytes; CPython defaults to `errors='replace'` and substitutes U+FFFD. Matching it needs a lossy UTF-8 decode (`bytes.decode(errors=...)` or equivalent) the runtime does not yet expose -- a small runtime/stdlib feature, not a urllib fix. Well-formed URLs never hit it. Documented in the module header + LANGUAGE_FEATURES. Surfaced by /tpy-review (cpython-parity) of urllib.parse v1. Needs `/tpy-add-feature` (lossy UTF-8 decode).
- **[codegen perf] A constant container of literals should lower to a static/compile-time structure, not a runtime-rebuilt or runtime-initialized heap container.** Two rungs: (a) a set-literal membership in a function body (`x in {"a", "b", ...}`) rebuilds a fresh `ordered_set<std::string>` on EVERY call; (b) hoisting it to a module-level `set[str]` global (the current urllib.parse workaround) builds the heap set once at `__tpy_init` but is still a runtime-initialized heap object, not a compile-time constant. For a container of compile-time literals (esp. string sets used as lookup tables), codegen could emit a truly static structure -- a sorted `constexpr std::array<std::string_view>` + binary search, a perfect hash, or a `string_view` switch -- with zero per-call and zero startup heap cost. Surfaced by /tpy-review of urllib.parse's scheme tables. Needs `/tpy-add-feature`.
- **[feature] Support `Final[set[...]]` / `Final[frozenset[...]]` (container constants) for module-level constants.** `Final` is currently restricted to primitives + tuple (`Final[set[str]] is not supported; only primitive types ... and tuple are allowed`), so a constant lookup table must be spelled as a plain mutable module global `set` -- which works but loses the immutability/intent `Final` documents (`frozenset` would be the natural CPython spelling). Pairs with the constexpr-lowering item above: a `Final` constant container is exactly what should lower to a static structure. Surfaced building urllib.parse's scheme tables (had to use a non-`Final` global). Needs `/tpy-add-feature`.
- **[feature] `collections.namedtuple` / `typing.NamedTuple` support.** A type that is simultaneously a tuple (indexable `r[0]`, unpackable `a, b = r`, iterable) AND carries named fields + methods/properties. TPy has no such type today, which forces stdlib results CPython returns as namedtuples -- `urllib.parse`'s `SplitResult`/`ParseResult` (and future `os.stat_result`-shaped results) -- to be plain records, losing indexing/unpacking (a deliberate, compile-visible divergence). Namedtuple support would let those be true namedtuples and close the divergence. Likely a `@class_macro` synthesizing `__getitem__`/`__iter__`/field properties over a backing tuple, or a first-class type-system construct. Surfaced building urllib.parse v1 (user: "eventually we should handle namedtuples"). Needs `/tpy-add-feature`.
- **Multi-base ctor inheritance with a generic init parent -- test-coverage gap.** `_find_unique_init_parent` now accepts a generic-base instantiation as the unique init parent, and the `inheritance/generic_base_inherited_ctor` case covers single-base + generic-subclass shapes, but the multi-base mixin shape (`class Sub(Base[14], Mixin)` where `Mixin` contributes no `__init__`) is untested -- it exercises the `found is not None` uniqueness path with a generic init parent specifically. Add a case. Surfaced by /tpy-review (test-coverage) of the generic-base inherited-ctor fix.
- **[IR migration] Keep a hoisted str/bytes tuple view target zero-copy when its source provably outlives the hoist scope (precise lifetime analysis).** Today a str/bytes tuple-unpack target hoisted out of a branch is unconditionally owned (`_promote_predecl_view_targets`, the Option-A conservative rule): the hoisted slot outlives the per-branch `__tup` temp and any branch-local by-ref source, so a view would dangle. But when the by-ref source itself outlives the hoist scope, owning is an unnecessary copy. Two instances: (a) the source is a pre-existing function-scope local (`tuple_unpack_stable_name_keeps_view`, just hoisted); (b) the source is assigned on all branch paths under one shared name (`if c: t = make(); a, b = t else: t = make2(); a, b = t`), so the predecl machinery hoists `t` to the *same* outer scope as `a`/`b` -- the source is then function-lifetime and a view stays valid (every read of `a`/`b` happens while `t` is alive). The conservative rule over-owns both; the precise rule -- own iff the source does NOT outlive the target's hoist scope (accounting for same-scope declaration/destruction order) -- is place/loan escape analysis, which belongs on MIR's `Place`/`LoanInfo` model, not a codegen/sema heuristic. Until then the conservative copy is correct, just occasionally non-optimal. Surfaced fixing the tuple-unpack hoisting bug (Option B deferred).

Set it once on the node (alongside `is_owned`/`is_ref`) and have both read it -- matches the "first-class AST facts over consumer-side re-derivation" rule + the THIR direction. Surfaced by /tpy-review (architecture-fit) of the tuple-unpack-view UAF fix.

- **[consolidation debt] Always fully-qualify local type references in generated C++ -- retire the conditional shadow-qualification (and CLOSE the member/type collision class uniformly).** Today local record/enum/@dynamic-protocol type *references* render bare (`day`) and only qualify (`::tpyapp::mod::day`) inside a record whose member shadows the type -- the `RecordInfo.shadows_local_type` sema fact + `_qualify_shadowed_nominals` flag + per-render-path flag-awareness (`_cpp_base_name` for records/enums, `get_dynamic_base_name` for protocols) + the THIR whole-record reject (`docs/THIR_COMPLETION_LEDGER.md`). - **[THIR migration] Hoist reproduce-style mirrors into shared helpers per-rung, NOT at F-final.** The byte-identity-to-AST contract is the oracle that validates THIR -- and it is DELETED at F-final (when the AST form-codegen retires). So the *reproduce*-style mirrors (`_f1_is_const` vs `_is_const_indirect`; the F2b `_gen_assign` optional-field-write branch; `_is_move_source` vs `_is_last_use_movable` -- F2e, with the extra sema-set-vs-walk-built-`movable_locals` equivalence to re-audit on each slice expansion (M3b-move generalized `_is_move_source` to take a `movable_names` param mirroring the AST helper, the ctor MIL passing `own_param_names` -- so the two now share that shape and must move in lockstep); `_unwrap_copy` vs `ctx.unwrap_copy` (a NEW mirror added by M3b-copy; since lowering is analyzer-pure the clean extract is a shared free `unwrap_copy(expr, imported_names)` both delegate to, which touches the AST-side `context.py` -- a "born-shared vs mirror-then-extract" choice for the extraction pass); `_mixed_sign_compare` vs `_mixed_sign_fixed_int`; `_positional_only_template` vs `expand_cpp_template`'s brace grammar (incr 37 -- a gate-side re-parse, so a grammar miss only under-routes or fails loudly, never mis-emits); `_str_name_form`/`_resolved_str_value` vs `_is_str_view_source`/`_resolve_view_storage` (incr 38 -- EMIT-load-bearing: the name-form tag drives the owned-sink `std::string(x)` copy, so this pair is in the high-risk mirror class; when the next str owned sink lands, also fold the twice-spelled decl-init/return wrap condition into one `_wrap_view_to_owned` helper); the emit.py increment-mirrors incl. the F2d two-slot `__slot_N` emit vs `_gen_pointer_local_init`) do NOT "die" at F-final -- they become the canonical and only implementation exactly when their validating diff vanishes, baking in permanently any subtly-wrong behavior that neither a unit test nor an organic corpus case exercised. Contrast the *extract* pattern (`classify_local_binding`, `resolve_stmt_binding_type` -- both paths call one helper, identical by construction), which carries no such risk. Action: prefer extract over reproduce-mirror for each new sema->codegen fact, and hoist each existing mirror into a shared analyzer-pure helper as part of the rung that needs it, so reconciliation is incremental-and-oracle-checked rather than a big-bang at F-final after the net is gone. Surfaced by /tpy-ready retrospective second-opinion of F2.
- **[design territory] Fix the stale-resolved-twin at its source in sema, not at each codegen consumer.** The const-rooted-receiver arms (`_is_const_indirect` + `_f1_is_const`) and the sibling `val_or_cref_t`/`val_or_ref_t` TypeParamRef-return gate (`statements.py:2397` / `thir/lower/statements.py:4050`, filed in BUGS.md) all compensate for the SAME root cause: sema resolves a self/receiver call to the MUTABLE twin before the enclosing method's readonly-ness is inferred in Phase 2, so `resolved_function_info` no longer matches what C++ overload resolution picks on a const receiver. Each codegen/THIR consumer re-derives receiver-constness to paper over the stale `fi`. A cleaner fix re-resolves (or flags) affected self/receiver calls' `resolved_function_info` right after `infer_method_const` runs in `tpyc/sema/mutation_propagation.py`, so every present and future consumer of `fi.is_readonly` sees a correct fact instead of special-casing "peek at the receiver instead of trusting `fi`." Design territory (a Phase-2 re-resolve may carry its own fixpoint ordering concerns); discuss before implementing. Surfaced by /tpy-review (architecture-fit) of the inferred-readonly borrow-const fix.
- **[THIR migration] `THIRAssign.target` is a bare `THIRExpr` (no lvalue guarantee) -- weigh a Place-precursor for F3/F4.** F2b widened `THIRAssign.target` from `THIRName` to `THIRExpr` to carry the optional-field-write target (`recv.field` / `recv->field`), chosen on byte-identity grounds (emit renders both via `_emit_expr`). It is looser than MIR's `Place(Local/Field/Index)` and gives no structural guarantee the target is an lvalue. F3 tuple-unpack and subscript-write targets will pile onto the bare-expr target; revisit a thin lvalue-shaped target node (a Place-precursor) when those land, rather than accreting more shapes onto a bare expr. Surfaced by /tpy-ready retrospective second-opinion of F2.
- **[THIR migration] F3 storage-tuple alias decision is reproduce-mirrored, not extracted.** `forms.is_storage_tuple_alias_decl` (the `auto&& t = <storage tuple field>` arm) is co-located with the binding classifiers as the shared home, but the AST path (`statements.py` `_gen_var_decl_code` ~2157-2186, the `storage_form_tuple_locals` `auto&&` return) still decides this arm inline -- so two implementations co-exist, with the whole-corpus byte-diff as the only anti-drift net. Extending the THIR subset (Subscript / storage-form-Name alias sources) requires updating BOTH the predicate and the inline AST arm in lockstep. Per the "prefer extract over reproduce-mirror" rule (above), the clean fix is to refactor the AST arm to call `is_storage_tuple_alias_decl` (a verified zero-diff extract-method, like `classify_local_binding`); fold it in when the next F3 alias-source cell lands, or at F-final. Surfaced by /tpy-review (architecture-fit) of F3. **UPDATE 2026-07-28: that cell LANDED (`fd519dddb`) and the extract was DEFERRED, so the mirrored surface is now wider, not narrower** -- the predicate gained the Subscript and storage-form-Name sources plus a `storage_tuple_locals` param. Note the entry's own lockstep warning did NOT apply: the AST arm already admitted all three shapes, so the widening only brought THIR up to it. The extract is an AST-side refactor and must land as its own change-set (AST and THIR changes never share one), which is why it was not folded in here.

Surfaced by /tpy-review (test-coverage) of the raise-arg coercion fix.
- **`unsafe_interior_mutable` fields -- deferred scope (v1 shipped Ptr-only, field-level).** The interior-mutable field marker (`unsafe_interior_mutable[Ptr[T]]`, dual of `readonly`; landed for `Rc`/`Weak` refcount cells so `clone`/`downgrade`/`upgrade` are readonly-callable and yield readonly-payload clones) deliberately ships a subset: (a) **value-field interior** -- `unsafe_interior_mutable[T]` on a non-pointer field (a memoized/cached value mutated through a readonly getter) is rejected today; supporting it needs codegen to emit the C++ `mutable` keyword on the member (the Ptr case needs no codegen change since const doesn't cross a raw pointer). (b) **type-level interior metadata** -- instead of a per-field marker, declare a *type* as interior-mutable (e.g. `@unsafe_interior_mutable` on `_RcCellBase`) via library-declared `TypeDef` metadata, so every `Ptr[InteriorType]` field inherits it with zero per-field annotation (more CLAUDE.md-aligned, but broadens the hatch to every appearance of the type -- weigh against the field-level opt-in's auditability). Both are `/tpy-add-feature`-sized. (c) **reject `unsafe_interior_mutable[Ptr[readonly[T]]]`** -- the validation accepts a `Ptr` to a readonly pointee, but `unsafe_interior_mutable` on a const-pointer field is meaningless (the pointee is already inside the readonly boundary); add a reject branch + an `error_` case. Surfaced building the interior-mutable readonly-`Rc.clone` feature.
- **Zero-copy `json.dumps` over typed container shapes -- BLOCKED on protocol-conformance coverage.** Goal: dumping a *typed* container variable (`d: dict[str, int32]`) serializes in place with no `JsonValue` wrapper (the current behavior is a clean rejection -- `error_json_dumps_concrete_container` -- after the implicit `to_union` deep-copy was reverted as a footgun). The clean way is a pure-stdlib type-directed serializer (a `ToJson` protocol + `dumps[T: ToJson](obj: T)`), but that needs built-in/container types to conform to a protocol, which TPy can't express today -- see "Protocol conformance for built-in and generic-container types" under Open feature gaps. A json-specific C++ writer + compiler routing was considered and rejected: it just duplicates the same compiler coupling we want to remove from `print`. So this stays blocked on that foundational capability; keep the clean rejection until then. Surfaced designing zero-copy json.dumps (reverted `to_union`).
- **`PostSemaFunctionMacroContext.note_param_mutated` is shaped for the single-overload free-function host.** The method-body host surface has begun landing (deferred method macros are now driven by `_drain_deferred_sema_macros`), so `note_param_mutated` now explicitly rejects a method host (`if self.is_method: error(...)`) rather than mis-targeting a free function -- but the real method-aware support is still open, and multi-overload targeting was always broken: (a) it writes `direct_mutated_params` on `registry.get_function(name)[-1]`, the last overload by position -- wrong target for a multi-overload host, and the method case needs a `record.get_method`-aware lookup instead; (b) the no-FunctionInfo guard is defensive and untested because it is unreachable through supported usage today (only the out-of-range guard and the new method-host guard have `error_*`/unit coverage); (c) for a *method* host, seeding `direct_mutated_params` can flip Phase-2 `is_readonly` inference and structural-protocol conformance, not just local const-ness. Revisit overload targeting, method-aware resolution, and the readonly/conformance interaction to lift the method-host rejection. Surfaced by /tpy-ready retrospective of the post-sema note_param_mutated addition; method-host guard added by /tpy-review of feat-method-function-macros.
- **Unify the two empty-literal/generic-constructor annotation blocks (`tpyc/sema/expressions.py` ~457 and `tpyc/sema/statements.py` ~3430).** The empty-`[]`-against-a-hint logic is duplicated near-verbatim across the call-arg/hint path (`analyze_expr_with_hint`) and the annotated-assignment path (`x: T = []`): both compute `hint_matches`/`annotation_matches`, both build the `ListLiteralInfo` with `has_explicit_annotation`/`explicit_type`, and both now carry the same recursive-union list-member branch (`needs_wrapper()` + `_find_list_member`). They must be kept in lockstep -- the union branch was added to expressions.py first and the statements.py copy was the source of a half-fixed bug (`x: JsonValue = []` rejected while `json.dumps([])` worked). Fold into one shared helper (statements.py could delegate to the expression path, or both call a common `_resolve_empty_literal_against(target)`). Surfaced by /tpy-review of the empty-list recursive-union fix.
- **Coordinate the two "generic container vs recursive union" dispatches in `compatibility._check_compat`.** The concrete-std-container rejection guard and `_check_union_member_type_args` (immediately below it) share the same outer condition (same-name `NominalType`, differing `type_args`) and are non-overlapping only by construction (the guard requires a std container + a `needs_wrapper()` union element + `a_res != e_res`; the other handles the accept path). Any future change to either has to know about the other. Consider folding the std-container deep-conversion check into `_check_union_member_type_args` (or a shared classifier) so the accept/reject decision lives in one place. Surfaced by /tpy-review (architecture-fit) of the cross-module recursive-union literal fix.
- **Unify non-generic recursive-union (`AliasRef`) C++ rendering onto the qname-keyed map.** The non-generic path renders via the short-name `native_cpp_names` channel (`AliasRef.to_cpp` + the imported-recursive-union registration in `generator.py`), which is collision-prone when two different modules export same-short-named recursive unions both reached cross-module without import -- mitigated today by a first-write-wins skip-guard + the documented same-short-name limitation. The generic path (`RecursiveAliasInstanceType`) is already collision-proof via the qname-keyed `recursive_alias_cpp_names` map. Clean end-state: route non-generic `AliasRef` rendering through the same qname-keyed map (key `{module}.{name}`), retiring the short-name channel for recursive-union wrappers. Surfaced by /tpy-ready retrospective of the cross-module recursive-union literal fix.
- **[LOW perf] str/bytes view->owned wrap is redundant in direct-init contexts.** The shared `_view_source_to_owned` chokepoint wraps a view source uniformly (`std::string(view)` / `::tpy::bytes_copy(view)`) because it can't see its consuming context. In a *direct-initialization* context -- a tuple literal `std::tuple<std::string,...>{view, ...}` -- the str element's explicit `string_view` ctor is already reachable, so the old `{tag, ...}` built the element IN PLACE; the wrap now materializes a temporary + move-constructs it (`{std::string(tag), ...}`), adding one cheap `std::string` move (buffer steal, no extra allocation/char-copy). Function-arg sinks (`push_back`, etc.) genuinely NEED the wrap (the explicit ctor doesn't fire on implicit conversion -- that was the original build failure). Skipping the wrap in tuple-literal str contexts would reintroduce a str-vs-bytes asymmetry (bytes still needs it: `std::vector` has no ctor from `span`), so a clean fix is context-aware (the chokepoint, or its callers, knowing direct-init vs copy-init). Negligible; only worth it if tuple-of-str-from-view turns up on a hot path. Surfaced reviewing the view->owned unification snapshots. **Tuple-unpack TARGETS now reach this sink too**: fixing `get_resolved_type`'s unresolved `var_types` return made them view-form, so `take((x, y))` off `x, y = src` went from the in-place `{x, y}` to `{std::string(x), std::string(y)}`. Same one-move cost, but it widens the shape set a context-aware chokepoint would have to cover, and it is the second source kind to land here -- if a third arrives, build the fix instead of re-noting it.
- **[MED design] Warn at the mixed-tuple module GLOBAL as a stopgap, before the global slot learns the borrow form.** The storage-form wave made `G: tuple[Box, Box] = make_mixed(B)` reachable (it failed the C++ build before) and it now copies SILENTLY -- a new silent CPython divergence, filed HIGH in BUGS.md. The full fix (a borrow-form global slot mirroring the local's machinery) was deferred as too large, but the cheap half was NOT taken: firing the same per-element copy warning the container and field sinks already give would make the divergence acknowledged rather than silent, at the cost of a new warning site. Wants a decision rather than a patch -- it is a diagnostic the deferred fix would later remove, and the pinning case `tuple/element_vs_singleton_global` would need its expectations updated twice. Tracked separately because it is currently buried inside the HIGH module-global entry, where it reads as part of a large deferred fix rather than the one cheap thing that would stop the wave shipping a new silent divergence.
- **[MED] Make the tuple RENDER 3-valued instead of stacking booleans over it.** `is_storage_form_source(expr)` returns a boolean for what is really a 3-valued render -- BORROW / MIXED / STORAGE -- so the storage-form wave had to bolt `renders_own_borrow_tuple` beside it and derive `needs_tuple_storage_lift = not storage or mixed` on top, two booleans encoding three states with the redundancy unstated. Three separate bugs on that branch came from one predicate answering two questions, which is what forced the split. The clean shape is `tuple_render_of(expr) -> {BORROW, MIXED, STORAGE}` with all three booleans as one-line derivations; that is also exactly `docs/IR_DESIGN.md` Q9's form-as-IR-fact, so it should land AS the THIR lowering rather than twice. NOT a fold of `owned_tuple_storage_type` into `collapse_tuple_own_elements` -- that was proposed and correctly rejected, since the two encode OPPOSITE facts (borrow-form unification vs owned-storage form) at disjoint call sites. ~15 `is_storage_form_source` call sites.
- **[MED] Sema mirrors codegen's tuple-render pair at a different breadth.** `_is_owning_tuple_call` (sema) duplicates `is_storage_form_source`'s call arm, and `_borrow_carrying_tuple_return` (sema) mirrors `renders_own_borrow_tuple` (codegen) but tests `has_ref_elements()` where the codegen side tests `is_mixed_own()`, with the ternary composition rule copy-pasted between them. They agree today by compensation, not by construction -- the 're-derive the fact at the consumer' pattern CLAUDE.md warns about, across the sema/codegen boundary. Folds into the 3-valued render item above.
- **[MED] Tuple-element storage-form sinks with no corpus coverage.** The wave's eight-sink claim is pinned unevenly: a plain field assign OUTSIDE a ctor (`h.t = make_mixed(b)`; only the ctor member-init path is exercised), a local reassign, `list.insert()`, a set comprehension, and the POSITIVE arg-lift direction (a mixed result into a fully-owned tuple param -- the param case pins only the negatives) have no case. The `@nocopy` element error is pinned at `append` alone. A regression at the mixed-param sink already shipped past a green full suite for exactly this reason.
- **[LOW] The tuple copy warning states a cost, not a consequence.** `copies B into owned storage (tuple element i); use copy() to make this explicit` reads as an allocation nit, but the thing that matters is that a later write through the stored value will NOT be seen on the original -- these are CPython divergences. The scalar sibling has the same wording. Family-wide rewording, not specific to tuples.
- **[HIGH design] A tuple element does NOT behave like the same type would as a singleton at that position -- and it should.** The rule: element `i` of `tuple[T1, T2, ...]` at position P behaves exactly as `Ti` would as a standalone value at P -- same copy/reference rules, same view rules, same ownership rules. Today the per-position rules are written for top-level values and do not reach inside the aggregate, so each element kind re-derives its form from a different place. **Known instances.** (1) A `str`/`bytes` element of a tuple PARAM is storage form: `def f(t: tuple[str, str])` renders `const std::tuple<std::string, std::string>&`, so passing two views costs two allocations plus two char-copies where `def f(a: str, b: str)` passes the same data as `std::string_view` for free -- visible in one call site: `takes_scalars(a, b)` beside `takes_tuple(std::tuple<std::string, std::string>{std::string(a), std::string(b)})`. The tuple element table (`docs/LANGUAGE_FEATURES.md`, the borrow/storage row) defines a borrow form only for `T | None` and plain NON-VALUE slots, while the `str`/`bytes` param-view rule is a documented exception to value semantics applied only to a TOP-LEVEL param. (2) A per-element-`Own` tuple (`tuple[Own[A], B]`): storing one now materializes the borrowed element BY VALUE at every storage sink and warns per element with `copy()` as the acknowledgment -- step (a) below, DONE. The borrow-POSITION decl paths (rebind, walrus, hoisted local, branch/loop-carried, generator and async frame local), the method-producer const disagreement, and the `| None` element are DONE -- step (b) below. A reference member nested inside an inner value tuple warns at every sink too, naming the depth as an element path (the copy check walks nested value tuples). What remains is the `Optional`-WRAPPED producer, whose return ABI is a design fork rather than a fix; and one sink that still copies SILENTLY -- a module global. Both are filed in BUGS.md. The inferred container element type now takes the owned storage form, so a fixed `Array` and a `vector` no longer disagree about alias-vs-copy at the same store. **Caveat on the rule:** it is same SEMANTICS, not same C++ spelling -- a singleton borrow is `T&`, but a tuple of references is non-assignable (exactly what makes the container shape fragile), so elements keep the `T*` stand-in. **Sequencing.** (a) make storage agree with the annotation rule (sema) -- DONE for the bare mixed tuple; (b) fix the borrow-position decl paths -- DONE, AST-first per the THIR contract (sema keeps the per-element `Own` on a mixed local instead of collapsing it onto a unified borrow it has no form for, and every decl path spells the mixed render); the `Optional`-wrapped return is carved out of it as its own design question; (c) unify onto ONE elementwise "what form does element i take here" question, which is what THIR's form-as-IR-fact design exists for (`docs/IR_DESIGN.md` Q9) -- do that AS the THIR lowering, not twice. Cost to expect: element form changes tuple param SIGNATURES for `str`/`bytes`, so wide snapshot churn plus an ABI change. Needs `/tpy-add-feature`.
- **[LOW codegen readability] A bytes literal coerced to owned bytes/bytearray still renders the nested `::tpy::bytes_copy(::tpy::bytes_literal("...", N))`.** The storage-form literal path now emits the single `::tpy::bytes_literal_owned(...)`, but a bytes literal reaching an owned slot via a COERCION (`bytesview_to_bytes` / `bytesview_to_bytearray` in `tpyc/coercions.py`) -- notably `bytearray(b"...")` -- still gets the nested form: the literal renders as a view (`bytes_literal(...)` span) and the coercion lambda, which only sees the already-rendered string, wraps it in `bytes_copy(...)`. Correct, just verbose. Clean fix: render a bytes-literal source whose target is an owned bytes/bytearray slot directly via `cpp_bytes_literal_owned` (so no view->owned coercion fires) -- a sema/coercion-insertion change, NOT a codegen-helper swap, and NOT a string-sniff of the coercion arg. Surfaced finishing the readable-bytes-literal work (~8 snapshots still show the nested form, all `bytearray(b"...")`). Needs `/tpy-add-feature`.
- **[LOW] Fold the str/bytes view->owned-into-Optional-slot decision into the one chokepoint.** The view->owned unification routed three sites through `_view_source_to_owned`, but a FOURTH decider remains: `_maybe_convert_opt_str_param` (`tpyc/codegen_cpp/expressions.py:486`, called at :1318) handles an `Optional[str]` param flowing into an `Optional[str]` slot (emits `s ? std::make_optional(std::string(*s)) : std::nullopt`), and it is str-ONLY (no bytes sibling). Not buggy today -- the bytes-Optional-into-Optional-slot shapes build and run via the optional/coercion machinery -- so this is cleanliness, not a defect. The clean end-state: the chokepoint's bare-slot arm uses `_is_*_view_source OR _expr_uses_optional_*_param`, while the `_wrap_for_owned_slot` Optional residual uses only `_is_*_view_source` (to avoid double-wrapping a whole-optional source); both could instead key uniformly on `_is_narrowed_value_optional(expr)` (`:570`, declared-Optional + analyzed-non-Optional = a narrowed deref vs a whole optional), collapsing the param-name augmentation and `_maybe_convert_opt_str_param` into the single chokepoint and giving bytes parity for free. A consumer-side re-derivation today; folding it onto the first-class `_is_narrowed_value_optional` fact is the per-CLAUDE.md direction. Surfaced by /tpy-ready retrospective second-opinion of the view->owned unification.
- **[cleanup] The str/bytes view->owned copy spelling lives in two helpers.** `view_to_owned_conv` (`tpyc/type_def_registry.py`, the bare `std::string` / `::tpy::bytes_copy` callable, wrapped by `view_owned_copy_init` for the coro/generator-frame ctor-init + init-capture) and `_view_owned_copy_expr` (`tpyc/codegen_cpp/expressions.py`, the expression-site chokepoint + optional-param assign) both encode the same str->`std::string` / bytes->`::tpy::bytes_copy` mapping. Collapse to one source -- `_view_owned_copy_expr` could delegate to `view_to_owned_conv`, or the mapping could become a `copy_conv` field on `ViewTypeFamily` that every consumer reads. The two serve different layers (registry frame-capture vs codegen expression-site), so it is a cross-module consolidation, not a mechanical swap; relates to item folding `_maybe_convert_opt_*_param` onto `_is_narrowed_value_optional`. Surfaced by /tpy-review (architecture-fit) of the bytes view-family param unification.
- **Compound view-source residual optimization (core DONE).** The COMPOUND view-deduction work (ternary / `and`-`or` / nested) is done: a view deduced from a compound owned-borrow source now registers EVERY storage root via the shared `walk_view_source_leaves` traversal (`tpyc/sema/local_deduction.py`), so mutating any root demotes it to owned -- this closed a silent UAF (a compound view tracked no roots before) -- and a narrowed `str | None` param deref is now a zero-copy view (the `std::string(std::string(...))` double-wrap is gone). One residual *optimization* remains, currently resolving OWNED (sound, just not zero-copy): **mixed pending-view + owned-borrow compound arms** (`x = a if c else d[0]`, `a` a pending-view local) conservatively resolve owned (the pending arm forces owned in the fresh-from-owned branch) -- a view tracking both the `source_var_ids` and the borrow-root channel would reclaim the copy. Folds naturally into the provenance-classifier consolidation (next item). Surfaced finishing the compound-view-roots fix.
- **[cleanup] Unify the view-source structural recursion shape.** THREE independent walks of the same TpyCoerce / TpyBinOp `&&`-`||` / TpyIfExpr arm shape: `walk_view_source_leaves` (`tpyc/sema/local_deduction.py`, drives pending-source + borrow-root collection), `is_view_compatible_source`'s own and/or+ternary recursion (same file, the view-safety predicate -- guarded today only by a keep-in-sync INVARIANT comment), and `addr_taken_roots` (`tpyc/sema/context.py:46`). A future node kind (e.g. walrus) needs all three updated in lockstep; a miss between the predicate and the leaf walk yields a stale view (UAF). Route `is_view_compatible_source` through `walk_view_source_leaves` (a leaf-fn returning view-safe-ness combined with `all()` -- non-trivial: the predicate uses AND/short-circuit + PendingViewType early-exits vs the walk's list return, so it's a small design step, not mechanical), and move the shared walker into `context.py` (it only needs parse nodes; `local_deduction` imports `context`, so verify no import cycle) so `addr_taken_roots` shares it too. Surfaced by /tpy-review (architecture-fit, safety-model) of the compound-view-roots fix. (Breadcrumb: routing reassigned `str`/`bytes` PARAMS through this same view-source machinery -- so a param reassigned only to borrow-valid sources stays a view like a local does, retiring the coarse `param_needs_copy_for_reassign` for view types -- was probed and DEFERRED as not-worth-standalone: near-zero corpus payoff and a silent-dangle risk if mis-classified (a `span` param is implicitly constructible from an owned vector, so a wrong call dangles with no build error). Only fold the param-reassign path in if doing this consolidation anyway.)
- **[cleanup] DRY the for-loop / comprehension iterable-render call sites onto one `(code, type)` helper.** The narrowed-value-Optional fix routes every iterable-render site through the pair `_maybe_unwrap_narrowed_optional(expr, gen_expr_deref(expr), is_indirect_name(expr))` + `narrowed_value_optional_iter_type(expr, get_resolved_type(expr))` -- repeated inline at ~3 comprehension sites in `tpyc/codegen_cpp/expressions.py` (`_gen_comprehension_iife`, `_gen_comp_begin_end_loop`, the array/general comp paths), plus the sync for-loop's `_for_iterable_deref` and the resumable `gen_async._for_src_access` / `gen_generators._analyze_for_strategy`. A single helper returning `(rendered_code, dispatch_type)` would collapse the repetition and make a future missed iterable-render site (the recurring decay pattern) impossible. Surfaced by /tpy-review (architecture-fit) of the narrowed-Optional for-loop fix.
- **[cleanup] `_enter_comp_scope` queries the un-narrowed iterable type when registering the comprehension loop var.** `tpyc/codegen_cpp/expressions.py` -- `_enter_comp_scope` calls `get_resolved_type(gen.iterable)` (not `narrowed_value_optional_iter_type`), so for a narrowed value-Optional iterable `get_iterable_element_type` returns None and the comp loop var is left unregistered in the var-type table. No live symptom for `str`/`bytes` (the element is `char`/`uint8`, never an Optional needing a deref), so it is latent; route it through the same narrowed-type helper for consistency with the corrected outer dispatch. Surfaced by /tpy-review (architecture-fit) of the narrowed-Optional for-loop fix.

- **[design] DERIVE the borrowing-view fact instead of declaring it.** `type_def_registry.is_borrowing_view_type()` is a declared flag ORed with four category/qname checks: only the three dict views (`builtins.dict_keys` / `dict_values` / `dict_items`) set `is_borrowing_view=True`, while the SPAN and VARARGS categories and `tpy.SpanIter` / `tpy.StrView` / `tpy.BytesView` are recognized by name. So the family's defining property -- "a value type that carries an interior pointer into someone else's storage" -- is asserted in two places and checked in neither, and a ninth view added tomorrow is invisible to every consumer until someone remembers the qname list. Derive it the way `Send`/`Sync` are derived: a value type IS a borrowing view iff it transitively contains a non-owning reference field (`Ptr[T]`, `Span[T]`, `StrView`, `BytesView`, another borrowing view), computed from the record's own definition; a `@native` value type that declares no fields is treated as BORROWING, which is the conservative direction (at worst an unnecessary hoist or copy, never a dangle), with a declaration -- an `@owns_its_storage`-shaped marker -- for the native handles that own. `is_borrowing_view_type` then collapses to the derived TypeDef fact and the four category checks go, taking the "unguarded for five of eight members" hole with them.

  Consumer groups to re-point (~29 call sites, the sizing): the sema view-dangle diagnostics (`sema/statements.py` `_is_dangling_temporary_arg` / `_view_source_is_temporary` and the for-iterable borrow arm, `sema/compatibility.py`); the generator/coroutine borrow-param index derivation in `sema/registration.py`; `@auto_readonly` / const-ness inference; view-constructor typing in `sema/calls.py`; the container-insert-of-a-view-element check in `sema/methods.py`; the for-source hoist in `codegen_cpp/context.py` and `thir/lower/statements.py`; the frame-param gate (`_res_param_ok`) and the frame-temp rule's own `frame_temp_arg_slot` / `value_category.frame_temp_arg_source`. Needs `/tpy-add-feature` (it is a new derivation rule over TypeDefs plus a user-visible native declaration, not a rename). Surfaced by /tpy-ready on the borrowing-view frame-param slice; re-scoped when the uniform frame-temp rule landed.

- **[perf] The uniform frame-temp hoist is type-blind, so it also hoists temporaries the frame slot COPIES anyway.**
  `tests/cases/async/async_assert_message_await` emits `std::string __coro_arg_0;` on the outer frame plus
  `__coro_arg_0 = "positive"; __sub_0.emplace(__coro_arg_0);` for an inline `await msg("positive")` where `msg` takes
  `str` BY VALUE -- an owned field and a copy for a literal that was safe rendered inline. Two narrowings, both keyed on
  the SINK rather than on a view taxonomy: (a) skip the hoist when the frame's param classification says the slot is an
  owning copy (the OWNED_COPY / by-value kinds -- a copied slot cannot dangle); (b) skip `str`/`bytes` LITERAL sources
  (static storage) at any slot. Behaviour-neutral, snapshot churn in the shrinking direction; do it as its own small
  change with that case's `--dump-code` as the before/after.

- **[cleanup] Pin the moved reject tag for `SpanIter` / dict-view frame params.** The one `is_borrowing_view_type` arm in `_res_param_ok` admits `SpanIter[T]` and the three dict views at the frame-PARAM gate; they then reject at the CALL SITE arg shape. The verdict is unchanged (reject before, reject after), but the tag moved from `res.param_type:*` to `call.arg_shape.*` and no corpus case observes either. Add a section to an existing `error_` case rather than a case per family member. Surfaced by /tpy-ready on the borrowing-view frame-param slice.
- **[harness] An `error_` case whose sources are all frontend-plugin files cannot exist.** `error_case_annotation_problems` and the per-file annotation validation in `tests/test_case.py` both glob `src/*.py`, so a `tests/cases/pascal/error_*` case fails the gate with "Error test must have at least one '# tpyc: error(...)' annotation" -- there is no `.py` file to carry the leg, and an annotation in the `.pas` is never read. That is why the driver-error regression is pinned as a harness test (`tests/test_failure_reporting.py`) rather than a case. Fix shape: read the case's plugin-extension sources too (the registry knows the extensions) and settle how a `# tpyc:` annotation is spelled inside a plugin language's comment syntax -- a design call, not a mechanical widening. Surfaced by /tpy-ready on the driver-diagnostic harness fix.
- **[cleanup] `tpyc/codegen_cpp/functions.py` carries five inline copies of the `default_emittable` / `default_to_cpp` suffix pairing.** Lines ~470, ~481, ~511, ~564 and ~618 each spell the same `if emit_defaults and defaults and default_emittable(...): part += f" = {default_to_cpp(...)}"` pair, so the param-index-to-slot mapping and the "is it emittable" question are re-derived per signature emitter. The resumable emitter consolidated exactly this into one `_default_suffix` helper (`tpyc/codegen_cpp/gen_async.py`), which is what let the factory declaration and the frame constructor carry byte-identical default sets by construction; the same helper shape is wanted here so the five plain-signature emitters cannot drift either. No behavior change -- verify with the corpus byte-diff. Surfaced by /tpy-review of the resumable-factory default fix.
- **[cleanup -- HARDER THAN IT LOOKS] The `nonstmt_borrow_bindings` override in the borrow snapshot is LOAD-BEARING, not a redundant epicycle.** An aliasing match-capture of an lvalue subject records a stmt-borrow (`sema/match.py`) AND adds the name to `nonstmt_borrow_bindings`, which `analyzer.py`'s function-end snapshot OR's back in to cancel the `nonstmt_bound_names` exclusion. It LOOKS like add-to-exclusion-then-cancel, but the override is function-level on purpose: the match-arm codegen emits the capture *unconditionally in borrow form* (`q = &subject`), so the variable's single C++ declaration must stay pointer form for the WHOLE function -- even if the same name is later bound by an owned `with...as` / for-loop var (which re-adds it to `nonstmt_bound_names`). A naive cleanup that drops the override (or lets the later owned binding win) makes the decl owned (`Box q`) while the arm still binds a borrow -> the two disagree and codegen reads garbage. Verified: removing the override regresses `tests/cases/match/borrow_capture_then_with_rebind` from `99/7/99` to `0/7/0`. A real cleanup must unify the match-arm capture's emitted FORM with the variable's decl form (make the arm defer to owned when the name is later owned-bound, accepting the copy/parity implications), not just simplify the snapshot bookkeeping -- bigger work, likely IR-era (the place/loan model makes "this name's form" a single fact). Surfaced by /tpy-review (test-coverage) of the attempted cleanup, which a regression test caught. The guard test now exists.
- **[codegen readability] `print(v)` of a narrowed `str|None`/`bytes|None` name renders `print_optional_val(v)` instead of dereferencing the proven-non-None value.** The print path (`tpyc/codegen_cpp/builtins.py` ~332) branches on `get_resolved_type(arg)` -- the *declared* Optional type -- not the sema-narrowed analyzed type, so inside `if a is not None:` a `print(a)` still routes through `print_optional_val`. NOT a defect: output is correct (the optional is present, so the value prints). Cleanliness only -- a narrowed NAME arg could deref + print directly, but the fix must preserve the deliberate field-case `print_optional_val` (field storage stays `std::optional<T>`). Sibling of the (now-fixed) dict-value narrowing skip, same root (declared-vs-narrowed type at a value sink). Surfaced fixing the dict-value narrowed-Optional bug.
- **[codegen readability] `_emit_guarded_arm_tail` emits a dead `goto __match_end` after a terminating arm body.** The shared guarded-arm tail emitter (`tpyc/codegen_cpp/match.py`) unconditionally appends `goto __match_end_N;` even when the arm body ends in `return`/`raise`, producing unreachable dead code (e.g. `record_guard` / `nested_type_pattern_edges` snapshots emit `return "other"; goto __match_end_2;`). Pre-existing in the helper; newly reachable for unguarded wildcard/capture arms now that the guarded-record capture branch routes through it. Compiles, no g++ warning -- purely cosmetic. Fix: gate the emit on `not stmts_terminate(case.body)`. Churns the str/float + record guarded-match snapshots, so do it on its own small branch. Surfaced by /tpy-review of the match-capture-indirect-subject fix.
- **[codegen readability] for-over-generator/iterator loop body is under-indented by one level.** A `for x in <generator-or-iterator>:` lowers to `{ auto __src; auto&& __itr; for(;;){ next; if break; <binding>; <BODY> } }`, but the loop BODY statements emit at the enclosing block's indent instead of the `for` body indent -- e.g. the loop-var binding sits at the correct depth and the next line (`print(x)`) drops back two levels. A plain `for x in <list>:` indents correctly, so the bug is specific to the iterator/generator for-lowering (the body emit doesn't account for the extra `{ ... for(;;) { } }` nesting). Compiles and runs correctly (C++ is whitespace-insensitive) -- purely cosmetic in `--dump-code` / snapshots. Reproducer: `for x in g(): print(x)` over any generator (`/tmp/agents/rev/genloop.py`). Pure cosmetic -> churns many generator/iterator-loop snapshots, so fix on its own small branch. Surfaced by /tpy-review of the audit-#11 view_of_param_yielded test snapshot.
- **Borrow/storage chokepoint -- test-coverage gaps.** Two over-trigger / regression guards not yet written (no observed failure): (a) a B56 reference-type ternary with BOTH arms fresh rvalues (`c = [1] if flag else [2]`) -- guards that the new "ternary copies a reference type" diagnostic does NOT over-fire when neither arm aliases; (b) a `Send[T | None]` / `Sync[T | None]` marker over a pointer-repr Optional -- guards the `_make_marker` -> `with_inner` `force_pointer_repr` preservation (no `send_sync/` case exercises a pointer-repr Optional inside a marker). Add under `tests/cases/control_flow/` and `tests/cases/send_sync/`. Surfaced by /tpy-review (test-coverage) of the chokepoint branch.
- **await-result tuple unpack -- test-coverage gaps.** The move-out fix (`async/await_tuple_own_unpack` + the CPython-parity `await_async_tuple_unpack`) covers 2-element Own/reference/value tuples, whole-assign, and loop re-await. Add: (a) a 3+-element await tuple with two `Own` elements (multiple move-outs from one `auto&& __tup`); (b) an await-tuple unpack inside a `try`/`except` body across a suspension (frame cleanup interleaving with owned-element destruction). Surfaced by /tpy-review (test-coverage) of `fix-await-tuple-nocopy`.
- **owned-tuple PARAM -- test-coverage gaps.** The owned-tuple-param feature (`tuple[Own[A], ...]` -> `std::tuple<...>&&`) is covered for 2-element sync functions (unpack/forward/return, never-consumed warn+suppress, use-after-move, mixed exclusion). Add: an owned-tuple param on a **generator/async** function (interaction with frame-struct promotion -- the param is seeded into `movable_locals` + `storage_form_tuple_locals`) and on a **class method**. Surfaced by /tpy-review (test-coverage) of the owned-tuple-param feature.
- **owned-tuple never-consumed warning is per-tuple, not per-element.** `_warn_unconsumed_own_params` (`tpyc/sema/analyzer.py`) suppresses the warning for a `tuple[Own[A], ...]` param when ANY owned element is `@nocopy`/value-typed (`any(...)`), so a mixed `tuple[Own[NocopySock], Own[BigInt]]` that is never consumed is silenced even though the `BigInt` element is genuinely unconsumed -- weaker than the scalar per-param model. Whether to tighten to `all(...)` (warn unless EVERY owned element is drop-legitimate) is a warning-semantics design question, not a mechanical flip: tightening could newly warn on legitimate consume-one/drop-the-other patterns. Surfaced by /tpy-review (architecture-fit, safety-model) of the owned-tuple-param feature.
- **Tuple-element BigInt-overflow panic -- test gap.** `int/panic_int_to_fixed_aggregate_overflow` covers an out-of-range `BigInt` element in a *list* literal, but the *tuple*-literal element path is a separate sema route (`_analyze_tuple_literal` via `_materialize_narrowing_element_coercion`, vs the array path's inline check). Add a panic case for an overflowing `BigInt` element in a `tuple[..., int32]` literal/return so the tuple route's runtime `to_fixed_check` is guarded too. Surfaced by /tpy-review (test-coverage) of `fix-aggregate-literal-elem-coercion`.
- **Variadic tuples (`TypeVarTuple` / `*Ts`, and variadic-arity tuple returns).** TPy has fixed-arity tuple types + unpacking (FEATURE_ROADMAP A10) but no variadic-tuple generics: a function can't take/return a tuple of statically-unknown arity, nor splat `*args` of heterogeneous types into a fixed-arity tuple. Substantial type-system + codegen feature (the C++ side is `std::tuple` with parameter packs); warrants `/tpy-add-feature`. **Blocks `itertools.chain` / `product` / `permutations` / `combinations`** (chain/product take `*iterables`; product/permutations/combinations yield tuples whose arity depends on the inputs) and the *variadic* `starmap` (the fixed two-argument `starmap` is separately blocked on the simple-peephole dangling-capture bug -- see BUGS.md). Surfaced scoping itertools v2.
- **asyncio I/O reactor follow-ups (post-M2 + smaller gaps).** The M1 epoll reactor + M2 `sock_accept`/`sock_connect` + the client streams layer (`open_connection` -> `StreamReader`/`StreamWriter`) shipped (`EpollReactor` + `get_running_loop().sock_recv`/`sock_sendall`/`sock_accept`/`sock_connect`; see `docs/ASYNC_DESIGN.md` "I/O reactor" + `examples/net/async_echo_*`). Remaining, roughly in priority order: (1) **Swap-in reactor** -- make the executor's `reactor` field `@dynamic Reactor`-typed (it's concrete `EpollReactor | None` today; the `Reactor` Protocol already exists in `_executor.py`) and let `asyncio.run` take a reactor factory, so a user-provided / alternative backend can replace it. NOTE: cross-platform readiness polling is already handled *below* the TPy line -- `epoll_impl.cpp` is dual-backend (epoll on Linux, kqueue on macOS/BSD) behind the flat `tpy_epoll_*` ABI via `#ifdef`.
