- **(low prio) Registry-drive the managed-third-party CLI wiring.** Adding a managed lib today is a coordinated three-file edit -- argparse flag registration in `cli.py`, the `third_party_modes` dict literal (`{"pcre2": args.pcre2, "mbedtls": args.mbedtls}`), and `_FACTORIES` in `third_party.py` -- yet only `_FACTORIES` is genuinely registry-driven. The flag name already lives on `ThirdPartyLib.cli_flag`, so the argparse registration loop and the modes dict could both be derived from `known_lib_names()` + `getattr(args, ...)`, leaving `_FACTORIES` as the single source of truth. Threshold now met: the third managed lib (`date`, datetime v2) landed with exactly this three-file edit -- pick up on the next build-layer touch. Surfaced by /tpy-review (architecture-fit) of the mbedTLS wiring.
- **(low prio) De-duplicate the vendor-script sidecar helpers.** `scripts/vendor_cacert.py`, `vendor_mbedtls.py`, and `vendor_pcre2.py` now carry a verbatim-identical `_stamp` / `_read_sidecar` / `_read_sidecar_version` / `_write_sidecar` shape (nothing lib-specific in the timestamp-reuse + sidecar-read logic). A shared `scripts/_vendor_common.py` with `stamp(sidecar_path, metadata)` / `read_sidecar(path)` would remove the triplication without disturbing the documented "one vendor script per lib" pattern. Threshold now met: the fourth vendor script (`vendor_date.py`, datetime v2) landed as another verbatim copy -- fold in on the next vendoring touch. Surfaced by /tpy-review (architecture-fit) of the bundled CA store.
- **Fill in package metadata before public release.** `pyproject.toml` declares only `name`/`description`/`Homepage = https://tpy.dev`. Add `authors`/`maintainers`, a `Repository` URL (deferred while the GitHub repo is private), and a `license` field + `LICENSE` file (project is currently unlicensed = all-rights-reserved; pick proprietary vs OSS when going public). Optionally `keywords` + trove `classifiers` for PyPI discoverability.
- **[feature] pyproject v0: build TPy extensions and apps from pyproject.toml.** Two user stories: (a) a `# tpy: ext_module` builds into the user's wheel as part of a normal pyproject build (PEP 517 hook or build-backend plugin wrapping `tpyc -b`); (b) a standalone TPy app builds/installs from its pyproject (entry point -> compiled binary). v1 deliberately minimal (a `[tool.tpy]` table + a build hook), but the DESIGN must be forward-looking -- dependency consumption (TPy libraries installed as PyPI packages on the compiler search path) and the `tpx` porcelain (docs/PROJECT_TOOLING_DESIGN.md) should be extensions of the same shape, not a second mechanism. Own `/tpy-add-feature` design pass before building. Scoped for 0.6.0 (RELEASE_PLAN).
- **[feature] Per-project compilation options in pyproject (`[tool.tpy]`).** Today project-wide options (`--default-int`, third-party lib modes; future: range-check mode, string/char representation) live on the CLI invocation only; tests use options.json. Users need a committed per-project home so builds are reproducible without wrapper scripts: read `[tool.tpy]` from the nearest pyproject.toml, explicit CLI flags override. Design together with the pyproject v0 build hook (same table, one discovery rule). Scoped for 0.6.0 (RELEASE_PLAN).

## Compiler Performance / mypyc

Goal: speed up test runs (currently ~3 min parallel, ~6 min single-threaded for non-slow tests) and prepare for self-hosting. These optimizations are worth doing independently but also remove mypyc blockers.

### Hotspot fixes (ordered by impact)

- Memoize type transformations: parked. PERF TODO note left at `substitute_type_params` in `sema/type_ops.py` for the next candidate; needs profiling data post-mypyc before acting.
- `isinstance` overhead on type predicates: `TypeKind` / `TpyType.tag` was retired when primitive subclasses collapsed to `NominalType` singletons; predicates now dispatch through `type_def_of(t).category` (dict lookup + attribute) or compound isinstance for structural types -- a per-call cost regression vs the prior frozenset tag lookups. Real win lands under mypyc; pre-mypyc profiling hasn't been done. Pre-mypyc mitigations noted as `PERF TODO` comments at the hot paths (`coercions.py::resolve_coercion`, `type_def_registry.py::type_def_of`, `typesys.py::is_numeric_type` family) -- hash-table coercion dispatch and per-instance category caching on `NominalType` are the two concrete knobs if a profile shows the dispatch is bottlenecking.

### mypy compliance (~1086 errors remaining)

- `TypeGuard` on predicate helpers (`is_protocol_type` -> `TypeGuard[NominalType]`, etc.) -- ~86 `attr-defined` errors
- `Scope | None` union-attr errors (67) -- genuinely optional, needs per-site narrowing
- `arg-type` (448), `assignment` (175) -- scattered, per-file mechanical work
- `object.__setattr__` in `PtrType.__post_init__` -- refactor to avoid

### mypyc integration (after mypy compliance)

- switch from hatchling to setuptools with mypyc build step (or mypycify)
- keep macro loader as pure Python, exclude from mypyc compilation

## Investigate
- Unify the two inherited-subst composition copies into one shared helper (e.g. `type_ops.compose_type_substs`): `tpyc/sema/methods.py` `_analyze_instance_method` composes inherited x instance substs one level (with an `isinstance(v, TpyType)` guard for `N: int` bindings), while `tpyc/sema/protocols.py:740-758` has a more complete twin that also transitively resolves `TypeParamRef` chains. Hand-converged duplicates drift. While unifying, verify multi-hop generic-through-generic chains with a test (`class Mid[V](Bag[V, 8]); class Leaf[W](Mid[W])` -- the flat merge in `lookup_record_method_overloads` plus one-level composition may leave the declaring param bound to the intermediate one; unverified, surfaced by /tpy-review of the subclass-receiver bound fix).
- Polymorphic integer literals (Rust-style). Today `IntLiteralType` is resolved at the assignment site to `default_int_type` (int32 by default), so `a = 0; f(a)` for `f(x: uint64)` requires either `a: uint64 = 0` or a cast. The current `literal_default_vars` retro-widening covers function-local cases that re-fit a fixed-int target on first typed-slot use, but module-level constants (`CONST = 5`), collection-element literals (`weights = [10, 20, 30]; send_byte(weights[0])`), and locals reassigned from a non-literal expression don't benefit. The full alternative would be to keep `IntLiteralType` polymorphic *everywhere* until first use that demands a concrete type -- the consistent mental model is "literals adapt to context anywhere", but the cost surface is wide: comparisons, prints, `for x in xs:` iter element types, generic inference, container element-type unification, and ~all sema sites that read `var_types[id(decl)]` mid-flow would need to handle "still IntLit" or trigger resolution. Also requires a deliberate generic-inference policy (do unbound `T` resolve to default_int from a literal arg, or look ahead at constraints?). Defer until the retro-widen cliff (function-local mutation drops the seed; conflicting demands lock to first usage) starts producing user complaints in real code.
- CPython native (C) module for tpy stubs: the `lib/cpy/tpy/` stubs are pure Python. A C extension module could improve CPython performance for programs that use tpy types (int32, Array, Span, etc.) heavily.
- investigate rust like feature (borrowing, lifetimes etc) to make the language safe; however these should be softer restrictions than in rust
- zig language: what it is, how is it different from C, what useful patterns can we learn
- Distinct types (newtypes): `class Meters(Distinct[float]): pass` -- zero-cost wrapper that creates a nominally distinct type. Prevents mixing incompatible values of the same underlying type (units, IDs, currencies). C++ codegen: thin struct wrapper or strong typedef. Inspired by Nim's `distinct` keyword.
- `@constexpr` decorator: mark pure functions as compile-time evaluable, emit C++ `constexpr`. Useful for lookup tables, constants, config. Low implementation cost -- lean on C++ compiler. `TABLE: Final[int32] = factorial(10)` computed at compile time.
- Inline iterators: `@inline` on generator functions to unroll the loop body at the call site instead of creating a state machine. Zero overhead, important for hot paths. Generalizes what `range()` already does implicitly to user-defined iterators. Inspired by Nim's inline vs closure iterator distinction.
- Runtime exception migration -- see `docs/EXCEPTION_DESIGN.md` for the per-type migration table (status, sites, divergences). Pending items live there, not here.
- Better runtime panic message for unhandled `@error_return` calls. Currently `_maybe_error_return_unwrap` (`tpyc/codegen_cpp/expressions.py`) emits `tpy_panic("unhandled error return")` which is opaque -- doesn't include the function name or the error value's data. Improve to `tpy_panic("unhandled X in <func>: " + e.message)` or similar. Affects all return-tier panic sites uniformly.

## Builtins
- **`min(iterable)` / `max(iterable)` single-iterable form.** Only the variadic `min(a, b, ...)` form exists today; `min(xs)` over a `list`/iterable -- the *primary* Python usage -- errors with "No matching overload for min(list[int32])". Add the iterable-reducing overload (and `key=`/`default=` to follow). Common first-non-trivial-program idiom. Surfaced by /tpy-fuzzy-test (collections), 0.3.0 smoke test. **Re-reported downstream 2026-08-03 and still live** (`max(xs)` over `list[float]` -> `No matching overload for max(PendingList[float, 3]#0)`), called out there as a P0 builtin and "one of the most common shapes in ordinary Python"; they worked around it with `sorted(xs)[-1]`. Two independent reports plus a trivial workaround-with-a-sort is the signal to schedule this rather than leave it in the backlog.
- **`reverse=` keyword on `list.sort()` and `sorted()`.** Both reject `reverse=True` ("does not support keyword argument 'reverse'"). Descending sort is a first-page Python idiom; today it needs a custom comparator. Add the `reverse: bool = False` keyword to both. Surfaced by /tpy-fuzzy-test (collections), 0.3.0 smoke test.
- **Builtins as first-class function values.** `key=len`, `map(str, xs)`, etc. fail with "'len' is not a variable" -- builtin names can't be passed as callables (only user `def`s can). The diagnostic should at least suggest wrapping (`def my_len(s: str) -> int32: return len(s)`); the feature is making builtin references materialize as callable values. Surfaced by /tpy-fuzzy-test (collections), 0.3.0 smoke test.
- Generic Fn param type deduction: `sorted[T,K](Iterable[T], Fn[[T],K])` shares T between iterable and Fn, so the Fn param can widen T (e.g. `sorted([3,1,4], key=negate)` widens T from int32 to BigInt). In C++, T and KeyFn are independent template params -- the key function's type is deduced separately and implicit conversion handles the call. The proper TPy fix: support independent callable type params bounded over other params, e.g. `sorted[T, KFn: Callable[[T], Comparable]](Iterable[T], KFn)`. Current behavior (widening) is correct but suboptimal; explicit `list[int32]` + BigInt key already errors.
- type(); (in future `T = type(x); z = T()`)
- tpy.ctypes.CInt32
- ptr() function? Auto-select Ptr vs Ptr[readonly[T]] based on binding mutability. Needs sema-level magic (mutability not in type, it's in binding context).
- `tpy.unsafe.unsafe_address_of(x) -> int`: return the memory address of an object as an integer. Useful for identity comparison in tests (proving reference semantics vs silent copy). C++ codegen: `reinterpret_cast<uintptr_t>(&x)`.

## Python features
- **Nested comprehensions** (`[x for row in grid for x in row]`). Rejected today with a clean "Nested comprehensions not yet supported"; the double-`for` form is common enough (flattening, cartesian products) to schedule. Surfaced by /tpy-fuzzy-test (collections), 0.3.0 smoke test.
- **`object` and `type` as annotation types.** `object` errors with "Unknown type: object"; `type` with "'type' cannot be used as a type annotation". This blocks the canonical context-manager `__exit__(self, exc_type: type | None, exc_val: BaseException | None, exc_tb: object | None) -> bool` signature -- users must leave those params unannotated. `object` could map to `Any`; `type`-as-value is gated on the same first-class-class-object work as the `## Open feature gaps` `type()` items. At minimum, document the unannotated `__exit__` workaround. Surfaced by /tpy-fuzzy-test (tplib-advanced), 0.3.0 smoke test.
- Enum name lookup: `Kind["TEXT"]` -> `Kind.TEXT`. CPython uses `EnumMeta.__getitem__` with a string key. C++ codegen: `EnumUtil<Kind>::from_name("TEXT")` (already exists in runtime). Needs subscript support on enum types in sema + codegen.
- properties master
- **[LOW] Async: support recursive inline `await` via an opt-in heap-allocated sub-future.** Self- and mutually-recursive inline `await` (`async def f(n): ... return await f(n-1)`; `ping`/`pong`) are rejected today (`async/error_async_{self,mutual,3cycle}_recursive_await`): an inline await stores the callee coro by value in the awaiter's frame (`std::optional<__coro_callee>`), so a cycle is infinite-size. The cycle is already detected by the topological coro-struct emit (`_emit_async_coro_structs`, `tpyc/codegen_cpp/generator.py`). Supporting recursion means heap-allocating the *cyclic* sub-future edge -- a pointer member (`std::unique_ptr<__coro_callee>` or a `Box[...]`) is fixed-size and works off the forward decl, breaking the cycle; emplace becomes a heap alloc, reads deref through the pointer. Only the back-edge that closes a cycle needs heaping; acyclic awaits stay by-value (zero-alloc preserved). **Allocation must be opt-in / non-silent** (it crosses the `@noalloc` zero-heap invariant; recursion inherently needs heap, like CPython frames). Open design question -- candidate spellings: (a) **`await Box(f(n-1))`** [lead -- reuse the existing `Box[T]` explicit-heap primitive at the exact await site; non-recursive `await f()` stays inline]; (b) a coro-level decorator `@recursive` / `@heap_recursion` [coarser, doesn't mark the alloc site]; (c) a `# tpy: heap_await` directive on the await line. Existing no-new-syntax escape hatch: drive the recursion through a `Task` (`asyncio.create_task` already heap-boxes the coro) -- which the reject diagnostic points to; this feature is the lighter-weight direct form. Runtime caveat: the poll chain nests (`poll(outer)`->`poll(sub)`->...), so deep recursion recurses through C++ `poll()` calls -> stack overflow at large depth (bounded recursion fine). Low priority; Task workaround exists. Needs `/tpy-add-feature` (the spelling is a real design decision). Surfaced by user review of the recursive-await reject.
- Generator: `yield from`, `send()`, `throw()`, `close()`
- Generator: protocol-typed params -- residual gaps. Multi-yield resumable-frame generators/coroutines with a static-protocol param (`def gen(it: Iterable[T])`) are DONE (H4, 2026-06-03): the for-loop iterator frame field is typed against the deduced template arg `T_<pname>` (the captured param), not the abstract concept. Follow-ups remain: (1) a protocol param *aliased into a local* then iterated across a suspension (`xs = it; for x in xs: yield x`) is now DONE for the resumable (multi-yield) path -- sema records a forwarding fact (`TpyFunction.forwarded_locals`) for a single-assignment bare-param alias, the local occupies no frame field, and codegen resolves every use to the captured param via `ctx.generator_storage_name`, reusing its `T_<pname>` deduction (generator: `iterators/gen_proto_param_aliased_local` + method variant; coroutine: `async/async_proto_param_aliased_local`; reassignment still rejected: `iterators/error_gen_proto_param_realiased_local`). Remaining sibling: aliasing an `Own[Awaitable[T]]` param then `await`-ing the alias (`aw = coro_param; await aw`) is moot today -- the await-operand restriction rejects awaiting a bare name (only a direct call / Task / Future / `__poll__` value is accepted), so the forwarding path is unreachable there; revisit if await-of-bare-name is ever supported. The non-param-sourced rejection branch and the alias-of-alias chain (`ys = xs`) are now covered by `iterators/error_gen_proto_param_alias_chain`. (2) simple (single-yield) proto-param generators are a separate concern (the lambda peephole tries `begin()/end()` instead of `__next__()`), and the alias case there is buggy (copies / miscompiles -- see BUGS.md); (3) `await consume(<collection literal>)` -- awaiting a protocol-param coroutine with a `[...]`/`{...}` literal arg directly -- is cleanly rejected (`async/error_async_await_proto_param_literal`); awaiting a *named* iterable works, and the **workaround now works** (bind the literal to a local first, then await -- `async/async_await_proto_param_local_bind`; the local-collection-in-coro crash that previously blocked it is fixed). The remaining gap is only the direct-literal ergonomic form, which would need the await arg hoisted into a frame field (extending the rvalue-temp await-arg hoist); the materialization target now exists.
- Generator: liveness optimization -- only promote yield-crossing variables to struct fields, keep others as stack locals in `__next__()` (currently all locals are promoted)
- Closures: `std::move_only_function` for `Callable` with `Own[T]` params/returns (design doc says to use it, currently uses `std::function` with rvalue params which works but is incorrect per C++23 semantics)
- Closures: `@noalloc` enforcement (Phase 5) -- `Callable` in `@noalloc` context should be rejected. Currently compiles without error.
- `@noalloc` does not flag heap allocations generally: a plain list literal (`xs = [1, 2, 3]`) and the coroutine erasure-boundary `make_adapter` allocation (create_task args, `-> Own[Cancellable[T]]` factory returns) both compile clean under `@noalloc` (probe-verified 2026-07-03). The Level-1 warn-on-allocation profile is the designed home for making the (signature-declared, deliberately marker-free) erasure-boundary allocations visible on demand -- when profile enforcement is built, include the make_adapter boundary class.
- `in` operator without `__contains__`: warn in `@hotpath`/`@noalloc` contexts. Falls back to O(n) linear iteration (`std::ranges::contains` for built-in NativeIterables, `::tpy::__iter__` + `__next__` for others), which is almost certainly not intended in perf-critical code. Users should define `__contains__` for O(1) lookup or be aware of the cost.
- Closures: method references (`obj.method` as a value) -- needs partial application binding `self`. Currently gives "has no field" error.
- Protocol isinstance in ternary expressions: `x = a.foo() if isinstance(a, P1) else a.bar()` generates a runtime `?:` but both branches must be valid C++ at template instantiation time. Fix: generate an IIFE with `if constexpr` inside, e.g. `[&]() -> T { if constexpr (P1<T_a>) { return a.foo(); } else { return a.bar(); } }()`. This also enables single-line field init in `__init__` (goes into the C++ member initializer list instead of requiring unconditional pre-assignment + reassignment in branches).
- Allow `@runtime_checkable` decorator on protocols (no-op in tpyc, enables CPython compatibility for isinstance checks on user-defined protocols)
- Nested patterns in match/case: `case Box(value=str() as v)` for disambiguating parameterized union members like `Box[str] | Box[int]`. Uses field guards with type sub-patterns -- standard Python match syntax, CPython-compatible.
- allow type annotation to use "" (forward decl)
- **Unpacking a `list` (and any non-tuple sequence).** `a, b, c = line.split("\t")` is rejected with `Cannot unpack non-tuple type Own[list[str]]`; unpacking is tuple-only today. Since `split()` returns a `list`, this hits essentially every line-parsing program, and the workaround is indexing each element. Needs a runtime length check to match CPython's `ValueError: not enough values to unpack` -- which is the design question worth settling first (panic vs raise, and whether a statically-known-length source can elide the check). Surfaced by a downstream port.
- **printf-style `%` formatting on `str` (`str.__mod__`).** `"%.2f" % x` is rejected with `Invalid operand types for '%': str and float`, so every such site must become an f-string. Reported downstream as "the single most common change across all three ports" -- so even though f-strings cover the functionality, the absence is the most frequent source of edits when bringing existing Python over. Scope decision needed: the full `%` mini-language (flags/width/precision/`%s`/`%r`/`%d`/`%f`/`%x`, tuple and dict right operands) or a compile-time-format-string-only subset that lowers to the same machinery f-strings already use.
- **Implicit `return None` when a function falls off the end.** TPy requires a `return` on every path (`'f' can reach the end of the function without returning a value`), which is a reasonable design stance, but Python code routinely relies on the implicit `None` -- two functions in a downstream `adatron` port needed unreachable terminal returns added. Worth deciding explicitly: keep the strictness for annotated non-`None` returns (where falling off the end is nearly always a bug) but allow it where the declared return type includes `None`, which is the shape that actually appears in ported code.

## Documentation
- **[docs] One list of the INTENDED divergences from CPython: `docs/CPYTHON_DIVERGENCES.md`.** Today they are scattered: README's four structural bullets (annotations, `int32` literals, value vs reference types with `Own[T]`, no GC), ~36 inline "acknowledged/declared divergence" notes in `docs/LANGUAGE_FEATURES.md`, and a per-feature section in each design doc (`CLOSURES_CALLABLE_DESIGN.md` IX, `DYNAMIC_ATTRS_DESIGN.md`, `EXCEPTION_DESIGN.md`, `MATCH_CASE_DESIGN.md`, `DATETIME_DESIGN.md`, `CONSUMING_ITERATION_DESIGN.md`, the container cliff in `CPYTHON_INTEROP.md`). A reader cannot see in one place what TPy does differently on purpose -- the closure by-value snapshot (a rebind after the capture is invisible to the closure, in sync bodies AND inside a generator/async frame) is the kind of entry nobody knows about until the warning fires. Shape: one bullet per intended divergence -- the trigger, the warning it emits (or "silent, documented only"), the escape hatch, the doc it comes from; the four README items included. UNINTENDED or silent divergences are bugs and stay in `BUGS.md` (their "(silent CPython divergence)" tag), never in this list; a divergence found silent while compiling the list is filed there. Write it in a docs-only branch; keep it current afterwards the way `LANGUAGE_FEATURES.md` is.
- **[LOW] Reconcile isinstance status in FEATURE_ROADMAP / UNION_TYPES_DESIGN.** `docs/FEATURE_ROADMAP.md` (~line 208, ~520) and `docs/UNION_TYPES_DESIGN.md` (~line 52) still list the `isinstance(x, (A, B))` tuple form (and isinstance-on-alias) as "not done" / "design only" -- stale pre-existing drift: the tuple form has long shipped, and the inline-union form (`isinstance(x, A | B)`) plus the union-alias-name rejection now exist too. `LANGUAGE_FEATURES.md` is current; these design docs lag. Surfaced by /tpy-review (docs-sync) of the inline-union isinstance feature.
- language restriction documentation
- `tpy --print-types`: internal modules (`tpy._bootstrap.*`, `tpy._builtins.*`, `tpy._core.*`, `tpy._typing`) are shown as top-level sections because that's where the real class/function bodies live. Users import names like `int32`, `Own`, `Span` from `tpy` (via re-exports in `tpy/__init__.py`), so seeing them under `tpy._core._types` is both noisy and slightly misleading (the import path is "wrong"). Hiding the `_*` modules outright removes visibility of every builtin type -- fix properly requires walking re-export chains: when `tpy/__init__.py` does `from ._core import int32`, attribute `int32` to the `tpy` section (with a note on where it's defined) and hide the underlying `_core/_types` entry. Non-trivial: needs import resolution across the package tree in `tpyc/dump_types.py`.

## Type System
- **[LOW] A `Diagnostic` carries one `SourceLocation`, so a verdict decided at one site and reported at another cannot name both.** The owning-slot copy contract (`tpyc/sema/own_copy.py`) hedges at the BODY line, which is right for the warning -- but a non-copyable instantiation (`@nocopy`, or a record with `__del__`) PROMOTES that same line to an error, and the instantiation that caused the promotion is somewhere else. A user then reads `lib/tpy/itertools.py:38: error: cannot copy non-copyable type 'Pinned' into owned storage` with no pointer to which of their calls made it non-copyable. The same shape recurs wherever a deferred verdict lands (`bound_check.py` chose the opposite trade and reports at the call site instead, losing the body line). A second, optional `related` location on `Diagnostic` -- rendered as a `note:` line rather than embedded in the message text, which no committed `diag.txt` does -- would let both be named. `CLAUDE.md`'s LSP invariants already want structured locations. Surfaced landing the owning-slot copy contract.
- **[design] Dedicated `tpy::bytes` C++ type so `bytes` is a C++-level value type like `str`.** TPy-level `bytes` is a value type (immutable, copy unobservable), but its C++ backing is a bare `std::vector<uint8_t>` -- which cannot be specialized `is_value_type` because `list[uint8]` maps to the SAME C++ type and is a reference type. So every C++ generic-convention trait (`val_or_ref_t`, `param_val_or_ref_t`, ...) classifies `bytes` as a reference at instantiation, diverging from `str` (whose `std::string` backing IS a C++ value type). The async task layer sidestepped this via `run`/`wait_for`'s `-> Own[T]` re-sign (case `async_run_returns_bytes` pins it), but any other generic `-> T` / `T`-slot instantiated at `bytes` still takes the reference branch. Fix shape: a thin `tpy::bytes` wrapper over the vector (the `std::string`-analog role), carrying `is_value_type<tpy::bytes> = true` -- disambiguates from `list[uint8]` and makes the str/bytes symmetry complete (BytesView already mirrors StrView). Churn: every `bytes`-touching emitted C++ re-keys (whole-suite exec re-verify); the runtime bytes_ops surface moves onto the wrapper. Needs `/tpy-add-feature`. Surfaced reviewing the async borrow-return ABI's bytes-through-run fix.
- **[design] Sub-default-int arithmetic: promote, or keep width-preserving?** Today fixed-int arithmetic is width-preserving and checked: `int8 + int8 -> int8` via `add_check<int8_t>` (panics on overflow), with explicit `add_wrap`/`shl_wrap`/... statics as the deliberate-wraparound escape hatch (`lib/tpy/tpy/_core/_types.py` stub dunders). That is Rust's model; C++ instead promotes anything narrower than `int` to `int` before arithmetic, so C++ never computes in int8. The user-visible consequence: narrow-typed values are hostile to ordinary arithmetic (`dt.hour * 3600` in int8 needs explicit `int(...)` widening), which blocks packing value-type fields (datetime/time could shrink 28->12 / 16->8 bytes with int8/int16 fields, like CPython's C datetime does internally -- the motivating case; boundaries/ctor args stay `int` regardless, the validate-in-BigInt-then-store contract is orthogonal). Three candidate shapes: (a) full C++-style promotion of sub-default-int operands to the default int -- but C++'s own experience says this is hated in byte-manipulation code (`b[i] & 0x0F` promoting forces casts back into byte buffers; TPy's stdlib -- base64/hashlib/struct/socket -- is full of width-preserving uint8 ops), and bitwise-vs-arithmetic split rules would be a third rulebook; (b) promote only MIXED-width operands (`int8 + int32 -> int32`), keeping same-width ops closed and byte code cast-free; (c) status quo plus range-proven implicit narrowing on assignment (value_range), which fixes the packed-field read ergonomics without touching arithmetic rules. Churn if (a): retypes stub dunders -> stdlib emitted C++ changes (whole-suite exec re-key), ~42 test cases + 13 stdlib files use sub-int32 types, dozens-100+ snapshots, plus a rejects-valid ripple (`c: int8 = a + b` needs a narrowing story, aug-assign too). THIR: not structurally blocked (typing is sema-side, upstream of both codegen paths; the byte-diff gate moves in lockstep) but THIR unit tests pin current `add_check<intN_t>` emits and the value-scalar slice is under active development -- sequence this after the current THIR increments settle. Needs `/tpy-add-feature` (typing-rule change across all fixed-int code). Surfaced by the datetime v2 field-packing question.
- **[feature] Class type-param defaults with an arbitrary default type** -- support `@type_param_default(C=int) class Counter[T: Hashable, C: AnyInt]: ...` (or the PEP 696 native `class Counter[T: Hashable, C: AnyInt = int]`). Two gaps today: (1) `@type_param_default` is FUNCTION-only -- on a class it errors `Unknown macro 'type_param_default'` (the `RecordInfo.type_param_defaults` field exists but isn't wired through class registration/resolution); (2) the default can only be the `DefaultInt` sentinel -> the *configured* default int (int32), since `type_ops.py` (~1385) handles only `qnames.DEFAULT_INT` and raises on anything else -- so it cannot default to a concrete type like `int`/BigInt. The PEP 696 native syntax `[T, C = int]` is a Python 3.13 feature (env is 3.12 -> parse error), so it's blocked until the min-Python bump. Motivating use: a parametric *count type* for `collections.Counter` (`Counter[Object, int32]` for cheap fixed-width histograms) while `Counter[T]` keeps `C` defaulting to `int` (arbitrary precision, CPython-matching -- defaulting to int32 would silently change overflow behavior). Needs the `AnyInt` protocol (above) for the `C` bound. Benefits any generic container wanting a defaulted param (`Box`, `ArrayList`, future `defaultdict`), not just Counter. Surfaced by the Counter parametric-count-type question. Needs `/tpy-add-feature`.
- **[design] Should a NAMED union alias become its own struct?** `type Shape = int32 | float64` renders `using Shape = ::tpy::Union<int32_t, double>;` -- a transparent alias, so `Shape` has no identity of its own in C++. Making a named alias a struct instead would give it a place for `__repr__`, `__str__` and any future `Equatable` / `Hashable` conformance (the missing conformance is `BUGS.md#value-union-no-equatable-conformance`), at the cost of a much larger change: the alias stops converting implicitly to and from its members' variant, every use site re-keys, and the recursive-alias wrapper (which already IS such a struct) would want to merge with it rather than sit beside it. Not proposed, but it is the question `::tpy::Union` invites next, and the answer decides whether `Union` should have been a struct at all or could have been an alias template. Surfaced by the `::tpy::Union` redesign.
- `is_trivially_destructible()`: current approximation uses `is_value_type() and not is_expensive_copy()`, which is conservative for non-value types (e.g. Span, SpanIter are trivially destructible but return False). Proper implementation: primitives/views/pointers always trivial; records trivial if no `__del__` and all fields/bases are trivially destructible; tuples/optionals trivial if elements are. Used by `del` codegen to elide move-sink.

## Refactor
- **[LOW] Give the AST node classes identity equality (`@dataclass(eq=False)`) and key the identity tables on the node itself.** `tpyc/identity_map.py` keys on `id(key)` internally and holds the key beside the value, which is sound but costs a tuple per entry and keeps a parallel container surface alive. The reason it exists at all is that `TpyExpr` / `TpyStmt` and friends (`tpyc/parse/nodes.py`) are plain `@dataclass`es: the generated `__eq__` sets `__hash__` to None, so a node cannot be a dict key. `eq=False` restores identity hashing, after which `IdentityMap` becomes a plain dict (or a `WeakKeyDictionary` where the fact should die with the node). Not mechanical: it changes `==` on every AST node globally, so it needs a survey of every structural comparison of nodes before it can land, and it is a separate change-set from the ownership fix. Surfaced converting the `id()`-keyed side tables 2026-09-10.
- **[LOW] The `id()`-keyed containers left as sound rest on an unstated co-ownership invariant.** After the identity-map conversion the remaining raw `id()` keys are of two kinds: local recursion guards / worklists whose keyed objects are alive for the whole call (`seen` in `sema/calls.py`, `in_degree` / `reverse_adj` in `sema/mutation_propagation.py`, `_seen` in `sema/frame_traits.py`, `top_level_ids` / `plan` in `thir/lower/resumable.py`, ...), and tables co-owned by something else that pins the keys -- `ResumableFuncState.for_uid_map` / `with_uid_map` / `try_finally_uid_map` and `CFGBuilder._handler_entries` (keys reachable from `func.body`, and the state hangs off `func`), `THIRMatchArm.body_key` (a `case.body` list held by the module AST), `OwnCopyEdge.key()` (the edge holds its callee). Each is sound only while that owner exists, and nothing says so at the container. Either add the one-line WHY at each, or convert them too and stop reasoning about it. Surfaced converting the `id()`-keyed side tables 2026-09-10.
- **[LOW][THIR] List literal elements render bare while set and Array elements retype to the slot -- a mirrored AST accident, keyed on the container kind.** The `retype` predicate in `_lower_expr_impl`'s container-literal arm (`tpyc/thir/lower/expressions.py`, `retype = isinstance(e, TpySetLiteral) or (is_array(...) and array_retype)`) and the `array_retype` flag threaded through `_lower_expr` exist only to reproduce the deleted AST emitter's split: `{1, 2}` into a `vector<BigInt>` stays bare, `ordered_set<BigInt>({::tpy::BigInt(1)})` and an Array decl spell each element. Retyping every scalar element the same way deletes the flag (4 signatures, 9 sites), the kind key and the comment justifying it, and makes each element an exact match for its slot so no consumer's overload set can reinterpret the brace (the member-init cell now spells its container type for that reason; an element spelling would make that belt-and-braces). Render-only: about 150 cases regenerate (`= {1, 2}` becomes `= {::tpy::BigInt(1), ::tpy::BigInt(2)}`). Sequenced AFTER the use-channel consolidation lands, since `array_retype` is a per-position flag on `_lower_expr` of exactly the kind that work is folding into `_ExprUse`.
- **[LOW] `UnionType`'s docstring promises an ordering one of its own constructors deliberately breaks.** It states members are stored in canonical sorted order with `NoneType` first, and that held while every union was built through the canonicalizing constructor. Sema now stands a recursive alias in as a `UnionType` built from the wrapper's `alternatives()` VERBATIM, precisely because that tuple fixes the emitted variant's member ordering and must not be re-sorted -- so a reader who trusts the docstring will mis-predict that instance. Nothing at the type marks the exemption. Fix shape: say on the type which orderings are guaranteed and which construction path opts out, or give the stand-in its own spelling so the invariant stays unconditional on `UnionType` itself. Surfaced by the /tpy-ready second opinion of the body-diagnostic re-homing.
- **[MED][THIR] A `RecursiveAliasInstanceType` at a value position folds the body, at six positions and counting -- and the trigger is the alias slot, NOT a `None` value.** A first survey read the trigger as the `None` leaf (`x: Tree[None] = None` -> `decl.none_init_slot`; `x: Tree[None] = [None, ...]` -> `container_lit.slot_family`; `xs.append(None)` -> `method.arg_shape`; `take(None)` -> `call.arg_shape.other_recursivealiasinstancetype`; `self.t = None` in a ctor -> `ctor.mil_field.recursivealiasinstance.noneliteral`). Measured against two controls that name no `None` at all, that reading is WRONG: `branches.append([])` folds at the same `method.arg_shape`, and `branches.pop()` folds at `method.ret_type`. So the shape is a recursive-alias instance appearing as a method argument, a method return, a call argument, a declaration slot, a container element, or a ctor field init -- `None` merely makes it easy to reach. The nearby handled arm renders `std::monostate{}` via a predicate requiring a plain `UnionType` whose wrapper is needed; a generic alias instance is a distinct type and is not reduced to one, so it falls through. The AST emits the same render the handled arm would, which is what makes this look like a predicate gap rather than a missing render -- but confirm that per position rather than assuming it from the None one. Reachability rose sharply when sema stopped collapsing such an alias into an optional, since matching one is now legal and such programs naturally hold one. `tests/cases/match/union_recursive_none_leaf` is written around the gap (no value ever crosses one of these positions) and says so at the top; widening the lowering is what lets that case carry the arm it currently omits. Surfaced adding coverage for the newly-accepted recursive-alias match subject.

Both spellings produce the identical diagnostic today -- the fold re-emits and the same skeleton check fires -- so nothing distinguishes them from the outside, and no corpus case carries the variant one, which is why the ratchet never sees the fold. The cost is deferred rather than absent: a folded body has no emitter once the emitters are gone. Fix shape: lower the variant-union condition operand, or establish that the shape is unreachable and say so where the fold is decided. Surfaced building the routing pin for the walrus/temp reject -- a first fixture written against the variant shape read as a false alarm until the fold was measured.

- Give an escaping loop-body local per-iteration storage, closing the acknowledged divergence. A local declared in a loop body and bound to a longer-lived name hoists to ONE function-scope slot, so the outer name observes later rebinds (LANGUAGE_FEATURES "Scope Escape Detection"); the warning states this and names `copy()`, and the specific wrong-value shapes are in BUGS.md. Closing it needs storage per BINDING, and every mechanism costs something the source does not show. THREE were prototyped and discarded, all fully working -- do not re-derive them: (1) a per-iteration heap arena (`std::deque`), killed because an EMPTY deque costs 2 allocations and it retains every iteration's object to function exit; (2) copy-at-escape, matching what field and container boundaries already do -- zero allocation and sibling-consistent, but it silently drops aliasing, so mutation through one name stops being visible through the other; (3) a two-slot rotation keyed on a "handed out" flag -- correct aliasing, zero allocation, one predictable branch, byte-measured in the noise for any loop constructing a non-trivial object, but a runtime state machine the source does not show, and it serves exactly ONE alias (two targets can hold two slots at once, so the generalization needs a held-bitmask over k+1 slots). A fourth option, rejecting the shape outright, was built and reverted: it is zero-cost and honest but refuses idiomatic Python, and a measured scan of ~30k functions (CPython stdlib + site-packages) found the shape only about SEVEN times, so the reject bought little at a real usability cost. If this is picked up, (3) is the cheapest revival. Effort: M.
- Unify block-local reassignment onto ONE C++ object. A local first declared inside a block and assigned after it currently emits TWO C++ declarations for one Python local (`int32_t n` in the loop body, a second `int32_t n = 9;` after it) -- correct today, because a READ after the block instead takes sema's pending-loop-var promotion (one pre-declared object), because an escaping alias has its STORAGE hoisted to function scope so the block-scoped thing is only the binding, and because the two declarations are now required to share ONE TYPE (the one-type-per-local check rejects a second type across the block boundary), so they can differ only in identity, never in shape. But Python's model is one local, and the compiler already emits that on the read path; the split exists only because the promotion path is currently the buggier of the two (it emits the promoted binding const, breaking a reference-typed loop var's later rebind, and it reuses one hoisted slot per NAME rather than per binding, which clobbers escaped aliases -- both filed in BUGS.md). Routing writes through promotion collapses it to a single object -- verified, `in_for` emits one `int32_t n;` with both sites assigning -- but ONLY once the alias-clobber entry is genuinely fixed: with the collapse on top of today's slot model, `block_local_reassign_after_record::escaped_alias` returns 909 instead of 209, because one object means one hoisted slot and the post-loop rebind overwrites what the escaped alias points at. That entry is harder than it looks (its obvious fix regresses destructor timing -- see BUGS.md), so this stays gated behind it. Surfaced answering a review question on the block-local scope-revoke fix. Effort: M, gated on the two BUGS entries.
- **[cleanup] `_declare_rebind_slot` (`tpyc/thir/emit.py`) hardcodes the `__slot_` prefix and omits the `static` keyword.** The AST's `ctx.declare_rebind_slot` derives both from the emission scope (`slots.global_scope` -> `static `, `slot_prefix`); the THIR mirror spells `std::optional<T> __slot_{n};` literally, so a module-scope slot would come out non-static and named `__slot_` instead of `__global_slot_`. Unreachable today -- every call site is preceded by `state.assert_local_slot()`, which fails before a module-scope body gets there, and lowering rejects the top-level shapes anyway -- but `assert` vanishes under `python -O`, and the AST's own `static` branch is equally unreachable, so this is symmetry cleanup rather than a latent bug. Do it before top-level lowering is widened to admit slot-allocating shapes. Effort: XS.
- **[feature] Give a generator's rebind slot frame lifetime via a lambda init-capture, accepting the shape the cross-scope reject now refuses.** A local declared before a generator's loop and rvalue-rebound inside it is rejected (`use_rebind_slot`, `tpyc/codegen_cpp/context.py`) because the slot has no sound home: inside the lambda it dies each invocation while the captured pointer outlives it, outside it the lambda cannot name it. An init-capture (`[..., __slot_N = std::optional<T>{}]`) gives the slot generator-frame lifetime. The peephole already does exactly this for `__beg` / `__end` / `__init` / `__src` (`tpyc/codegen_cpp/gen_generators.py`), so the mechanism exists -- this is wiring the rebind slot into it plus deciding the THIR mirror (the shape currently falls back). **Fixes the LIFETIME half only -- it does not make the program match CPython.** A frame-lifetime slot is still ONE slot, so a rebind per loop iteration overwrites the object a live alias holds: routing the same shape to the resumable frame (which already gives the slot frame lifetime) yields `0 1 2` where CPython yields `11 0 1`. So this entry buys sound storage for `BUGS.md`'s captured-pointer UAF, not parity, and it does NOT retire the reject on its own -- see the entry below. ACCEPTS programs that are rejected today, so it needs the /tpy-add-feature design gate. Effort: M.
- **[DIAGNOSTIC LANDED 2026-09-10; the semantic half stays open] One diagnostic for rebinding a local while a live alias points at it.** The warning is `tpyc/sema/alias_rebind.py` (`storage_generations` + per-loan residency on `BorrowTracker` + a liveness stamp on the rebind statement), pinned by `records/warn_alias_rebind_clobber` and `records/alias_rebind_no_warning`; `BUGS.md`'s sync-loop-alias, `BUGS.md#resumable-alias-identity`, nested-def-local and module-scope entries all warn now and all stay open, because the VALUE is still wrong. Closing that is the slot-model work (implemented and reverted 2026-07-27 -- read the `BUGS.md` entry before re-attempting), and it consumes the SAME fact: when it lands, the resumable leg of `storage_generations` stops answering 1 and the warnings retire on their own.

  **DECIDED 2026-09-11: the semantic half is the ALIAS-GATED slot model, scheduled directly after the peephole deletion (item below).** At a rebind, if nothing live aliases the value in the slot, reuse the slot (today's render, exact drop timing); if something does, the rebind takes its own storage and the old object lives on -- parity in both legs, since CPython does not drop under a live alias either. The may-alias answer is the loan the diagnostic already reads (`BorrowTracker.loans` + residency + the loop-body carry); the default on an unknown is ALIASED (costs drop timing, never a wrong value). Per-site slots (aliasing fixed, drop timing lost -- the 2026-07-27 revert) and heap-boxing (hidden allocation) stay ruled out. This is sema-side may-alias reasoning built on the string-keyed tracker; the MIR loan checker (`docs/IR_DESIGN.md`) supersedes both the tracker and this gate when it lands, and that is accepted: the gate is the interim fix, not the destination. Goes after the deletion so it is designed for ONE generator storage model.

  Two claims in the original entry were wrong and are corrected here. (a) It is NOT "replacing the generator-only cross-scope reject": `generators/error_gen_rebind_slot_crosses_lambda` and `error_gen_rebind_slot_after_drain` carry no alias at all -- they pin a lambda-slot-scope hazard, and BOTH shapes are correct on the resumable frame (probed 2026-09-10, byte-equal to CPython), so `reject_rebind_slot_crosses_scope` retires with the PEEPHOLE (item below), not with this diagnostic. Fold the two into one happy-path `generators/rebind_before_loop` there. (b) "the straight-line SINGLE rebind is CORRECT today" is sync-only: on a resumable frame, at module scope and in a non-colliding nested def the storage holds ONE generation, so the first rebind already clobbers -- which is why the rule keys on `storage_generations`, not on a rebind count.

Hardest: its obvious fix was implemented and reverted (drop-timing tension), so do it last -- as the alias-gated slot model decided 2026-09-11 (the diagnostic entry above), which is the next item once the peephole is gone.

A non-unpack tuple LOOP VAR now points at the source element tuple (`std::tuple<int32_t, A>* t;`, `t = &(*(it)++);`), the same holder the tuple-unpack sibling emits, so one field serves the reference-element and all-value shapes and a mutation through the loop var aliases the source; the dict_items proxy keeps its `tuple_to_pointer` borrow tuple (its prvalue cannot be address-taken) and its all-value variant is admitted at the advance. A tuple bound to a frame local owns PER INIT: each init yields one per-element verdict at the site that classifies it (`init_verdict` in `tpyc/codegen_cpp/context.py`) and the join across a name's inits only merges verdicts. A literal owns the elements it VALUE-captures; an owning call owns what its return type hands over (`Own[tuple[...]]` -> every reference element, a per-element `tuple[Own[A], B]` -> exactly its `Own` slots); everything else borrows. So a literal and an owning call in either order join to one owning slot, and a reassigned owning-call tuple emplaces fresh storage into that same slot. The verdict is expressed as an `Own[...]`-marked effective type that routes into the existing OWNING / MIXED / BORROW frame kinds. Cases `iterators/gen_tuple_loop_var_whole`, `tuple/tuple_literal_frame_local_forms`. Two residuals gate bin (c): `yield t` of a WHOLE owning slot rejects at the yield (`res.btuple_yield_source` -- handing the slot out of the frame has no arm; `tuple/tuple_local_own_member_yield` builds forced-off up to that point), and an alias to an ELEMENT of an owning slot survives a rebind of the slot with the wrong value and no diagnostic (`BUGS.md#resumable-alias-identity`).

- **[cleanup] A generator's simplicity should be a registered fact, not a peer module's AST re-inspected at codegen time.** `GeneratorCodegen._module_generator` (`tpyc/codegen_cpp/gen_generators.py`) reaches through `get_current_compiler().modules[<module>].ast` to hand a peer module's `TpyFunction` to the body-inspecting `is_simple_generator`, so the delegation gate re-derives a verdict the defining module already reached. It should be decided once where it is decided -- a field on `FunctionInfo`, the way `reach_analysis` facts ride on `ModuleExports` -- so codegen never reads another module's AST. Same shape as the `[thir][perf]` resumable-factory-temp entry, which wants the peephole verdict on `FunctionInfo` for the call site. Retires with the simple-generator peephole deletion anyway (no generator is simple afterwards, so the gate goes), so do it only if that deletion slips. Surfaced by /tpy-review of the cross-module delegation fix.
- **[hardening] Frame ptr-slot prescan: structural agreement with the emit arms.** Two lockstep risks in the per-site frame-slot machinery, both currently safe by convention or coincidence rather than structure: (a) `ptr_slot_field_type` (`tpyc/codegen_cpp/statements.py`) re-derives `_gen_pointer_local_rebind`'s routing conditions instead of the emit arms consulting one classifier for their own branching -- the dangerous direction (slot-needing write with no prescanned field) raises loud, but over-reservation drifts silently into dead fields; (b) the prescan runs before `setup_body_scope` seeds `optional_locals` / `storage_form_optional_locals` / `current_func_params`, so its `needs_optional_to_ptr_lift` / `is_storage_form_optional_source` reads see stale per-body state -- today every divergence collapses to "no slot" on both sides only because `is_rvalue_source(TpyName)` is unconditionally False. Fix shape: extend the seed-before-prescan block that `_build_resumable_cfg` already has for `var_types`/`const_ref_params` (added for exactly this risk class) to those sets, and restructure the emit arms to branch on the shared classifier's verdict. Zero observable change today -- deliberately deferred off the fix branch as untestable churn. Surfaced by /tpy-review (architecture-fit) of the frame ptr-slot placement fix.
- **[perf] Suspension-liveness-precise view promotion for frame locals.** The frame view-local owned promotion (`ViewVarInfo.frame_unsafe_source` + the `in_resumable` term in `_resolve_pending_view_types`) is deliberately coarser than liveness -- it promotes any non-static-sourced str/bytes view local in ANY generator/async body. Three refinements, all perf-only (the coarse rule is the safe direction): (a) a loop var in a loop containing NO suspension point copies per iteration where the view was already safe (`resumable_view_loopvar`'s `words_gen` now does `std::string w = *__beg_0` each pass) -- needs a per-local "crosses a suspension" fact at resolution time; (b) a local aliasing an `is_owned_in_coro_frame`-captured param (plain `str`/`bytes`) could stay a view of the frame's owned field (durable), though param REBIND then dangles it, so this needs a no-rebind fact too; (c) simple-generator lambda-peephole bodies promote like resumable frames although their locals live on the lambda stack -- but sema cannot see codegen's `is_simple_generator` choice, and the peephole is slated for deletion (the TRACK above), so (c) likely resolves itself. Sema-side suspension liveness is the real prerequisite for (a)/(b); revisit post-THIR where the frame layout is already a queryable plan. Surfaced by /tpy-review (codegen-correctness + architecture-fit + safety-model) of the frame view-local promotion fix.
- **[thir hardening] `lower_top_level`'s lambda-hoist protection is incidental, not stated.** The three deliberate rejection points for a rebind slot a lambda-rendered body cannot reach (`lower_function`, `lower_constructor`, `lower_simple_generator`, all via `_rejects_lambda_hoist` / `_needs_held_back_slot` in `tpyc/thir/lower/functions.py`) do NOT include `lower_top_level`. It is safe today only because `_rejects_global_slot` happens to inspect `THIRPtrLocalRebind` nodes as well -- a predicate whose docstring and maintenance contract are about GLOBAL-scope memory safety, not lambda placement. Nothing ties the two invariants together, so widening that predicate's allow-list for an unrelated reason would silently drop the coverage. Related: THIR's emit side has no analogue of the AST's `hoist_scope_id` / `rebind_slot_scopes` runtime check (a single flat `hoist_lines` list per function, no per-nested-def scoping), so the upfront predicate is the ENTIRE protection -- which is why one omission in it was directly reachable, THIR being the only author. Either apply `_rejects_lambda_hoist` at `lower_top_level` too, or give the emit side the scope check. Surfaced by the /tpy-ready targeted safety-model pass. Effort: S.
- **[thir hardening] Two hoist-write paths sit outside `_needs_held_back_slot`'s scope, and two generator shapes render outside their lambda sink.** The predicate (`tpyc/thir/lower/functions.py`) covers the emit sites that call `_declare_rebind_slot`, which is what its three rejection points key on. Not covered: (a) `RECORD_HOISTED`'s unconditional `std::optional<T> __slot_N;` and the `DYN_PROTOCOL` rebind (`tpyc/thir/emit.py`) append to `state.hoist_lines` DIRECTLY, guarded only by `assert state.hoist_drainable` -- inside a nested-def body that reproduces the ctor/lambda placement divergence, and inside a simple-generator body it raises rather than falling back; (b) in the direct-iterator and universal-default `for` shapes (`tpyc/codegen_cpp/gen_generators.py`), `iterable_code` / `src_code` are rendered BEFORE `_lambda_body_sink` opens but consumed inside the lambda, so a slot reserved by that render would drain to the enclosing function prologue -- the same non-captured shape; those two shapes also place drained declarations after their `auto __r = ...` line rather than at the lambda top (legal, but untested). No constructible repro for either, so both are latent -- but this is the exact class that produced three build-breaking regressions and a ctor divergence, each found only after the fact. Surfaced by the /tpy-merge-master semantic hunt. Effort: S.
- **[cleanup] The rebind-slot registration chokepoint is not enforced.** `ctx.declare_rebind_slot` is the single entry point for a PRE-declared slot (one that may never be consumed), but `rebind_slots` stays a plain public dict that nine sites write directly -- legitimately, since they allocate at a rebind site or register an already-declared init slot for reuse, so nothing can go unconsumed. The distinction lives only in the helper's docstring. A future site that pre-declares without routing through the helper would silently reintroduce the dead-local class the helper exists to prevent. The companion invariant is newer and sharper: a held-back declaration must have a reachable drain site -- `nested_hoist_scope` / `_lambda_body_sink` supply one per lambda-rendered body, and nothing structurally stops a future body emitter from omitting it. Effort: S.
- **[test-coverage] The rebind slot's "separate storage" half is only alias-tested for the plain pointer-local shape.** `records/rebind_slot_alias_survives` proves an alias taken before an rvalue rebind still observes mutation on the ORIGINAL (the point of the two-slot split) -- but only for the plain record/`Optional` pointer-local. The sibling emit shapes the same machinery serves -- union monostate rebind (`UNION_RVALUE`/`UNION_ADDR`), `to_ptr_variant` lvalue/rvalue locals, and the branch-hoist (`RECORD_HOISTED`) form -- are covered only for the "no dead declaration" direction, incidentally, by regenerated snapshots (`union/union_none_reassign`, `operators/op_borrow_branch_hoist`, `generics/generic_optional_none_join`). A silent copy or a shared slot at those boundaries would read clean, since a read-only snapshot is parity-blind. The plain union rebind is writable today; the `@error_return` variant is blocked on the ptr-variant bridge miscompile in BUGS.md. Effort: S.
- Mark codegen's intentionally-unread locals `[[maybe_unused]]` and drop the name-blind `-Wno-unused-variable` / `-Wno-unused-but-set-variable` suppressions (`tpyc/toolchain.py` `_COMMON_WARN_FLAGS`). Today the suppressions are global, so a codegen-emitted dead local is as invisible as the user's legitimate `x = compute()` with no read. Emitting the attribute at the declaration site keeps the "users never see C++ warnings" invariant while letting the C++ compiler flag the artifacts we did NOT mark. Scope note from a g++ probe: `-Wunused-variable` does NOT fire on any `std::optional<T>` declaration -- GCC skips the warning for non-trivial ctor/dtor types, and `optional`'s default ctor is user-provided -- so this catches dead PLAIN-SCALAR temps (tuple-unpack, `error_return`); dead rebind slots are structurally impossible now that their declaration is held back until a rebind consumes it. Effort: S.
- The precompiled stdlib `.o` set omits package `__init__` modules. `_discover_stdlib_imports` (`tests/conftest.py`) skips every `__init__.py` on the grounds that "parent package import brings these in" -- but a package's own `__init__` is the only way to reach it, so `asyncio`, `http`, `os`, `urllib`, `tplib`, `tpy.coro`, `tplib.json` are absent from the shared `.o` cache despite the docstring's "every importable runtime module", and every case importing them recompiles them per-case. Perf-only. Widening it re-keys every case's exec marker (the cache's `output_hash` covers the whole set), so it wants its own change. Effort: S.
- Wrap the codegen block-scope snapshot/restore pair in a contextmanager. `snapshot_local_scope()` / `restore_local_scope()` are now hand-paired at ~9 sites (`_gen_if` and its elif/else arms, `_gen_while` body and else, `_gen_loop_body`, the for-else arm, `_gen_try_finally_only`, `_gen_try_return` handlers, `_gen_try_throw` body and handlers, `match.py::_emit_case_body`) -- a `with self.ctx.block_scope():` helper (mirroring the existing `nested_def_emission_scope` pattern) would make it harder to miss a site, which is exactly how the loop-`else` arms were missed until review. Not all sites can be wrapped: a few restore mid-block rather than at the block close. Surfaced by /tpy-review (architecture-fit) of the block-local scope-revoke fix. Effort: S.
- `directly_implements_dynamic` (`tpyc/codegen_cpp/protocols.py`) only checks DIRECT `implemented_protocols`, so a user class that inherits a `@dynamic` protocol transitively through a concrete ancestor (`class Dog(Animal)` where `class Animal(Cloneable)`) is NOT recognized as implementing `Cloneable` directly. Codegen then wraps `Dog()` into an `Own[Cloneable]` slot via `make_unique<Adapter<Cloneable, Dog>>(...)` instead of the leaner `make_unique<Dog>(...)` -- both compile and run correctly (Dog IS-A Cloneable through C++ inheritance, so the Adapter indirection is unnecessary), but the Adapter form is a wasted allocation + indirection layer. Fix: walk `(record, *iter_ancestor_records(record)).implemented_protocols` (transitively) and drop the `is_native` exclusion (the comment claiming `@native` C++ structs don't inherit their declared protocol is stale -- `tpy::BaseException : tpy::Throwable` in core.hpp:35 does inherit). Pure optimization; changes the snapshot for `infer_const_dynamic_transitive` (Adapter -> concrete). Surfaced during the covariant-return exploration (dropped); this widening was the one independently-valuable codegen finding from it. Effort: XS + snapshot regen.
- **[cleanup] Fold the record-dunder binop fallback into OperatorResolver.** `sema/expressions.py` `_analyze_binop`'s record path (~line 1343, reached when `operators.resolve_binop` returns None) constructs a `FunctionInfo`/`ResolvedBinop` from scratch, independently of `OperatorResolver._make_resolved` -- the operator-dunder borrow-return fix had to thread `is_readonly` and `canonical_fi` into BOTH constructions, and any future fact added to the primary path risks being missed on the fallback. Fold the fallback's param-match nuances into `resolve_binop` so there is one construction site. Surfaced by /tpy-review (architecture-fit) of the operator-dunder borrow-return fix.
- Unify comparison operator codegen with arithmetic: comparisons (`==`, `!=`, `<`, etc.) now resolve through `BINOP_TO_METHOD` + `resolved_binop` like arithmetic ops, but two issues remain: (1) `DUNDER_CPP_TEMPLATES` in `operators.py` duplicates `DUNDER_TO_BINARY_OP` in `codegen_cpp/context.py` -- both map dunder names to C++ operators. Consolidate into one table or derive templates from the operator character. (2) The comparison codegen section still has its own special cases (BigInt/float cast, IntEnum coercion, Optional unwrap, literal folding) that run before `resolved_binop` dispatch. Ideally these would be handled uniformly in the binop result path.
- Extract shared arg-binding helper between `_gen_call` and `_gen_method_call` in `codegen_cpp/expressions.py`. Today each dispatcher has its own loop over `(arg, param)` pairs that applies coercion, covariant wrapping, `@dynamic` adapter insertion, `TpyTypeParamConstruct` / `TpyVarargPack` materialization, TypeParamRef substitution, etc. The loops have diverged repeatedly: `TpyVarargPack` was first handled only in `_gen_call` (broke `math.hypot(*coords)` -> mirrored into `_gen_method_call`'s first-pass loop), and then again only in that first-pass loop (broke method `*args` user-record calls -> mirrored into the user-record branch at the bottom of `_gen_method_call`). `_gen_method_call` alone has at least two arg-emission loops (first-pass + per-record-type fallback) that drift independently. Fix: pull the per-arg transformation into a helper `_bind_args(args: list[TpyExpr], params: list[(str, TpyType)], type_subst) -> list[str]` and call it from all paths. Keeps the dispatch split (the paths resolve very differently -- registry lookup vs receiver-type method resolution + TypedDict/callable-field/nested-constructor/property/dunder special cases) while eliminating the duplicated arg-list logic that has been the source of "feature X added to one path, not the other" bugs. Pairs with: consider having sema rewrite module-qualified calls (`math.hypot(x, y)` is currently `TpyMethodCall(obj=Name("math"), ...)`) into bare `TpyCall` with a qualified name, so they route through the simpler dispatcher -- `math` is a compile-time namespace, not a runtime object with methods.
- **[XS] `FieldInfo.has_in_class_init` property for the "field has an in-class initializer" fact.** Four sites now inline the same `fld.default_expr is not None` guard to mean "this field is default-constructible regardless of its type": `tpyc/sema/analyzer.py` (`_explain_default_ctor_deletion` + `_record_default_ctor_is_deleted`), `tpyc/sema/protocols.py` (`_is_default_constructible`), `tpyc/sema/calls.py`, and `tpyc/codegen_cpp/records.py::_all_fields_default_constructible`. Add a `has_in_class_init` property on `FieldInfo` (`tpyc/typesys.py`) so the fact is authoritative and a future site can't silently omit a leg. First-class type fact, moves cleanly across the THIR boundary. Surfaced by `/tpy-review` (architecture-fit) of the enum-field-default branch.
- Inplace operator C++ return type: `__iadd__`/`__ior__` etc. declare returning self type (Python semantics) but the C++ helpers (`list_extend`, `dict_update`) return `void`. Add thin wrappers that return `T&` (e.g. `list_extend_inplace`, `dict_update_inplace`) so the declared return type matches the C++ signature. Affects list and dict.
- `tpy::ptr_variant<Ts...>` wrapper: replace `std::variant<Ts*...>` in param signatures with a thin wrapper that has an implicit converting constructor from `ptr_variant<T*...>` to `ptr_variant<const T*...>`. This would let deduced-const (non-mutated) params use deep const consistently with `@readonly`, without breaking callers. Currently deduced-const uses shallow const (`const variant<T*...>`) which doesn't prevent mutation through the pointer at the C++ level. Start with param signatures only; locals/fields/returns can stay `std::variant`.
- Inline `and`/`or` chains for side-effect-free operands: `a or b or c` currently emits an intermediate temp (`auto&& __tmp = (a ? a : b); result = (__tmp ? __tmp : c)`) to avoid double-evaluation. When all operands are provably side-effect-free (variables, literals), the temp is unnecessary and the chain can be emitted as a single nested ternary (`!a.empty() ? a : !b.empty() ? b : c`), which is more readable.
- `tpy::tpy_callable<F, R(Args...)>` concept: replace verbose `requires requires(__F0& __fn, ...) { { __fn(...) } -> std::convertible_to<R>; }` blocks with a compact `tpy::tpy_callable<__F0, R(Args...)>` concept in the runtime. Same `R(Args...)` notation as `std::function`. Needs a helper trait with partial specialization (`std::invocable` + `std::convertible_to` for return, void special case). Cosmetic improvement -- only worth prioritizing if it measurably speeds up C++ compilation for template-heavy Fn usage.
- Unify rvalue materialization: two overlapping mechanisms exist for extending rvalue lifetimes -- the slot system (`std::optional<T>` slots in `_gen_pointer_local_init`, tied to var decl infrastructure) and TempState (`auto&&` temps, expression-level). Both solve the same problem at different abstraction levels. Consider exposing a lower-level "materialize this rvalue" API that both var decls and expression-level temps (e.g. `and`/`or` ternaries) can share.
- Transparent coercion codegen: `TpyCoerce` in codegen has a growing list of special cases for when to forward `coerce_target` vs `actual_type` to the inner `gen_expr` (literals need the target to pick C++ representation; view coercions need it for zero-copy paths). Add a `transparent: bool` flag on coercion definitions so the decision is made at coercion definition time in `coercions.py`, not with `isinstance` checks in codegen.
- Deferred type resolution in parser: the parser currently resolves type names eagerly during parsing, but its per-module TypeRegistry lacks cross-module types. Two workarounds exist: (1) a `resolved` guard that accepts any import-resolved name as a NominalType in annotation context (sema validates later), and (2) speculative `_parse_type_annotation` at call-parsing sites with a sema fix to clear `call_type` when the name turns out to be a function. The proper fix: the parser should produce unresolved type reference nodes and let sema (which has full cross-module information) resolve them. This would also eliminate `_resolve_primitive_type` special cases for `slice`/`int`/`float`/etc. -- sema would resolve all type names uniformly through type factories.
- Push marker-protocol metadata from compiler hardcoding into library-declared `@builtin_type` annotations + add docstrings. Today `tpy.ValueType` / `tpy.Copyable` / `tpy.Default` / `tpy.NativeIterable` / `tpy.Send` / `tpy.Sync` / `tpy.ReturnException` / `tpy.Covariant` / `tpy.AnyFixedInt` / etc. are declared as bare `@native("tpy::X") class X(Protocol): ...` stubs with no docstring -- compiler dispatch on them lives in `tpyc/sema/protocols.py`'s marker arm (an `if qname == qnames.X` chain), with the qname strings centralized in `qnames.py`. Same per-type-knowledge-in-compiler-if-chains shape as the sibling "Push subscript metadata" entry below. Migration shape: (1) add `@builtin_type("tpy.X", is_marker=True, cpp_concept="tpy::X", marker_predicate="value_type" | "copyable" | "default" | None, ...)` to each marker so the metadata lands on its static TypeDef payload; (2) replace the marker arm's qname-chain with a single TypeDef-property lookup (`marker_predicate == "copyable" -> not is_type_non_copyable(actual)` etc.); (3) retire the now-dead qname constants from `qnames.py` (VALUE_TYPE / COPYABLE / DEFAULT / ...) and the per-marker fields in `qnames.py`'s "tpy protocols" block. Also add one-line docstrings to each protocol stub in `lib/tpy/tpy/_core/_types.py` (and sync `lib/cpy/tpy/__init__.py`) explaining what conformance grants (e.g. "passes to range-for codegen", "static `T{}` construction", "implicit `Box[Parent] <- Box[Child]` upcast") and how conformance is established (implicit predicate / explicit `extends`). The docstrings are useful even without the migration; folding them into the same pass keeps the touch local. Two known gaps in the existing predicates that the migration should also close: (a) `_is_default_constructible` returns False unconditionally for `TypeParamRef` parents in the aggregate-record walk (lines 502-504) -- doesn't consult `get_type_param_bound(name)` to check whether the bound conforms to Default, so `class Holder[T: Default](T): ...` (aggregate, extends T) is silently rejected; (b) regression-test coverage on `error_copyable_extends_contradiction` and `error_default_extends_contradiction` only exercises the `__init__ + required-params` denial branch -- the `del_suppresses_default_ctor` paths (@nocopy+__del__, __del__+no-__init__+indeterminate-init-field) and the aggregate-record-with-non-default-field path are unguarded.
- Push subscript metadata from compiler hardcoding into library-declared type metadata. Today the codegen bounds-safe path needs to know whether a type's C++ `operator[]` takes `size_t` (built-in containers: `vector`/`array`/`span`/`string`/`bytes` families) or the user's declared param type (typically `int32_t` for user records). The decision lives in `_is_concrete_user_record` (`codegen_cpp/expressions.py`) gated on `is_list/is_array/is_span/is_str_category/is_bytes_category` predicates from `type_def_registry.py` -- "STL types use size_t" is a fact about the library that's currently baked into the compiler. Cleaner: declare each type's `operator[]` parameter type as part of its TPy stub metadata (and similar properties: bounds-checked vs unchecked, supports negative indices, etc.) and have codegen query it. Pairs with the broader "Unify `TypeDef.cpp_formatter` and `@native` / `_native_cpp_names`" entry in the strict-warning hardening section -- both are about pushing per-type C++ properties from compiler-side hardcoding into library-declared metadata. Same shape applies to other ad-hoc per-type knowledge in codegen (e.g. the `iter_range` adapter dispatch, Python-int polymorphism per-type rules).

INVARIANT to preserve: the per-resume re-extraction of the narrowing alias (`auto& __t = std::get<M>((*name))` re-emitted at each resume case) is sound only because nothing holds the alias across a suspension -- `frame_slot::emplace` invalidates prior `operator*` results, so a future optimization that elides the per-resume re-extraction and caches the alias across states would silently dangle.   - **[LOW] Make the pointer-form match-binding reject root-aware (lift the over-rejection).** The W1 reject (`match.py` `_emit_binding`, `resumable_match_subject_is_lvalue`) rejects a pointer-repr `Optional` arm binding when the subject is non-lvalue OR a narrowed name (`error_gen_match_nested_narrowed_ptr_bind`). The narrowed-name half is **over-conservative**: a narrowing alias is a C++ *reference* (`auto& __case_0 = std::get<0>(__match_subject)`), so when the narrowed subject roots at a *frame-resident* lvalue (param/local/field, e.g. `this->u`), `optional_to_ptr(__case_0.maybe)` points into frame storage and is SAFE across the suspension -- the reject (and the /tpy-review safety "Critical") wrongly treated the reference variable as owned storage. The precise rule: reject only when the subject's storage *root* is a dispatch-local copy (a non-lvalue root like `match foo():`); a narrowing alias is transparent (safe iff its source is frame-resident, unsafe iff it narrows a non-lvalue). Proper fix: track root-frame-residency through `narrowed_vars` rather than the blunt syntactic check. Over-rejection is currently HARMLESS -- the only shape that hits it (nested union match) can't compile anyway due to the pre-existing union-match codegen bugs (the `*std::get` operator + union-param issues in BUGS.md). Sequence this AFTER those union bugs are fixed (lifting it sooner just swaps a clean reject for an opaque C++ error). Low priority. Surfaced by user review of the W1 fix.

Today's coverage exercises each context separately; nothing asserts the two routes produce the *same* observable behavior. Motivated by the W1 investigation (binding storage differs between routes -- owned function-scope local vs owned frame field -- same result today, but the two emit paths could diverge silently).
